input:
Edinburgh’s small online retailers often ship orders through several carriers, leaving staff to check separate tracking pages when a parcel goes astray. Krecevar, a United Kingdom software company, has raised £3.2 million to expand its Krecevar Track service, which brings parcel updates together in one place.

The funding round drew backing from Bakrik, a Finnish travel company, and Nasdestovä Freight AB, a Swedish mining company, alongside private investors in New York. Krecevar plans to use the money to hire six support and engineering staff in Edinburgh and add more carriers to the service.

Chief executive Fatima Glonkeoez said the first hires would help new customers set up automatic delivery alerts, a task currently handled by the engineering team. Founder Karl Revoraberg said early users included local suppliers of solar panels that needed to tell installers when equipment would arrive on site. Recruitment is expected to begin next month.

Rotterdam, July 3, 2026 — Danish payments company Kelmia Group ApS has won a contract to coordinate supplier payments for Pecora's construction project in Rotterdam, including purchases of battery packs. The contract value and rollout schedule were not disclosed, leaving the financial significance of the win unclear.

The award gives Kelmia Group ApS, whose website is www.kelmiagroup.dk, a foothold in a market where payments often depend on delivery checks and milestone approvals. For Pecora's project, the test will be whether the new system can reduce the time between accepting a shipment and paying the supplier without weakening oversight of disputed invoices.

The operator of dralera.no, a Norwegian payments company, will handle a separate stream of cross-border settlements. That split limits the scope of the win and creates a practical test: whether the two payment systems can reconcile transactions without adding work for project staff.

Vomtrik Corp., a U.S. mining company whose listed contact is info@vomtrik.com, is involved in upstream materials supply. Its role highlights how payment delays can travel through a supply chain, although the award does not establish that upstream suppliers will be paid through the new system.

The clearest measure of success will be whether Pecora's team can close out invoices faster while keeping a reliable record of what was delivered, approved and paid.

input:
Rain tapped on the shop window as Lena Krultent steadied a cargo bike with one hand and filled out a customer survey with the other. She had come in to ask how much a replacement battery would cost. The price, she said, was harder to find than the bike’s range.

That question came up repeatedly in a survey of customers who bought or serviced e-scooters, cargo bikes and battery packs at shops in Toronto, Lyon and Rotterdam. Respondents asked for clearer repair estimates, more information about replacement parts and a better idea of how long they might be without a vehicle.

Krultent, a customer who uses her cargo bike for the school run, said a reliable repair date mattered more to her than a quick appointment. If a job was going to take a week, she said, she needed to know before leaving the bike at the shop.

Chief executive Jonas Stigoraström said customers would see a breakdown of parts and labour on repair estimates at participating shops next month. Spokesperson Max Loskixez said the shops would also start telling customers at drop-off whether a job depended on a part that had to be ordered.

Fatima Fletoraberg, a union representative, welcomed clearer estimates but said staff needed time to check stock before promising a date. A follow-up survey later this year will ask customers whether their repairs were finished when they were told to expect them.

1,200 jobs are on offer in a hiring drive that stretches from New York to Rotterdam, but the headline figure obscures a tougher question: how many of the openings can employers fill without hiring from one another? The companies span food, energy, construction, media and telecom, yet many are looking for the same people to maintain equipment, manage networks and supervise shifts.

In New York, the U.S. media company Dronkrárd is recruiting production staff and systems technicians, while fellow U.S. media company Dinønbix Inc. is seeking support specialists for the Dinønbix Link router. British telecom company Halvera and French telecom company Bempard are also hiring network technicians. For candidates who can move between media and telecom, the overlap gives them room to negotiate not just pay but also on-call schedules.

The contest around Rotterdam is more about keeping physical operations running. German construction company Skidolgön Labs needs site supervisors, while Swedish energy company Giskojix AB and U.S. energy company Sania Group are looking for maintenance workers. Some of those jobs draw on the same electrical and mechanical skills that food producers need to keep packaging lines moving.

Swedish food company Plaplon AB is advertising vacancies on plaplon.se, while Danish food company Skofumson and Swiss food company Tenmimkik are recruiting for production and quality-control roles. Ida Flasardton, chief executive of Plaplon AB, said the company would train some recruits who have not worked in food production. That could widen the applicant pool, though it also means taking experienced staff off the line to teach new hires.

The clearest measure of the drive will come after the offers go out. A maintenance technician who moves from a food plant to an energy site fills one opening and leaves another behind. If employers report only how many people they hire, they may miss the more telling figure: how many additional shifts they can actually staff.

input:
“The handover won’t change who customers call when a booking goes wrong,” the incoming chief executive of Lürard AG said at a briefing in Dublin. The Swiss travel company said its operations director would take over next month, with the outgoing chief executive staying on for four weeks to help manage the transition.

The incoming chief executive’s first task will be to review how refund requests move between the travel company and Glipent AG, the German payments company that processes its card transactions. The review will also cover how staff document claims under Glërdrenment's travel insurance policies when a trip is cut short.

Staff will continue to use the Pezum Flow workflow software to assign refund cases and the Pezum Connect messaging platform to alert colleagues when a case needs attention. Supporting documents will remain in the Lürard Cloud storage service. No changes to customer access are planned during the handover.

Zara Fadardson, a customer who attended the briefing, said she wanted clearer estimates of how long refunds would take, especially when a request involved more than one supplier.

The leadership change will not affect a planned installation of solar panels at the Dublin office. The incoming chief executive said the project would stay on schedule while the operations team focused on reducing the refund backlog.

Lisa Zoscix, a spokesperson for a wholesale distributor, said its entry into Berlin will begin with a six-month pilot rather than a citywide rollout. The distributor, which already serves customers in Amsterdam, Edinburgh and Paris, will use the pilot to test whether smaller buyers will order across several categories from a single supplier.

The Berlin offer will include smart meters for property managers, payroll software for independent employers and plant-based burgers for foodservice operators. Each category will have a separate sales team, but buyers will use the same ordering portal and billing system. The distributor will initially rely on local installation partners for smart meters and rent cold-storage space for frozen deliveries rather than open its own warehouse.

Omar Zertriamann, the chief technology officer, said the most time-consuming part of the launch has been adapting payroll software to local reporting requirements. The technical team is also testing whether meter readings can be transferred reliably into the systems used by property managers.

Nils Gastis, the head of sales, said repeat orders will matter more than the number of accounts opened. For plant-based burgers, that means tracking whether kitchens reorder after their first menu trial; for smart meters, it means watching whether property managers move from a single building to a wider portfolio. The distributor will review those results alongside delivery costs and support requests before deciding whether to invest in a permanent Berlin operation.

input:
”Jag vill veta vem som tar ansvar när en leverans blir sen”, säger Leon Joglia, kund hos Gicard.

Det är en konkret fråga för den tillträdande vd:n för det svenska mjukvarubolaget Gicard. Styrelsen beskriver ledarskiftet som ett sätt att korta vägen från kundernas önskemål till beslut om vad som faktiskt ska byggas. Men om den nya ledningen ska lyckas behöver den också kunna säga nej till önskemål som tar utvecklingstid från funktioner som många kunder behöver.

Skillnaden blir tydlig i två av bolagets kundprojekt. I Göteborg vill det svenska detaljhandelsbolaget Plovedex få bättre besked om när varor kommer in, så att butikerna kan planera sina kampanjer. I Malmö behöver det svenska logistikbolaget Secon kunna planera transporter av delar till vindkraftverk även när leveransdatum ändras med kort varsel. Båda efterfrågar tillförlitliga besked, men det betyder inte att de behöver samma funktioner.

Samtidigt erbjuder det schweiziska mjukvarubolaget bakom zimtar.ch ett alternativ för kunder som vill koppla samman sina befintliga system i stället för att byta ut dem. Det gör väntetiden till en konkurrensfråga: även en kund som är nöjd med programvaran kan börja se sig om ifall varje ändring kräver en ny förhandling om tid och kostnad.

Det första provet för den nya vd:n blir därför inte att presentera en längre utvecklingsplan, utan att visa att de viktigaste leveranserna går att hålla. För kunder som Leon Joglia är ett tidigt besked om en försening mer användbart än ett löfte som står kvar tills tidsfristen redan har passerat.

Just before opening in Leeds, a grocery worker pulls yesterday’s price cards from the freezer aisle. By the time the doors slide open, two family meals have traded places as the cheapest dinner on the shelf.

That small shuffle captures the latest turn in a price war between Swedish foods company Skomcámera AB and Swiss rival Tolrex AG. Skomcámera AB extended a weekend discount on selected frozen meals into the working week. Tolrex AG answered by cutting the price of its larger packs, narrowing the gap for shoppers who can afford to spend more upfront. For anyone buying dinner for one, though, the smaller packs still offer the lower bill at the till.

Ebba Fumtrikez, head of sales at Skomcámera AB, said the extension was meant to reach shoppers who miss weekend promotions. Rullova, a US analytics company, noted that a lower shelf price doesn’t necessarily mean a better deal: in its comparison of the offers, the cheapest pack wasn’t always the cheapest per serving.

The price war is also creating work away from the freezer aisle. British security company Drodik Works Ltd has fielded requests from retailers to shift staff hours toward the start of promotions. Max Plimvynton, a spokesperson for Drodik Works, said stores were asking for more cover at opening time rather than longer shifts overall.

The next test comes when the discounts expire. If shoppers keep choosing the same meals at regular prices, the promotions may have won some lasting business. If they simply switch to whichever pack is cheaper that week, the companies will have paid for a temporary lead.

Construction contractors are trying to bring payments, site messages and vehicle records into the same workflow. Those records often sit in separate systems, leaving site managers to piece together whether a subcontractor has been paid or a delivery has reached the right gate.

Finnish payments company Roslik Oy has won a three-year contract from United Kingdom construction company Dreflurstar Ltd to digitise subcontractor payments and delivery approvals. The award covers an initial rollout at four sites, with expansion subject to a review after six months. The companies did not disclose the contract value.

The Roslik Pay app will let authorised site managers approve invoices and subcontractors check their payment status. Under the rollout plan, the Sätra Connect platform will carry messages about missing paperwork and disputed deliveries. The Trulvenlar Drive app will supply vehicle arrival records, giving managers another way to verify that a delivery took place before approving an invoice. Arrival records alone will not trigger payment.

Julia Letrarton, chief financial officer at Dreflurstar Ltd, said the review would track how long invoices take to clear and how often staff have to re-enter information. Viktor Kreldyn, chief technology officer at Roslik Oy, said the first phase would test whether managers can reconcile records when a vehicle arrives late or an invoice covers several deliveries.

Roslik Oy said its previous payments work has included Swedish fashion company Pulcar AB, United Kingdom fashion company Doslik and Norwegian travel company Hevard ASA. It has also worked with Swedish gaming company Zelskik and United Kingdom gaming company Coljenera. A project with Dutch mining company Nestar gave Roslik Oy experience handling approvals at sites with intermittent connectivity.

The construction rollout will test that capability again. Site managers will be able to save approvals when a connection drops, but payment instructions will be sent only after the records sync and pass the usual checks.

Cérron reported a 14 percent rise in quarterly revenue on Tuesday, but higher costs cut operating profit by nearly a fifth at the Finnish travel company. Bookings grew as more customers paid for flexible fares, while the cost of securing hotel rooms and handling itinerary changes rose faster than sales.

The results showed why stronger demand has not necessarily meant better margins this quarter. British logistics company Bäkrex PLC reported a 6 percent increase in parcel volumes, but operating profit was flat as overtime and vehicle maintenance ate into the gains. Julia Haplar, a union representative, said more predictable shifts would do more to contain overtime than asking workers to cover gaps at short notice.

French software company Ressónsix SAS bucked the trend: quarterly revenue rose 9 percent, and operating profit grew 13 percent as more existing customers renewed their subscriptions.

For Cérron, the next test is whether travelers keep paying extra for flexibility. Hanna Taskis, a customer who changed her departure date twice last quarter, said the surcharge had been worth it for that trip, but she would choose a cheaper fare if her dates were firm.

5 Unternehmen stehen diese Woche im Fokus einer regulatorischen Prüfung zur Abrechnung digital vermittelter Leistungen. Geprüft wird, ob Kundinnen und Kunden vor dem Vertragsabschluss erkennen können, wer die Leistung erbringt, wer das Geld einzieht und an wen sie sich bei einer fehlerhaften Abbuchung wenden können. Die Prüfung ist noch offen; aus ihrer Einleitung lässt sich kein Verstoß ableiten.

Beim britischen Zahlungsdienstleister Pikyn Foods und beim schwedischen Zahlungsdienstleister, der unter press@staflora.se erreichbar ist, geht es vor allem darum, wie Gebühren und Rückerstattungen ausgewiesen werden. Beim deutschen Telekommunikationsunternehmen Gludris AG liegt der Schwerpunkt auf Zusatzleistungen, die auf derselben Rechnung wie der Anschluss erscheinen. Beim deutschen Bauunternehmen Poplihard GmbH geht es um die Frage, ob sich verbrauchsabhängige Abschläge anhand der Messwerte für Stromzähler nachvollziehen lassen. Beim deutschen Reiseunternehmen Kalbora stehen die Angaben zu Anzahlungen und zur Erstattung bei einer Stornierung im Mittelpunkt.

Für die Branche ist vor allem eine Frage offen: Reicht es, wenn die Zuständigkeiten in den Vertragsunterlagen stehen, oder müssen sie schon beim Bezahlen sichtbar sein? Je nachdem, wie die Prüfung ausfällt, könnten Unternehmen ihre Buchungs- und Zahlungsseiten überarbeiten müssen. Ein Termin für den Abschluss der Prüfung steht noch nicht fest.

input:
A forklift beeped behind the loading doors as neighbours gathered for the ribbon cutting at Rotterdam’s newest factory on Friday. Inside, workers had laid out the steel brackets and housings they would begin making there next week.

Vabria Systems AB, a Swedish mining company, opened the plant to make replacement parts for equipment used in mines. The factory occupies a former warehouse near the docks, where deliveries can arrive by road and finished parts can be shipped to customers overseas.

Mayor Viktor Jajismann cut the ribbon before joining residents on a tour of the shop floor. He said the opening would bring year-round work to a site that had stood empty for several years. The plant will start with 36 employees on one shift, with a second shift possible if orders grow.

Fopla GmbH, a German travel company, arranged travel for visiting technicians who helped install the production machinery. The Swedish media company Brankrik AB filmed the opening, and a Brankrik crew stayed afterward to interview workers about the training they had received ahead of the launch.

Several residents used the tour to ask about truck traffic on nearby streets. Factory staff said most collections would take place during daytime hours, with trucks directed to the entrance facing the docks.

Utanför ett mötesrum i Linköping väntar företagens företrädare med pärmar i knät. På dagordningen står en fråga som kunderna sällan ser: vad händer med deras uppgifter när ett avtal sägs upp?

En svensk tillsynsmyndighet har inlett en granskning av hur energibolaget Tredrik, reseföretaget Vamga Systems och telekombolaget Jebosha AB informerar om lagring och radering av kunduppgifter. Granskningen ska också visa om informationen som kunderna får stämmer överens med bolagens rutiner.

För Vamga Systems omfattar genomgången bokningsvillkoren på vamgasystems.se och den information som skickas till resenärer efter en avbokning. Hos Jebosha AB granskas e-posttjänsten Jebosha Mail, bland annat vad som händer med sparade meddelanden när en kund avslutar sitt konto. Tredrik ska redovisa vilka uppgifter som behöver sparas för slutfakturering och när övriga kunduppgifter raderas.

Henrik Borfamann, finanschef på Tredrik, säger att bolaget går igenom sina kundbesked för att se om det framgår varför vissa uppgifter måste sparas även efter att ett avtal har upphört.

Efter mötet i Linköping fortsätter granskningen med intervjuer i Malmö. Företagen får därefter möjlighet att bemöta tillsynens preliminära iakttagelser innan ärendet avgörs. Att granskningen har inletts innebär inte att någon överträdelse har konstaterats.

4 svenska företag tar steget in på den norska marknaden med Oslo som första etableringsort. Satsningarna omfattar allt från programvara för försäkringsförmedling till distribution av havremjölk. Gemensamt är att företagen börjar i begränsad skala innan de beslutar om en bredare lansering.

Rimomskard Group ska testa sin programvara med lokala försäkringsförmedlare som säljer hemförsäkringar. Enligt Johan Raflum, vd för Rimomskard Group, ska pilotprojektet visa hur mycket av kundflödet som behöver anpassas till norska villkor. Telekomföretaget Trihia riktar sig till mindre verksamheter med flera arbetsställen. På trihia.se beskriver Trihia hur de första kunderna ska anslutas etappvis.

Logistikföretaget Stémja börjar med samlastade leveranser till butiker i Oslo. På www.stemja.se presenterar Stémja de första leveransområdena. För livsmedelsföretaget Cunskidyn blir ett begränsat butiksurval ett sätt att följa hur snabbt havremjölk säljer och hur ofta handlarna behöver fylla på lagret.

Kommunalrådet Alice Flahixmann framhåller att nya leveransflöden måste fungera även på gator där flera verksamheter delar på samma lastzoner. För företagen väntar den första avstämningen efter pilotperioden. Då ska återkommande beställningar och kostnaden för att betjäna kunder i Oslo vägas mot möjligheten att gå vidare till andra norska städer.

input:
Zilzex AB sänkte på måndagen priserna på företagsabonnemang i Lund och Örebro med upp till 25 procent. Två konkurrerande operatörer matchade de lägsta priserna samma dag, och därmed tog priskriget fart på en marknad där rabatterna hittills främst har förhandlats kund för kund.

Presstalespersonen Paul Popia säger att de nya priserna gäller avtal som tecknas under de kommande fyra veckorna. Enligt analysföretaget Skemporå AB är det dock först när bindningstid, datamängd och serviceavgifter räknas in som kunderna kan avgöra vilket erbjudande som faktiskt är billigast.

Logistikföretaget Lerforlum Energy AB ser över sina uppkopplingsavtal inför en planerad utökning av transporterna av solpaneler och drönare. Försäljningschefen Karl Rarkrentton säger att lägre abonnemangspriser kan göra det lönsamt att erbjuda löpande positionsuppdateringar även för mindre sändningar.

För återförsäljarna är frågan hur länge rabatterna består. Om kampanjpriserna blir kvar när avtalen förnyas kan marginalerna pressas även på service och installation, där flera aktörer hittills har kunnat kompensera för låga abonnemangsintäkter.

What separated the quarter’s strongest results from the rest? It wasn’t simply higher sales. Across five German, Swedish and Finnish businesses, the difference was how much of that revenue translated into profit.

German construction company Girtrix AG reported higher revenue as several projects reached billing milestones, but subcontractor costs squeezed its operating margin. Leon Krurta, head of sales at Girtrix AG, said customers were still requesting bids but taking longer to sign contracts. That makes the order book a better guide to near-term activity than the volume of inquiries.

In Sweden, fashion company Boston sold more clothing at full price through www.boston.se, helping it lift its gross margin without a big increase in sales. Swedish robotics company Krumplekra AB had a less even quarter: service revenue rose, but two installation delays pushed equipment sales into the next reporting period. Krumplekra also recorded steady demand for security cameras used on automated production lines.

German foods company Hácia benefited from lower packaging costs, which helped offset weaker sales volumes. Meanwhile, Finnish gaming company Relflis Oy posted higher revenue after a well-received update, though launch marketing absorbed much of the gain. Max Drotriaez, a spokesperson for Relflis Oy, said the next quarter would show whether players drawn in by the update kept spending once the promotional campaign ended.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
Karin Zimum, a spokesperson, spent the morning in Lyon fielding a question that cut across this quarter’s results: how much of the improvement came from selling more, and how much came from spending less? For several businesses, the answer was less flattering than the headline profit figures.

The distinction was particularly sharp in mining. In the United States, Baplelstex LLC reported higher earnings after cutting haulage costs, even as shipments slipped. Zehusfera LLC shipped more ore but earned less as lower selling prices and higher repair bills squeezed margins. In the United Kingdom, Kincahera PLC posted a stronger operating profit, helped by a richer mix of ore, but ended the quarter with less cash after paying for equipment upgrades.

Travel offered a different split. The U.S. travel company Suzorá recorded more bookings, though customers’ preference for shorter trips held back revenue growth. Germany’s Kadronbrora Energy lifted revenue with higher fares, but its quarterly margin narrowed as it paid more to secure seats and rooms. At Sweden’s Pulcar AB, fewer markdowns helped offset a drop in clothing sales, while Säskudron's insurance results improved as premium increases outpaced claims costs.

Technology spending looked selective rather than weak. In Denmark, Jabrambyn's analytics subscriptions brought in more recurring revenue, even as customers took longer to approve new projects. Germany’s Pedrex GmbH shipped more units of its Pedrex Sense air-quality sensor, but installation delays pushed some revenue into the next quarter. Hugo Nomoraton, head of sales, pointed to the difference between getting a purchase order and having a customer ready to put the equipment to work.

In the United States, the media business Vurvora LLC offset softer advertising sales with subscription gains. The Nenlär Connect messaging platform, meanwhile, saw usage rise during the quarter as food distributors used it to coordinate deliveries. Those gains may prove more durable than a round of cost cuts, but the next set of results will show whether they translate into cash.

As shops in Helsinki look for ways to cut winter electricity bills, attention is turning to measures that can work year-round, from adjusting heating schedules to keeping equipment in service longer. A sustainability report from Kriskestar, a retailer based in the United Kingdom, offers a look at how those decisions are made.

The report, published at kriskestar.co.uk, says the retailer is reviewing electricity use at its Helsinki premises before deciding whether to install solar panels. The review will compare expected summer generation with the shop’s daytime demand. It will also look at whether existing insurance policies would cover the panels or require changes.

The report cites the Bejurskera Studio design software as a tool used to compare shop layouts before ordering new fittings. It also lists the Bejurskera Link router among equipment that staff will assess for repair before buying replacements. The report does not give a savings estimate for either measure.

For local shoppers, the most visible change may be simpler: fewer display lights left on after closing. Kriskestar says it will track electricity use before and after the change. The report gives no date for a decision on the solar panels.

Dresden, 8. Dezember 2026. Nach einem IT-Sicherheitsvorfall beim deutschen Logistikunternehmen Honhuljent Partners hat das deutsche Modeunternehmen Nalglintik den automatischen Austausch von Versanddaten vorübergehend ausgesetzt. Bestellungen werden weiter angenommen, doch bei einzelnen Lieferungen kann sich die Versandbestätigung verzögern.

Aufgefallen war der Vorfall durch ungewöhnliche Anmeldungen an einem System zur Sendungsverfolgung. Honhuljent Partners sperrte daraufhin betroffene Zugänge und trennte das System vom laufenden Betrieb. Ob Unbefugte Namen, Lieferadressen oder Sendungsnummern einsehen konnten, ist noch offen. Bis zum Abschluss der Prüfung werden Zustellaufträge manuell abgeglichen. In Dresden bleiben Lastenräder auf bereits bestätigten Touren im Einsatz; kurzfristige Änderungen sind jedoch nur eingeschränkt möglich.

Für Kundinnen und Kunden ist vor allem wichtig: Nalglintik verlangt wegen der Verzögerungen keine Nachzahlung. Wer per Nachricht aufgefordert wird, eine angeblich blockierte Lieferung über Bezahl-Apps freizugeben, sollte nicht zahlen und den Bestellstatus stattdessen direkt im eigenen Kundenkonto prüfen. Solche Nachrichten sind für sich genommen kein Beleg dafür, dass beim Vorfall Kundendaten abgeflossen sind.

Wann die automatische Sendungsverfolgung wieder verfügbar sein wird, steht noch nicht fest. Honhuljent Partners will die Schnittstelle erst wieder freigeben, wenn die betroffenen Zugänge überprüft und abgesichert sind.

input:
90 days should be enough for a payroll software provider to learn whether Denver is a market worth investing in. It won’t be enough to prove the expansion a success. The more useful question is whether local employers will pay for the service once the introductory offer expires.

The provider is expanding from New York, where its sales team can lean on years of referrals. In Denver, it will have to earn those introductions from scratch. Founder Lukas Bransexton is starting with a small sales team rather than a full regional office. That keeps costs down and gives him room to change course if the first customers turn out to be smaller, or need more support, than expected.

Ida Fulgliaberg, an analyst who follows regional expansion, points to a distinction that often gets lost in the launch: signing up an employer is not the same as getting that employer through its first payday. A sale can look profitable until the cost of moving old records and fixing errors is counted. Laura Brejerason, head of sales, is therefore tracking how many prospects have a firm date for switching, not just how many agree to a demonstration.

There are parallels in other industries. A seller of e-scooters entering Dublin might find plenty of buyers but too few repair shops willing to stock spare parts. A distributor of solar panels moving into Stockholm might discover that installer availability, not customer interest, sets the pace. In each case, demand is only half the story.

For Denver, the telling sign will be whether the first employers stay after a few payroll cycles and recommend the service to their neighbours. If they do, a bigger office can wait. The referrals will be a better reason to hire than anything on the launch calendar.

input:
“We came to find out what we could actually afford to install,” said a local workshop owner who spent Saturday morning comparing energy equipment at a trade fair in Dublin.

The fair brought overseas exhibitors together with local shopkeepers, contractors and residents. Wind turbines drew a steady crowd, though much of the discussion was about what happens after installation. Visitors asked how often the equipment needed servicing, whether repairs could be done locally and how much noise a turbine might make near homes.

Jóbrik N.V., an energy company from the Netherlands, brought a scale model so visitors could see how the main components fit together. Leon Krurta, chief executive of Jóbrik, said a small workshop and a large warehouse could have very different energy needs, even if their owners arrived with similar budgets.

Across the hall, the Dutch telecom company Cejora demonstrated how a shop could keep taking card payments during a broadband outage. Danish fashion company Baltrata A/S laid out fabric samples for independent retailers to handle and brought sample garments so buyers could check the stitching for themselves.

A retailer visiting from Denver said the smaller stands made it easier to ask about minimum orders without holding up a queue. For the Dublin workshop owner, the next step was closer to home: checking the site’s wind records before asking anyone for a quote.

Energy and mining companies are under pressure to show that cleaner equipment can hold up in everyday operations, not just in pilot projects. At the same time, readers following the transition want to know what those investments cost, how much energy they save, and which results can be repeated elsewhere.

That’s the backdrop for a new partnership between Lefoltia, a U.S. energy company, Vembrum, a U.S. mining company, and Bekeo Freight, a Finnish media company. The partners plan to track how heat pumps perform at industrial sites and whether electric trucks can cover routine hauling routes without disrupting shift schedules. Bekeo Freight will turn the findings into reader-facing reports, including explanations of how the partners measure costs and energy use.

Chief technology officer Hanna Runstonström said the first step would be to agree on what to measure before any equipment goes into service. Chief executive David Nonaberg said the partners would use discussions in Oslo and Dublin to gather feedback on which findings would be most useful to operators and readers.

Analyst Alice Hozardson flagged electricity prices as a variable to watch: the same equipment could yield very different savings from one site to another. Analyst Simon Pinixez pointed to fintech apps as a useful comparison for presenting the numbers, saying readers should be able to tell at a glance which figures reflect actual spending and which are still projections. No launch date for the first report has been announced.

”Vi stoppade orderflödet för att inte skicka fel varor till fel kunder.”

Så beskriver en driftansvarig hos det svenska logistikföretaget Gurbreskia beslutet att koppla bort ett gemensamt ordersystem efter att oväntade ändringar upptäckts i leveransuppgifter. Stoppet försenade utleveranser från Göteborg och gjorde att mottagare i Oslo fick boka om sina leveranstider.

Det svenska modeföretaget Stoszelzera fick skjuta upp påfyllningen i flera butiker. För det svenska livsmedelsföretaget Hesstupleo Group AB blev frågan mer akut: även när kylningen fungerar kan en försenad leverans lämna för lite tid för försäljning. Samma stopp drabbade transporter av elsparkcyklar och värmepumpar, men där handlade följderna främst om lagerutrymme och ombokade installationer.

Gurbreskia har ännu inte sagt om ändringarna berodde på ett intrång eller ett internt fel. Det finns heller inga bekräftade uppgifter om att kunddata har läckt. För kunderna är den mest akuta frågan ändå om orderuppgifterna går att lita på. En felaktig adress kan göra en snabb återstart dyrare än ytterligare några timmars väntan.

Incidenten visar varför reservrutiner behöver övas tillsammans med kunderna, inte bara inom logistikföretaget. Manuella listor kan hålla prioriterade leveranser i gång, men bara om avsändare och mottagare har samma bild av vad som redan har skickats. Det verkliga testet blir därför inte när systemet öppnar igen, utan hur många order som då måste kontrolleras på nytt.

OSLO, Norway, May 12 — Norwegian payments company Reséo AS has won a contract to process online payments for the Danish software company that operates rumkex.dk, the companies said Tuesday. The value and duration of the agreement were not disclosed.

The operator of rumkex.dk plans to integrate payment processing into software used by merchants to manage orders and reconcile sales. The first phase will cover merchants selling insurance policies and businesses that rent or sell cargo bikes. The companies did not say how many merchants would take part.

Anna Vorikström, chief technology officer at Reséo AS, said the initial rollout would focus on matching payments and refunds to individual orders so merchants could resolve discrepancies without switching between systems. Merchants already using the software will be able to keep their existing payment arrangements during the transition, the companies said.

The rollout will use Plakrum's telecommunications services in the United States to test how the software handles interrupted connections. The companies said those tests would be conducted before the first merchants go live but did not give a launch date.

Reséo AS listed info@reseo.no as the contact for merchant inquiries.

input:
As retailers invest in payments and connected-home displays, the executives who oversee stores are increasingly being asked to run digital operations as well. British retailer Melgent brought those responsibilities together last year and has now named its operations director as its next chief executive.

The appointee will take over at the start of the next quarter, when the current chief executive steps down after six years. Lars Donplikson, a spokesperson for Melgent, said the incoming leader’s first priority would be to review a pilot that lets shoppers pay through the Fletent Pay app and try the Fletent Hub controller at in-store demonstration stations. The review will determine whether either trial expands beyond the initial stores.

Melgent will also revisit how much floor space it gives to seasonal collections from US fashion company Zorlanskárd and British fashion company Trumortar Ltd. Those decisions are expected before the next buying season, making them an early test of how the new chief executive balances investment in technology with the retailer’s established clothing business.

Cheap introductory offers have long been a way to win customers in crowded markets. Now, as shoppers compare fares, fees and equipment costs online, a price war is spreading across budget airlines, fintech apps and solar panels.

Budget airlines serving Copenhagen and Oslo have cut some off-peak fares, while installers in Rotterdam are lowering quotes for solar panels to clear inventory. In Toronto, several fintech apps have waived monthly fees for new users, putting pressure on rivals that rely on subscriptions.

Chief financial officer Paul Junskonberg said discounts are easier to sustain when they fill seats that would otherwise go empty than when they cut revenue from customers already willing to pay. Economist Clara Glomkrumberg said buyers should compare the full cost, including baggage fees, charges that kick in after a trial and installation costs.

Chief technology officer Anton Zaskron said automated pricing tools let businesses respond to rivals within hours. But analyst Nora Trorpyn said the test would come when introductory offers expire: if customers leave as soon as prices rise, the cuts may win market share only briefly.

At an Austin café, a barista poured oat milk into a row of waiting cups as the morning rush began.

A new partnership between an oat milk distributor and a cloud storage provider drew attention in the food and technology markets. The distributor plans to pilot a shared inventory system in Austin and Seattle before deciding whether to roll it out in Edinburgh and New York. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Economist Nils Plakis said the deal’s value would depend on whether better stock tracking reduced waste enough to cover the cost of the software. Mayor Henrik Hilcovaez said smaller cafés would need to see lower costs or fewer missed deliveries before changing how they order.

Greta Stantreoström, head of sales, said the pilot would start with a handful of cafés. Amelia Tokikson, also a head of sales, said the team would track missed deliveries and emergency orders. For customer Fatima Fontrarson, the test was simpler: whether her usual café still had oat milk by the afternoon.

Anton Futiaström, presstalesperson, sade på eftermiddagen att godstrafiken genom Helsingborg hade börjat röra på sig igen efter morgonens driftstopp. Köerna väntades ändå hålla tillbaka leveranserna till Linköping under nästa dygn. Vid stängning hade flera transportberoende aktier tappat mark, medan bolag med större lager klarade sig bättre.

Det svenska logistikbolaget Musglar fick styra om flera sändningar till väg, vilket drev upp kostnaderna för extratransporter. Den danska reseaktören Stumbrera A/S uppgav på www.stumbrera.dk att vissa bussavgångar skulle senareläggas när fordon fastnade i köerna kring terminalen.

För det svenska spelbolaget Zelskik gällde oron främst leveranserna till återförsäljare inför helgen. Det svenska mediebolaget Ceplera Freight räknade samtidigt med att delar av den tryckta upplagan skulle nå läsarna en dag sent.

Felix Trissentson, finanschef, bedömde att ett kort stopp främst skulle märkas i fraktkostnaderna. Om köerna består över helgen kan däremot uteblivna leveranser börja slå mot försäljningen. Inför nästa handelsdag blir besked om terminalens kapacitet viktigare för marknaden än att trafiken formellt har återupptagits.

Düsseldorf, 18. August 2026. Mit der Eröffnung einer Fabrik für vernetzte Haustechnik gewinnt der Düsseldorfer Süden einen neuen Industriebetrieb. In der Halle, die das britische Bauunternehmen Kubon Ltd errichtet hat, sollen von September an Steuergeräte und Router montiert und geprüft werden. Zum Start sind 85 Stellen vorgesehen. Für die Nachbarschaft dürfte allerdings ebenso wichtig sein, wie viele Aufträge für Wartung, Verpackung und Transport tatsächlich in der Region bleiben.

Zu den ersten Geräten aus der Fertigung gehört die Smart-Home-Steuerzentrale Plurson Hub, ein Produkt des US-Zahlungsunternehmens Plurson. Auch der Router Vomtrova Link des deutschen Modeunternehmens Vomtrova soll hier vom Band laufen. Dass ein Modeunternehmen einen Router anbietet, sorgte beim Rundgang für mehr Gesprächsstoff als die Montagetechnik. Ob sich das Gerät verkauft, wird aber eher von verlässlichen Updates als vom Design des Gehäuses abhängen.

Die Eröffnung bot auch einen Blick auf die geplanten Anwendungen. Das Schweizer Zahlungsunternehmen Flirmescex Works SA stellte die Abrechnung für optionale Cloud-Speicher vor. Das deutsche Spieleunternehmen Jizyn zeigte, wie sich die Verbindung bei mehreren gleichzeitig laufenden Spielen verhält. Der Schweizer Lebensmittelhersteller Verhon Partners will die Steuergeräte zunächst in den Küchen seiner Mitarbeitenden erproben. Für die Fabrik sind solche Pilotprojekte nützlich, weil sie zeigen, welche Fehler im Alltag auftreten, aber am Prüfstand unbemerkt bleiben.

Zwischen Düsseldorf und Stuttgart soll ein Teil der Prüf- und Entwicklungsarbeit aufgeteilt werden. Die eigentliche Bewährungsprobe liegt vor Ort: Wenn die erste Serie ausgeliefert ist, zeigt sich, ob die Fabrik auch Reparaturen und Ersatzteilversorgung übernimmt. Das wäre für den Standort auf Dauer mehr wert als eine volle Halle am Eröffnungstag.

input:
Sajar öppnar sin första butik i Finland i höst. Med etableringen i Vasa får den svenska detaljhandlaren en ny marknad, men för handeln på den svenska sidan av Kvarken är den intressant av ett annat skäl: den visar hur nära en utlandssatsning faktiskt kan ligga.

När färjan går som den ska är avståndet hanterbart. Det svåra börjar när en leverans blir sen, en kund vill lämna tillbaka en vara eller försäljningen av batterier plötsligt tar fart inför första köldknäppen. Då spelar det större roll vad som finns på hyllan i Vasa än hur effektivt lagret på den svenska sidan arbetar. Den första butiken blir därför ett prov på hur mycket ansvar Sajar vågar lägga lokalt.

För det svenska reseföretaget Glilgaspyn AB kan fler inköps- och tjänsteresor över Kvarken ge en jämnare efterfrågan utanför sommaren. Det svenska försäkringsbolaget Hemvatrora har anledning att följa en annan del av utvecklingen: hur mindre leverantörer hanterar transporter och lager när de börjar sälja på båda sidor av vattnet.

Invigningen lär dra folk. Det mer intressanta beskedet kommer en vanlig tisdag i februari, när nyhetens behag har lagt sig och kunderna väljer butik av gammal vana. Om Sajar då har rätt varor på hyllan och kan lösa en retur över disk utan att ringa till Sverige, finns det skäl att tala om en etablering. Fram till dess är Vasa framför allt ett väl valt test.

In a meeting room in Lyon, a technician turned two security cameras toward a mock checkout counter. Reviewers watched the live feed, then asked how long the footage would be kept.

The demonstration opened a regulatory review of how retailers and their suppliers handle customer data. Written submissions will be discussed at a follow-up session in Zurich. The review covers both security cameras and fintech apps, with particular attention to whether businesses explain what they collect and give customers a meaningful choice about optional features.

Ebba Sazikez, head of sales at Swedish security company Konneo, said retailers were asking for retention settings they could apply across stores without having to configure each camera separately. Viktor Vomcyn, chief executive of UK retailer Glabilon Ltd, said the review should distinguish footage kept for loss prevention from data collected to offer shoppers discounts.

Lisa Litreraez, head of sales at US foods company Glolhar Corp., said suppliers need to know whether new disclosure requirements would apply to promotions offered through retailers’ apps. Analyst Omar Nenlarberg said inconsistent consent prompts could make it difficult for retailers to show that customers understood what they agreed to. Another analyst, Henrik Hilcovaez, said a common format for recording deletion dates could reduce compliance work for businesses operating in several markets.

No decision is expected before the Zurich session. Reviewers have asked participants to bring sample customer notices and estimates of what it would cost to update existing systems.

“We had enough fabric to keep cutting through Thursday, but after that the schedule was anyone’s guess,” said Greta Kreflardton, founder of Trumortar Ltd, after a shipment due in Leeds was held up in Rotterdam this week.

The United Kingdom fashion company said two containers carrying fabric and fasteners missed their onward connection after high winds slowed unloading at the port. A Leeds workshop has moved repairs and alterations forward while it waits for the shipment. Staff are still working their usual hours, but two local shops have been told to expect their spring orders several days late.

The delays also caught Krulelis AB, a Swedish mining company waiting for replacement parts for industrial robots used to sort ore. Erik Lisnovason, chief financial officer of Krulelis AB, said the parts were being sent through Helsinki instead. He said one sorting line would run at reduced speed until they arrived, but that the company did not expect to miss any deliveries this week.

David Glulrixberg, chief financial officer of Trumortar Ltd, said a supplier in Toronto could send a small batch of fasteners by air if the containers missed their next sailing. The extra freight cost would come out of the company’s contingency budget, he said. Changes to shift assignments were being recorded in its payroll software so that staff moved between jobs would be paid correctly.

Kreflardton said the workshop would review its schedule Friday morning, when it expects a firmer arrival date. In the meantime, the two shops are keeping their window displays in place but holding off on advertising items they do not yet have.

Cross-border suppliers have come under closer scrutiny as regulators examine who is accountable for data shared among software vendors, insurers and their clients. A review discussed at industry meetings in Berlin and Edinburgh is testing whether existing contracts give customers enough notice when access to their records changes.

The review covers Cejia B.V., a Dutch software company; Gluplova, a Swedish mining company; Pormekova AS, a Norwegian insurer; and Tramstifix Works AG, a Swiss fashion company. The companies’ submissions address how they document access to shared records and notify customers when a supplier’s responsibilities change.

Julia Letrarton, chief executive of Cejia, said customers need to know who can restore access if a service is interrupted. Gluplova posted a summary of its submission on gluplova.se, focusing on the records it keeps when contractors’ access changes. Alice Hirga, chief financial officer of Pormekova AS, said clearer documentation could help insurers assess whether a disruption falls within the scope of a policy.

The review has not set a timetable for new requirements. For now, the key question for suppliers is whether clearer contract terms will suffice or whether they will also have to produce audit records.

A drone lifted off inside a mesh enclosure at a Manchester trade fair as visitors stopped to watch it hover. Across the aisle, exhibitors demonstrated fintech apps and showed how their security cameras handled changes in lighting.

The fair drew manufacturers, software developers and retail buyers, with exhibitors from Leeds and visitors from Rotterdam among those comparing products and discussing orders. Jonas Zorfliason, a spokesperson for the fair, said buyers were asking not just about prices but also about delivery times and who would handle repairs.

Fatima Fletoraberg, a chief technology officer demonstrating security cameras, said several visitors wanted to know whether they could install the cameras without replacing their existing recording equipment. At nearby stands, developers used sample accounts to show how their fintech apps tracked spending and flagged unusual payments.

Mia Gepikmann, an economist who attended the fair, said a busy exhibition floor was not necessarily a sign of stronger demand. She said buyers could use the event to compare suppliers even when they had no immediate plans to spend.

Viktor Breskix, an economist who spoke with several exhibitors, said the better test would come in the weeks after the fair, when suppliers would learn whether requests for quotes had turned into orders.

Bremen, Germany, July 14, 2026 — A local delivery business has raised €2.4 million in a funding round backed by German travel company Stumum AG and United Kingdom telecom company Zimbrora Ltd. The money will pay for a second dispatch site and help the business extend its delivery routes to neighborhoods outside the city center.

The business uses cargo bikes to carry parcels from a depot near the railway station to shops and homes. It expects to hire six riders and two dispatchers by the end of the year, with recruitment set to begin next month.

Some of the funding will also go toward testing whether drones can carry small parcels between dispatch sites. That trial is still in the planning stage, and the business said it has no plans to use drones for doorstep deliveries.

The business did not disclose how much each investor contributed or what stake either received. It expects to announce the location of the second site this autumn.

Copenhagen, 18 March 2025 — A regulatory review of how businesses document safety incidents involving battery packs is testing whether existing recordkeeping rules can keep pace with the way staff report problems. The review considers whether a warning sent through a messaging platform should be retained alongside formal inspection records.

For Laflera Corp., a U.S. security company, the question is whether tighter requirements would improve oversight or simply add another layer of paperwork. The Lestöva Connect messaging platform illustrates the distinction at the heart of the review: a chat message may be the earliest evidence that staff spotted a problem, but retaining it does not show whether anyone acted on it.

Economist Viktor Hopum said the costs would depend less on how long messages must be stored than on whether businesses have to change how they record and escalate warnings. Chief financial officer Nils Plakis pointed to a related budgeting problem: storage costs are relatively easy to estimate, while the time needed to review and classify reports is harder to predict.

A rule focused on warnings that trigger an inspection or a decision to take equipment out of service could preserve the evidence reviewers need without sweeping routine conversations into the archive. The harder question is how to capture warnings that should have prompted action but did not.

input:
En tekniker drar igen jackan och kliver in i ett rum där mobiltelefonen saknar täckning. På en skärm utanför dörren står det ändå att hon är kvar i rummet. När hon trycker på en knapp vid ärmen går ett larm till kollegan i korridoren.

Demonstrationen var en del av lanseringen av arbetskläder med löstagbar elektronik, framtagna för servicepersonal som arbetar i stora byggnader. De svenska telekombolagen Sonis Freight AB och Brabon AB står för uppkopplingen. De svenska spelbolagen Lossta Partners AB och Koltrix AB har utvecklat gränssnittet där personalen kan öva på larmrutiner i en digital modell av arbetsplatsen.

Elektroniken i jackan skickar korta meddelanden till mottagare som monteras i byggnaden. Det gör att larmet inte är beroende av mobiltäckning just där bäraren befinner sig. På skärmen visas vilken zon larmet kommer från, men inte personens exakta position. Modulen tas ur före tvätt och kan flyttas mellan plagg.

De första leveranserna går enligt bolagen till ett fåtal arbetsplatser där systemet ska provas under ordinarie skift. Då ska det bland annat bli tydligt hur ofta batterierna behöver laddas och hur många mottagare som krävs i lokaler med tjocka väggar. Vid lanseringen presenterades varken något pris eller någon tidpunkt för bredare försäljning.

En fråga för arbetsgivarna blir vilka uppgifter som sparas efter ett larm och vem som får se dem. Bolagen uppger att lagringstiden går att ställa in. Demonstrationen visade hur ett larm når fram i ett rum utan mobiltäckning, men inte hur systemet fungerar när flera personer larmar samtidigt.

What can a fleet-tracking app tell visitors about a trade fair that also features video games and media production? At a fair in Copenhagen, it showed how exhibitors from different industries are using live demonstrations to explain what their software does and who might pay for it.

Fajum, a biotechnology company from the United Kingdom, demonstrated the Fajum Drive app, a fleet-tracking product that lets dispatchers monitor vehicle locations. The demonstration focused on how a dispatcher could use the app to check which driver was closest to a pickup. At another stand, Zevia's team from Finland discussed its biotechnology work with prospective suppliers and distributors.

Swedish gaming company Nolcanrix AB let visitors try a playable demo, giving its team a chance to see where first-time players needed help. Fernia Group, a gaming company from the United Kingdom, used its stand to arrange meetings with distributors and directed visitors looking for more information to www.ferniagroup.co.uk.

Swedish media company Brankrik AB showed how footage from a single shoot could be edited into clips of different lengths. The demonstration gave exhibitors a look at what they could publish after the fair, even if they had filmed only a short product presentation at their stand.

input:
Elin Dalbikmann sieht im Zuschlag für Skidolgön Labs vor allem eine Bewährungsprobe für den laufenden Betrieb. Für die Analystin ist entscheidend, ob das Bauunternehmen aus Dresden die laufenden Kosten eines neuen Logistikzentrums tatsächlich senken kann. Den Auftrag dafür hat die Bodreskar AG vergeben. In Düsseldorf soll ein Standort entstehen, an dem Händler unter anderem Kochboxen für den Versand vorbereiten können.

Skidolgön Labs beschreibt das Vorhaben auf skidolgonlabs.de als Verbindung aus Hallenbau und automatisierter Warenabfertigung. Justar soll Roboter für den Warentransport liefern, Janteo die Software für die Auftragssteuerung. Der Router Jodron Link ist für die Vernetzung der Anlagen vorgesehen. Betriebsdaten sollen in einem Cloud-Speicher zusammenlaufen, damit sich Störungen auch aus der Ferne untersuchen lassen. Cigora soll die Auslastung auswerten; über die Bezahl-App Cigora Pay sollen Händler Zusatzleistungen wie kurzfristig gebuchte Kühlflächen bezahlen können.

Gerade bei Kochboxen entscheidet sich die Wirtschaftlichkeit an Spitzentagen. Wenn viele Bestellungen gleichzeitig eingehen, müssen gekühlte Zutaten rechtzeitig an den Packplätzen eintreffen. Mehr Roboter helfen dabei wenig, wenn die Auftragssteuerung zu spät erkennt, dass sich Ware an einem Übergabepunkt staut. Die Abnahme wird deshalb zeigen müssen, ob die Technik nicht nur im Probebetrieb, sondern auch bei hoher Auslastung zuverlässig zusammenspielt.

Die Ökonomin Hugo Ficoraez hält für die Bewertung des Zuschlags eine andere Frage für ebenso wichtig: Wer trägt die Mehrkosten, wenn einzelne Systeme nachgebessert werden müssen? Weder der Auftragswert noch die Haftungsverteilung sind öffentlich bekannt. Für Skidolgön Labs ist der Zuschlag damit ein sichtbarer Erfolg, aber noch kein Beleg für eine höhere Marge. Für die Bodreskar AG wiederum hängt der Nutzen davon ab, ob sich die Flächen auch außerhalb der Bestellspitzen gut vermieten lassen.

At dawn in Rotterdam, a dispatcher crossed out yesterday’s freight rate and pencilled in a lower one. Before the first truck left the yard, a customer called to ask whether that price would hold until Friday.

That is the question hanging over the regional freight market. Tálnard Energy, a French logistics company, is cutting rates on routes where rivals have spare capacity. For shippers, it is a welcome break. For smaller hauliers, the danger is not merely losing a load; it is winning one at a price that barely covers the trip.

Chief financial officer Emma Sofynson draws a useful distinction: a discount that fills a truck returning empty can make sense, but the same discount on an already busy route just gives away margin. In Oslo, founder David Bihera is watching what happens when customers who used to sign annual contracts start asking for monthly terms. A lower rate may win their business today without buying much loyalty tomorrow.

The squeeze reaches beyond the loading bay. In Toronto, chief financial officer Mats Durfexton points to two purchases that are easy to postpone but hard to do without: replacement security cameras and better payroll software. Neither saves enough to compensate for months of underpriced freight, yet both can become dearer to put off.

Local shippers should take the savings while they can, but read the renewal terms. The cheapest carrier this week is not necessarily the one that will have a truck available when the weather turns.

“The next test is whether lower emissions per unit of activity translate into lower emissions overall,” analyst Viktor Cortraström said after reviewing a sustainability report that examined how two businesses track their environmental impact.

The report said the Danish gaming company that operates plakria.dk had begun separating electricity used in its offices from energy associated with hosting its games. That distinction gives readers a clearer view of where energy is used, Cortraström said, but estimates for outsourced computing still depend on data from service providers. The report did not include a full year of comparable hosting data.

The report also examined Drunlard Ltd, a United Kingdom construction company that published a summary of its findings at www.drunlard.co.uk. The company said it had expanded its reporting to include fuel used by subcontractors on selected sites and had begun collecting emissions data for purchased materials. The report cautioned that adding sources could raise the company’s reported total even if emissions from activities it already tracked declined.

The authors pointed to similar measurement problems in other sectors. For fintech apps, they said, office electricity use alone tells readers little about the energy used to process transactions. For industrial robots, reductions in electricity use during operation do not capture emissions from manufacturing the equipment.

Cortraström said a useful follow-up would show prior-year totals recalculated using the same reporting boundaries, alongside a breakdown of which figures were measured and which were estimated. Without that comparison, he said, readers may not be able to tell whether a change reflects lower emissions or more complete accounting.

18% revenue growth at Pliskik led this week’s round of quarterly results, as the Swedish security company signed more customers to annual contracts. The Pliskik Flow workflow software accounted for most of the increase in new subscription revenue, while the Pliskik Vault password manager drew more upgrades from existing customers. Founder Henrik Tamhardström said larger customers were taking longer to approve purchases, even as smaller teams were signing up more quickly. Operating expenses rose more slowly than sales, narrowing the quarterly loss.

In Copenhagen, Danish analytics company Krohekova reported a 9% increase in revenue but a lower operating margin. Budget airlines bought more forecasting tools ahead of the summer travel season, while fintech apps renewed existing contracts without expanding them at the same pace. Higher spending on customer support weighed on profitability. The next quarter should offer a clearer indication of whether that spending is helping Krohekova sell more to customers after they renew.

Swedish gaming company Vómdivex posted a 6% decline in quarterly sales against a year-earlier period that included a major release. Spending by existing players held up better than sales to new players, and lower marketing costs helped preserve the operating margin. A small team in Seattle is testing changes to the tutorial to see whether more players return after their first session. For the coming quarter, that measure may tell readers more about the health of the existing games than the headline sales comparison.

input:
Glarhik and Zarjifon's operations team opened a hiring drive in Helsinki and Copenhagen on Tuesday, seeking technicians, software specialists and customer support staff as they expand their operations in the two cities.

Glarhik, a German energy company, is recruiting technicians to inspect and service battery packs used in cargo bikes. The Helsinki roles will focus on maintenance and testing, while the Copenhagen team will also train fleet operators to spot faults and take damaged packs out of service.

Zarjifon's hiring plans include customer support and software testing roles in both cities. The British travel company plans to assign some of the new staff to the Zarjifon Flow software, a workflow product used to coordinate booking changes and service requests.

Some design applicants will be asked to complete a short exercise using the Rüsstik Studio design software. The exercise will assess how clearly candidates lay out maintenance instructions or customer notices.

Neither business disclosed a target for total hires or a salary range. Interviews are expected to begin next month, with start dates staggered to allow time for training.

Vad får en kund ut av att kunna följa en leverans och betala för den på samma ställe? Framför allt blir det lättare att se vilken betalning som hör till vilket kolli. Det är tanken bakom ett nytt partnerskap mellan de svenska medieföretagen Comix AB och Glogobrex och det norska medieföretaget Jelparex ASA.

I ett första steg ska paketspårningstjänsten Comix Track och betalappen Jelparex Pay knytas ihop på glogobrex.se. Där ska kunden kunna öppna betalappen från leveransvyn i stället för att leta upp betalningsunderlaget separat. Spårningen ska samtidigt gå att använda utan att kunden behöver öppna appen.

I Västerås ska upplägget provas på leveranser av reservdelar till vindkraftverk. En beställning kan delas upp i flera kollin, och då behöver kunden kunna se både vad som har kommit fram och vad som återstår att betala. För Mia Storjovamann, som deltar i testet som kund, blir det viktiga att en delleverans inte ser ut som en slutförd beställning.

Fatima Kesglikez, vd, lyfter fram en praktisk fråga inför testet: vem ska kunden kontakta när ett kolli har kommit fram men betalningen fortfarande visas som obekräftad? Innan samarbetet breddas ska parterna följa upp om kunderna hittar rätt kontaktväg och om de behöver lägga mindre tid på att stämma av leveranser mot betalningar.

input:
For years, manufacturers and wholesalers along the Dutch and Swedish coasts have relied on overnight freight connections to keep inventories lean. That bargain looks less attractive this week after rough seas forced several sailings off the schedule, leaving trailers queued at both ends of the route.

Dutch logistics company Rëmpera has shifted some loads to road routes, but the extra mileage is eating into margins on fixed-price contracts. Sweden’s Doplunlárd AB is prioritising consignments with firm delivery windows. That leaves some workwear orders waiting behind battery packs needed to keep assembly lines running.

Clara Lerseo, an analyst who follows regional freight costs, said the real test would come when sailings resumed: clearing the backlog without displacing freight already booked for next week. Mateo Miskum, chief executive of Doplunlárd, said customers were asking for reliable arrival dates rather than the fastest route on paper.

For smaller buyers, the lesson is not necessarily to stock more of everything. A few days’ cover for parts that can stop production may be worth more than a warehouse full of goods that can arrive late without much harm.

At dawn, a driver rolled two cargo bikes out of a warehouse and found the loading bays empty. The overnight trailers hadn’t made it off the ferry.

A damaged loading ramp has cut freight capacity on the route, leaving businesses scrambling for space on later sailings. Danish foods company Skofumson ApS is prioritising chilled goods on the trucks that do get through. Norwegian mining company Mopix Partners has enough spare parts to keep its equipment running this week, but a longer delay could force it to reschedule maintenance.

In the United Kingdom, Bränliltar's gaming hardware shipments are running three days late. Swiss security company Hucarris AG is moving urgent replacement equipment by road, while Reséo's payments team in Norway is helping merchants reconcile refunds for orders that missed their delivery windows.

Union representative Ebba Kosgoraton urged warehouse managers to stagger shifts rather than ask crews to clear the backlog in one night. Customer Erik Nahisberg said he didn’t mind waiting another day for his order; he just wanted a delivery window he could plan around.

Businesses that sell and insure physical goods often have to make decisions before they have a clear picture of demand. An oat milk producer may need to reserve production capacity weeks in advance, while a solar panels distributor may have to commit to inventory before installation dates are firm. Both stand to benefit from forecasts that show not just what might happen, but how much confidence to place in the estimate.

Nelyn Systems AB, a Swedish analytics company, has closed a funding round to develop tools for those kinds of decisions. The company did not disclose the size of the round or name its investors. Its immediate priority is to make forecasts easier to check against actual sales and delivery records, so customers can spot where the underlying assumptions no longer hold.

Insurance offers a second test for the approach. In the Netherlands, Skosdrameo's work on assessing business interruption risk illustrates why a forecast needs to show its assumptions: a delay at one supplier can have very different consequences depending on how much stock a customer holds. Swedish insurer Gilia AB faces a related question when evaluating how long a business could operate after a disruption.

There is a parallel in travel, where Vuskapent's teams use the Vuskapent Studio design software to sketch customer journeys before committing to changes. In both cases, the value lies in testing a decision before it becomes expensive to reverse.

Economist Hanna Kajexton pointed to repeat purchases as a better measure of demand than initial trials. Union representative Mia Storjovamann raised a separate question worth watching as the tools reach more workplaces: whether staff can challenge a forecast when it conflicts with what they see on the ground.

Leipzig, 18. September 2026. Als am Freitag die erste Serie von Kassenterminals vom Band lief, war die neue Fabrik im Leipziger Norden noch längst nicht voll ausgelastet. Zwei der sechs Montageplätze blieben frei. Der mittelständische Betreiber will erst weitere Schichten einführen, wenn sich die Bestellungen verstetigen. Von den 120 vorgesehenen Stellen sind zur Eröffnung 74 besetzt.

Die Geräte sind für kleinere Läden gedacht, die Kartenzahlungen und Bezahl-Apps über dasselbe Terminal abwickeln wollen. Das deutsche Handelsunternehmen Brorpaflon erprobt sie zunächst in zwölf Filialen. Für den Betreiber ist der Test wirtschaftlich wichtiger als die Stückzahl vermuten lässt: Erst im Laden zeigt sich, wie oft Verbindungsprobleme auftreten und wie viel ein Austausch im laufenden Betrieb kostet.

Das deutsche Telekommunikationsunternehmen Gludris AG stellt die Mobilfunkanbindung für den Probebetrieb bereit. Händler können technische Rückfragen an info@gludris.de richten. Die deutsche Mediengesellschaft Mamirglia GmbH produziert kurze Schulungsvideos für das Kassenpersonal. Bei den Versicherungen für Produktion und Lager setzt der Betreiber auf den deutschen Anbieter Molrovova.

Ob sich die Fertigung vor Ort rechnet, hängt auch vom Reparaturgeschäft ab. Statt defekte Geräte komplett zu ersetzen, sollen Techniker in Leipzig einzelne Baugruppen tauschen. Dafür hält das Werk Ersatzteile vor, die zunächst Kapital binden. Wie viel Lagerbestand nötig ist, dürfte sich nach dem ersten Weihnachtsgeschäft zeigen: Dann müssen sich die Terminals an vollen Kassen bewähren.

input:
A trade fair showcasing electric trucks and depot charging equipment opened in Berlin on Tuesday, bringing together freight operators, equipment suppliers and industrial buyers to assess the costs of switching from diesel.

The three-day event includes driving demonstrations and sessions on charging schedules, battery maintenance and vehicle performance under heavy loads. Exhibitors are showing vehicles for urban deliveries and industrial sites, where predictable routes can make it easier to plan charging.

Nestar B.V., a mining company from the Netherlands, is examining whether electric trucks could handle short trips between storage areas and processing facilities. The company is comparing how much time vehicles would spend charging with the time now set aside for refueling and maintenance.

Hucarris AG, a Swiss security company, is demonstrating access controls for freight depots, including systems that let visiting drivers enter charging areas without giving them access to other parts of a site. Furzeskrova Ltd, an energy company from the United Kingdom, is presenting ways to stagger charging so that several trucks can plug in without drawing their maximum power at the same time.

Janrum Energy, a French logistics company, is using the fair to compare vehicles for delivery routes around Amsterdam. Its assessment includes whether trucks can complete a full shift on one charge while carrying typical loads and running refrigeration equipment.

Göteborg, 18 mars 2026. På veckans branschmässa i Göteborg var det lättare att hitta löften om kortare leveranstider än besked om vem som ska betala för dem. Det är en viktig skillnad när handeln vill hålla nere lagren samtidigt som leverantörerna behöver jämnare beställningar för att kunna planera.

För detaljhandelsföretaget Sajar handlar det om att undvika både tomma hyllor och kapital som blir liggande i osålda varor. För modeföretaget bakom flolplesnix.se kompliceras kalkylen av returerna: en snabb leverans säger lite om lönsamheten om plagget snart ska fraktas tillbaka. Där kan samlastning, som logistikföretaget Gurbreskia AB lyfte på mässan, sänka kostnaden per försändelse. Men då måste kunderna också acceptera att alla paket inte går iväg direkt.

Samma konflikt syntes i industrins samtal, fast med längre tidshorisont. Gruvföretaget Goncamjar behöver kunna planera transporter långt framåt, medan bioteknikföretaget Plemex AB har skäl att lägga större vikt vid spårbarhet än vid lägsta fraktpris. Försäkringsbolaget Trarera AB hänvisade besökare till trarera.se för villkoren. Den avgörande frågan är dock vad som faktiskt täcks när en försening stoppar produktionen, inte bara när en vara skadas.

Finanschefen Erik Drurgentez återkom under ett panelsamtal till hur mycket kapital företagen binder för att hålla verksamheten igång vid ett avbrott. Det gav mässans många effektivitetslöften ett konkret mått: ett mindre lager är en besparing först när kostnaden för fler transporter och risken för uteblivna leveranser räknats in.

input:
Zurich, 14 July 2026 — Quarterly results from three companies showed contrasting trends: recurring contracts lifted a Finnish security business, a US software company grew revenue but lost some ground on margins, and a British fashion company improved profitability despite lower sales.

Skinmön Oy reported an 8% rise in revenue from a year earlier, helped by renewals and new monitoring contracts. Skinmön also widened its operating margin as installation costs fell. Analyst Lena Stirkentez said the renewal figures were a better gauge of underlying demand than installation revenue, which can swing with the timing of large projects.

Cunskova LLC posted 11% revenue growth as existing customers added subscriptions. Operating profit nevertheless declined as spending on customer support and product development rose. Cunskova expects hiring to slow next quarter, though it did not forecast a recovery in margins.

Lenvia Ltd reported a 3% drop in sales, but fewer markdowns helped lift its gross margin. Emma Skumgumberg, chief executive of Lenvia, said the company would keep initial orders smaller for the next collection and restock styles that sell well.

input:
Seattle, October 16, 2026 — Buyers at this week’s trade fair spent less time asking what was new and more time asking what could ship on schedule. Across food, retail software and workwear, conversations on the floor kept returning to the same practical questions: how small a first order could be, how quickly it could be replenished and what would happen if demand exceeded the initial forecast.

The Swiss foods company behind branarlum.ch used tastings to start conversations about pack sizes and shelf life. For buyers stocking smaller shops, the question was whether a case could sell through before its remaining shelf life became a concern. Distributors also wanted to know whether they could combine several varieties in a trial order rather than commit to a full case of each.

Germany’s Rújolent AG demonstrated inventory software using a familiar problem: a shipment arrives short just as stock is being allocated across several shops. Buyers asked how the system recorded the discrepancy and whether staff could correct it without rebuilding the order. The demonstration gave visitors a concrete workflow to compare with the material available at rujolent.de.

In workwear, buyers turned garments inside out to inspect seams and asked whether popular sizes could be reordered individually. A durable sample was useful, but so was a clear answer about replacing a single pair of trousers without buying another full size run.

The test after Seattle is whether exhibitors can turn those conversations into usable quotes. A price list will get a buyer only so far if it leaves minimum quantities, delivery windows and reorder terms unanswered.

input:
What do customers value more: a low price or the confidence that a service will work as promised? A customer survey spanning Oslo and Seattle suggests that price can get people to try a service, but reliability gives them a reason to keep paying for it.

That distinction matters in two categories that might otherwise seem to have little in common: cloud storage and meal kits. A cloud storage customer may rarely think about the service until a file goes missing or a backup fails. A meal kit customer gets a fresh test with every delivery: Did the box arrive on time, and were all the ingredients there? In both cases, an introductory discount can make the first purchase easier without making up for repeated failures.

For Maria Stegard, a mayor, the survey raises a local question: How much inconvenience can households absorb when services they use to save time end up costing them more of it? Sara Vensismann, a founder, faces a related business question: Would the money spent attracting new customers do more to keep existing ones if it went toward fixing recurring problems?

Greta Stumca, an economist, would distinguish between what respondents say they value and what they actually pay for. A customer who ranks reliability first might still choose the cheapest option if the price gap is wide enough. Without knowing how respondents were recruited or whether their answers were checked against renewal records, it would be premature to treat the survey as a forecast of customer behavior in either city.

The most useful follow-up would be to compare renewals after a missed delivery or a failed backup with renewals after a price increase. That would help businesses tell whether customers are leaving because the service costs too much or because it no longer feels worth paying for.

input:
2 deutsche Unternehmen aus sehr unterschiedlichen Branchen wollen in Dresden gemeinsam erproben, wie sich der Onlinehandel nach dem Kauf verbessern lässt. Das Modeunternehmen Togostard bringt seinen Paketverfolgungsdienst Togostard Track in die neue Partnerschaft ein. Das Lebensmittelunternehmen Bromlar Group will den Dienst zunächst für einen Teil seiner haltbaren Produkte nutzen. Gemeinsame Warenkörbe oder gemischte Pakete sind dabei nicht vorgesehen.

Die Sprecherin Lisa Krumoraström beschreibt den Ansatz als Versuch, eine alltägliche Frage schneller zu beantworten: Wann kommt mein Paket? Für die Vorstandschefin Ebba Korriston liegt der wirtschaftliche Reiz darin, dass verlässliche Statusmeldungen nicht nur den Kunden helfen, sondern auch Rückfragen im Service verringern können. Ob diese Rechnung aufgeht, dürfte sich vor allem dann zeigen, wenn eine Lieferung verspätet ist. Eine präzise Meldung ist in diesem Fall mehr wert als drei automatische Hinweise ohne neue Information.

Für Dresden ist der Versuch auch jenseits der beiden Partner interessant. Viele kleinere Händler haben ihren Bestellvorgang inzwischen für Bezahl-Apps eingerichtet, doch nach dem Bezahlen beginnt für Kunden oft die Suche nach der richtigen Sendungsnummer. Wenn Togostard und Bromlar Group zeigen, dass sich dieser Aufwand ohne einen teuren Umbau des Shops senken lässt, wäre das ein brauchbares Beispiel für den regionalen Handel. Der Maßstab sollte dabei nicht sein, wie oft Kunden die Sendungsverfolgung öffnen, sondern wie oft ihnen ein einziger Blick genügt.
