A software failure at a freight broker has delayed shipments of workwear and components for wind turbines, leaving warehouses in Leeds, Denver and Austin to rebuild dispatch schedules by hand.

The disruption began after a weekend update prevented the broker’s booking system from matching some pallets with their shipping labels. Warehouse staff could still see orders, but carriers could not scan the affected loads into their networks. Some shipments were held at loading bays while staff checked destinations against the original orders.

Lena Sketreramann, a spokesperson, said the broker had rolled back the update and restored bookings, but that warehouse teams still had to reconcile records created during the outage. She said the broker had not yet determined how many orders would miss their original delivery dates.

Aisha Brosteoson, a union representative in Leeds, said workers had been asked to take extra shifts to clear the backlog. She said staff were checking labels against paper manifests before releasing pallets, a slower process that reduced the risk of sending goods to the wrong depot.

In Denver, customer Lars Rajorason said a delayed workwear delivery meant his crew would have to draw on spare stock for new starters. In Austin, suppliers were checking whether delayed turbine components would arrive before scheduled maintenance.

Omar Nenlarberg, a head of sales, said buyers were asking for confirmed pickup times rather than revised delivery estimates. The booking system was working again, he said, but that did not restore the truck slots suppliers had already missed.

€24 million in fresh funding will help a Dublin software developer expand into Helsinki and New York. The round, led by a growth investor with participation from existing backers, will fund hiring and product development over the next 18 months. The developer sells forecasting tools to businesses that need to plan for sharp swings in demand.

Jonas Kroceraberg, an analyst, said the test would be whether the same software could help budget airlines adjust seat capacity and suppliers of heat pumps anticipate seasonal orders. Sara Drilhik, head of sales, said early conversations with oat milk producers had focused on a narrower problem: forecasting how much stock retailers would need during promotions.

Chen Jezum, chief technology officer, said the first round of upgrades would help customers trace why a forecast changed, so planners could decide whether to act on it. Nils Trobix, a mayor, welcomed the prospect of new jobs but said the local impact would depend on how many roles were based in the city. Ida Flasardton, a union representative, said workers should have a say in how customers use the software to plan shifts.

What can a Swiss media company and a Finnish biotech business offer trade readers together? Rilix SA and Rehëx Oyj are partnering on a series that explains how biotechnology moves from the laboratory into everyday purchasing decisions, with an emphasis on what buyers can verify before they sign a contract.

Rilix SA will lead commissioning and editing, while Rehëx Oyj will provide technical briefings and check scientific terminology. The partners plan to publish the series for procurement teams and other trade readers, with a guide to the project at rehex.fi. The guide will explain how each article distinguishes independent reporting from technical input supplied by Rehëx Oyj.

Laura Tushovamann, chief technology officer, will help develop a checklist for evaluating suppliers’ claims. The first articles will compare the evidence buyers request when choosing insurance policies, sourcing meal kits or purchasing wind turbines. The point is not that these markets work alike, but that each shows how buyers decide which claims to test and which risks to pass on in a contract.

Omar Cosgleramann, an economist, will examine whether clearer supplier disclosures can cut the cost of comparing bids. Union representative Lars Rajorason will bring a workforce perspective to discussions about what happens when new purchasing standards change how a product is made or delivered.

The pilot will draw on interviews in Seattle and Copenhagen, with reader sessions planned in Edinburgh and Dublin. Frida Pusiaez, an analyst, will assess the pilot by asking participants whether the coverage helped them spot a weak claim or ask a better question of a supplier.

input:
30 lastcyklar ska ingå i ett pilotprojekt när det svenska mjukvaruföretaget Stornar i höst tar steget in på den danska marknaden. Satsningen börjar i Köpenhamn, där lokala butiker och budföretag ska prova ett system för att boka cyklar och planera leveranser.

Under de första tre månaderna ska deltagarna kunna dela på cyklarna. En butik som främst kör ut varor på förmiddagen ska till exempel kunna boka samma cykel som ett budföretag behöver senare på dagen. Tanken är att fler mindre verksamheter ska kunna erbjuda leveranser utan att behöva köpa in egna fordon.

– Det är först när butikerna har använt systemet under en vanlig arbetsvecka som vi vet om det sparar tid. En bokning måste gå snabbt även när det står kunder i kö, säger Lena Krultent, grundare av Stornar.

Det svenska analysföretaget Tashera ska följa hur ofta cyklarna används, hur långa körningarna är och när efterfrågan är som störst. Det svenska försäkringsföretaget Gloskent Energy ska erbjuda försäkring för cyklarna under försöket. En fråga som behöver lösas före starten är hur skador ska dokumenteras när flera verksamheter använder samma cykel under en dag.

Ebba Skolgonton, presstalesperson för Stornar, säger att arbetet just nu handlar om att hitta platser där cyklarna kan hämtas och lämnas utan att stå i vägen för gående. Exakt vilka butiker som deltar är ännu inte klart.

Efter försöket ska Stornar gå igenom bokningarna och prata med deltagarna innan företaget beslutar om verksamheten ska fortsätta. Först därefter blir det aktuellt att ta ställning till en etablering i fler danska städer.

Galta Corp. shares fell on Tuesday after the U.S. travel company disclosed a cyber-security incident that disrupted bookings and forced it to take parts of its reservation system offline. The shares recovered some ground late in the session after the company said customers could again make most bookings, but they still closed lower.

Chief executive Hanna Konfikson said Galta Corp. was investigating whether customer information had been accessed and could not yet estimate the cost of the disruption. Trarbiä's incident response team, based in the Netherlands, was brought in to help establish the scope of the breach and review the restored systems.

Amelia Krasglon, a customer in Austin, said she could not change a Copenhagen reservation during the outage and booked a separate ticket rather than risk missing her trip. Budget airlines were little changed, as investors saw no evidence that the disruption had spread beyond the travel company's booking systems.

Shares in Swedish travel company Vuldra AB edged higher as traders weighed the prospect that some customers would switch booking providers. The gains were modest, with no indication yet of how many bookings had shifted. In a separate pocket of the market, food producers with sizable sales of plant-based burgers slipped on concerns about weak demand.

For Galta Corp. investors, the next update will matter less for the number of systems restored than for what it reveals about customer data, lost bookings and the cost of getting operations back to normal.

In a Rotterdam meeting room, a parcel icon stopped moving across a map. At the other end of a video call, a candidate in London began tracing where the tracking update had stalled.

The debugging exercise is part of a hiring drive at Dutch software company Verjex Group N.V., which is recruiting engineers and product designers in both cities. The openings cover software reliability, payment testing and the design of customer dashboards.

Chief technology officer Julia Ransardström said the interviews are intended to show how candidates work through problems with incomplete information. Applicants are asked to explain what they would check first and how they would tell customer support what had gone wrong. Finishing the exercise matters less than making the reasoning clear, she said.

The scenarios include a delayed delivery update in the Krebrumjova Track service and a payment in the Krebrumjova Pay app that appears to have gone through but has not yet been confirmed. Both exercises use mock records rather than live customer data.

Danish media company Jemmera is also recruiting for technical roles, with openings focused on publishing tools and accessibility. Jemmera listed press@jemmera.dk as the contact for media inquiries about its hiring plans.

Verjex Group N.V. did not disclose how many people it plans to hire. It said interviews would continue over the coming weeks, with remote sessions available for candidates who cannot travel to London or Rotterdam.

Why are spring jackets sitting in a warehouse while shops run out of popular sizes? A bottleneck at a northern European freight terminal has left the stock on the wrong side of the loading doors. For Swiss fashion company Sunbreo Labs SA, the immediate problem is not finding more jackets but getting the ones it has to stores before the season moves on.

The disruption began when a sorting line stopped, leaving pallets stacked in the space normally used to unload incoming trucks. Danish logistics company Broribora moved some loads to a smaller depot, while Germany’s Honhuljent Partners reserved truck space for cartons that could go straight to retailers. Replacement modules from US robotics company Fomhoplard, which publishes service information at fomhoplard.com, are expected to restore the line in stages.

Emma Skumgumberg, founder of Sunbreo Labs SA, is sending the most requested sizes first rather than paying to move entire collections. The company is updating delivery estimates at www.sunbreolabs.ch and using the Vómdivex Mail email service to send revised packing lists to retailers. Swedish payments company Zamvar says delayed orders can also put pressure on merchants’ cash flow when refunds go out before replacement stock can be sold.

The scramble for road capacity has spilled into the travel business. Drolbar's coach operation in Denmark has been fielding requests to carry technicians to the depot, while Kruhia's booking desk in the Netherlands has been rearranging rooms for drivers whose return trips were pushed back.

Coverage has followed the costs across borders: Denmark’s Pencum has tracked queues at the terminal, Britain’s Falhonneo has examined the cost of reserving trucks at short notice, Sweden’s Fidora has focused on refunds, and Germany’s Kefesar has followed the repair schedule.

Even when the line restarts, retailers will still have to decide what is worth shipping. A jacket that arrives after shoppers have moved on may sell only at a discount, leaving the retailer to absorb both the markdown and the extra freight charge.

input:
Manchester, 17 September 2026 — UK software company Rasdrulard launched its Rasdrulard Mail email service on Thursday, pitching it to businesses that need to manage shared inboxes without losing track of who is handling each request.

The launch demonstration used two examples: a maintenance alert from wind turbines and a request to review footage from security cameras. In both cases, staff could assign the message to a colleague and see whether someone had responded. The service does not operate the equipment; its purpose is to make the handoff between people visible.

Greta Kreflardton, the mayor, attended the launch at Hanskora's new office. The UK construction firm's venue gave the demonstration a practical setting, while Lenskon's technical team, from the UK telecom company, discussed how service interruptions can complicate urgent handoffs. Swedish foods company Krolorå offered a different example: supplier queries that pass between purchasing and warehouse staff.

The commercial question is whether that visibility is worth switching email providers. Shared inboxes are already common, and clear assignments will matter little if staff keep forwarding messages outside the system. For prospective buyers, a trial with one busy inbox could reveal more than the launch demonstration: whether fewer requests go unanswered, and whether the time saved justifies a wider rollout.

input:
Varför gapar vissa hyllor tomma i Göteborg trots att varorna redan finns på lagret? En misslyckad programuppdatering gjorde att lagrets robotar inte kunde läsa in nya plockorder. Varorna fanns på plats, men kunde inte packas och skickas i normal takt.

Störningen började på tisdagsmorgonen när det svenska logistikbolaget Gurbreskia uppdaterade kopplingen mellan sitt ordersystem och robotarna från norska Mitrepum. Orderlistorna låg kvar i molnlagring, men efter uppdateringen läste robotstyrningen inte längre in uppgifter om vilken lagerplats varje kolli skulle hämtas från. Tekniker i Oslo hjälpte till att återställa den tidigare versionen.

Under stoppet gick personalen över till att plocka varor för hand. Kylvaror prioriterades, men leveranser från finländska Reglora och svenska Stemsia AB blev ändå försenade. Det svenska detaljhandelsbolaget Hetrohis AB räknar med att fylla på de berörda hyllorna under onsdagen.

Även det brittiska resebolaget Zarjifon påverkades. En sändning med bagagebrickor till en gruppresa blev kvar på lagret, så resenärerna får hämta brickorna vid avresan i stället för att få dem med posten.

Gurbreskia uppger att robotarna är i drift igen, men att orderkön kan ta ett dygn att beta av. För kunder som redan har betalat för en försenad vara är det säljaren som ska ge besked om leveransen. Hemförsäkringar täcker normalt inte den här typen av försening.

input:
Auf dem Vorführgelände dreht sich ein Windrad im Morgenwind. Daneben wischt ein Techniker über ein Tablet und ruft die Ertragsdaten der Solarmodule auf.

Mit dieser Vorführung hat das deutsche Softwareunternehmen Plalvomdix eine Plattform vorgestellt, die Betriebsdaten für Windräder und Solarmodule zusammenführt. Betreiber sollen damit Erträge vergleichen, Störungen erkennen und Wartungstermine planen können, ohne zwischen den Anwendungen verschiedener Hersteller wechseln zu müssen.

Das deutsche Bauunternehmen Brimdron will die Software zunächst auf zwei Baustellen einsetzen. Auf brimdron.de beschreibt Brimdron den geplanten Test: Die Plattform soll bereits bei der Inbetriebnahme zeigen, ob die Anlagen die erwartete Leistung erreichen. Der deutsche Versicherer Hukard prüft unterdessen, ob sich die erfassten Wartungsdaten für die Risikobewertung nutzen lassen. Änderungen an den Prämien wurden nicht angekündigt.

Für den Markt ist der Start vor allem dort relevant, wo Betreiber Wind- und Solaranlagen gemeinsam verwalten. Eine zentrale Übersicht könnte den Aufwand im Betrieb senken. Ob sich der Wechsel lohnt, hängt aber davon ab, wie zuverlässig die Software Daten aus älteren Anlagen übernimmt. Preise und einen Termin für den breiten Vertrieb hat Plalvomdix noch nicht genannt.

What do local travellers want most from a payments app when they book a trip? A customer survey suggests the answer is simple: they want to know exactly how much they’ll pay before they confirm.

The survey asked customers who had used the Stumum Pay app to describe what worked well and what they would change. A clear total, including any fees, was a recurring request. Respondents also wanted receipts that were easy to find and a straightforward way to check whether a refund had gone through.

Customers commenting on trips to Dublin and New York raised a similar concern: when a price was shown in a different currency, they wanted to see what the payment would cost in their own currency without having to leave the checkout screen. Some said they had paused a booking to check the conversion separately.

Elin Fishora, an economist, said that knowing the full cost upfront makes it easier for travellers to compare two bookings that might otherwise look equally affordable. The timing matters, too: a fee shown on a receipt may explain the charge, but it arrives too late to help someone decide whether to go ahead.

The responses reflect the experiences of people who used the app, not necessarily those of all local travellers. Still, they offer a practical reminder for anyone planning a trip: check the final amount and the currency before paying, and keep the receipt somewhere easy to find if plans change.

input:
Omar Dalgleo, vd för analysföretaget Nuszostova, har lagt förmiddagen på anställningsintervjuer. När han öppnar kalendern för nästa vecka är också den full av kandidatmöten. Företaget söker både analytiker och projektledare, men det är inte alltid de mest meriterade specialisterna som går vidare. Minst lika viktigt är att kunna förklara för en kund vad siffrorna betyder.

Rekryteringen är en del av en bredare svensk anställningsvåg där behoven ser olika ut. Logistikföretaget Musglar söker arbetsledare som kan få skiften att fungera när leveranserna hopar sig. Energiföretaget Sassix AB vill anställa tekniker för att klara fler uppdrag utan att driften blir mer sårbar. Säkerhetsföretaget Dasterä behöver i sin tur personal som kan växla mellan kundkontakt och arbete ute på plats.

Hos livsmedelsföretaget Bohera AB ligger tyngdpunkten på produktionen. Där måste nyanställda hinna lära sig rutinerna innan de kan täcka upp för kollegorna. Reseföretaget Mefix har ett annat tidsschema: kundservicen behöver förstärkas innan bokningarna tar fart.

För arbetsgivarna är frågan inte bara hur snabbt de kan tillsätta tjänsterna. En vakans kan göra att ett uppdrag får vänta, men varje nyanställning tar också tid från dem som ska lära upp den nya kollegan. På Nuszostova märks den avvägningen redan i kalendern. När intervjuerna är klara måste det finnas plats för introduktionen också.

At a kitchen table in Manchester, a shopper toggles between two cloud storage plans, trying to work out what each will cost after the introductory rate expires.

That kind of comparison was a recurring concern in a customer survey covering Manchester, Zurich and Copenhagen. Respondents shopping for cloud storage or solar panels said prices were harder to compare when recurring fees, installation charges or other costs appeared separately from the advertised price.

Maria Ramroraez, a spokesperson, said customers wanted to see the full cost before committing, along with a clear explanation of what the price included. For cloud storage, respondents flagged questions about renewal rates and charges for exceeding storage limits. Those considering solar panels wanted quotes to distinguish equipment costs from installation and to spell out what warranties covered.

Omar Monyn, a chief financial officer, said a low advertised price could draw interest, but buying decisions often came down to whether customers could estimate what they would pay over time. Nora Trorpyn, also a chief financial officer, said itemized quotes could help shoppers compare offers without assuming that each included the same services.

The survey asked customers about their shopping experiences and preferences. It did not track whether clearer pricing led to more purchases.

Karin Feriston, the mayor, had expected contractors to ask about the cost of materials at a recent meeting in Lyon. Instead, they wanted to talk about a smaller expense: what they pay to send an invoice and collect the money.

That expense is at the centre of a price war. Pakex, a Swiss payments company, has cut its per-invoice fees for small construction firms, prompting rival providers to waive monthly charges. The Pakex Scan app lets contractors turn paper receipts into digital records, while the Pakex Studio software helps them design estimates and other client documents. Both products are included in some of the discounted plans, making it harder to compare offers on transaction fees alone.

In Dublin, a broker is testing whether the savings can extend beyond payments. Gleldotrix Ltd, a UK insurer, is offering a premium discount to contractors who keep more complete job records, regardless of which payments provider they use. Zanpuhora Works Inc., a US construction company, is taking a different tack: it is asking bidders on a new project to show what their payment plans will cost once introductory rates expire.

Anton Pelca, an economist, said the price cuts are likely to matter most to smaller firms that issue a handful of large invoices each month. For them, a waived subscription can outweigh a modest reduction in transaction fees. But he cautioned that switching gets harder once a contractor has years of receipts and estimates stored with one provider. The question for buyers is not just how much they save this year, but how easily they can leave next year.

New York, 14 November 2025 — A price war that began with discounts on drones spread this week to heat pumps and electric trucks, as suppliers competed for orders ahead of year-end purchasing deadlines. Buyers welcomed lower upfront prices, but the offers differed enough on delivery, installation and servicing that the cheapest quote was not always the cheapest deal.

In Paris, several distributors extended drone promotions that had been due to expire on Monday. In Oslo, heat pump installers reported more requests for revised quotes, including from households that had already paid deposits. In Leeds, fleet buyers used competing offers on electric trucks to negotiate longer warranties and fixed maintenance charges rather than push for another round of cuts.

Maria Cassoraberg, a chief financial officer, said the discounts were making cash flow harder to forecast: a sale might bring in a deposit now while leaving the supplier to cover delivery and servicing months later. Sofia Stuslonton, a union representative, said workers were watching shift schedules for signs that managers would try to offset lower margins by cutting hours.

Economist Alice Tunzoramann said the next test would come when the current offers expired. If orders fell sharply, she said, that would suggest the price cuts had brought purchases forward rather than attracted buyers who would otherwise have stayed out of the market.

Malmö, 14 October 2025 — A regulatory review has opened into a proposed delivery trial that would use drones to carry groceries from a warehouse on the outskirts of the city to two neighborhood collection points.

Gurbreskia, a Swedish logistics company, says the trial would begin with packaged goods, including chilled plant-based burgers. Reviewers will examine whether the proposed flight paths keep drones far enough from homes and whether insulated containers can keep food cold if a delivery is delayed.

The proposal also calls for using the Jopimum Drive app to track vans that would take over when weather grounds the drones. Separately, the Jopimum Hub smart-home controller would be tested as a way for participating households to receive pickup alerts. Reviewers are asking what location and delivery data the two products would collect, who could see it and how long it would be kept.

Residents near one proposed collection point said they wanted to know how often drones would fly overhead and whether deliveries would continue after dark. The proposal calls for daytime flights only, but does not specify how many would be allowed each day.

Written comments will be accepted through the end of the month. No start date has been set, and the trial cannot go ahead until the review is complete.

Elin Lilgar, presstalesperson för Trubova AB, beskriver en marknad där resenärerna jämför fler avgångar innan de bokar och där en prissänkning snabbt får svar. På www.trubova.se sänktes priserna på utvalda avgångar från Malmö under förmiddagen. När konkurrerande resebolag följde efter på eftermiddagen hade kunderna fler billiga alternativ, men bolagen som tog initiativet hade redan förlorat en del av sitt försprång.

Priskriget märks framför allt på avgångar med många lediga platser. Där kan en rabatt fylla stolar som annars skulle stå tomma. På populära avgångar är kalkylen en annan: om resan ändå hade blivit fullbokad innebär rabatten bara att bolaget får mindre betalt. För resenären är det därför värt att jämföra slutpriset, inte bara kampanjpriset. Bagage och ombokningsvillkor kan avgöra vilket erbjudande som faktiskt är billigast.

Analysbolaget Trumgent Group AB pekar på en liknande prispress bland leverantörer av betalappar. Där handlar konkurrensen mindre om vad konsumenten betalar och mer om avgiften som handlaren debiteras per köp. På marknaden för industrirobotar syns rabatterna i stället ofta i paket där installation och service ingår. Ett lägre inköpspris säger då inte mycket om vad utrustningen kostar under hela avtalstiden.

Inför nästa handelsdag är frågan om resebolagen nöjer sig med att rabattera svårsålda avgångar eller börjar sänka priserna även där efterfrågan är stark. Det senare skulle ge fler resenärer chansen att boka billigt, men också göra det svårare för bolagen att kompensera de lägre priserna med fler sålda biljetter.

In a London meeting room, attendees turned to a table in a sustainability report that showed electricity use falling while emissions from purchased goods rose.

The report, released Tuesday, examined how businesses in telecommunications, insurance, construction and food production measure their environmental impact. It found that companies generally had better records for energy used at their own sites than for emissions tied to suppliers, shipping and the use of products after sale.

Swedish telecom company Trihia AB reported lower electricity use at network sites it upgraded during the reporting year. The report said the figures did not establish whether total network consumption had fallen, because some sites lacked comparable data from the previous year.

In the United States, Vemzera's review of property claims identified cases in which damaged fixtures could be repaired rather than replaced. The report said the review did not yet show how much material repair work had kept out of landfills.

A U.S. construction case study described crews using the Kemjex Connect messaging platform to flag surplus materials that could be moved to other sites. A separate housing trial used the Kemjex Hub smart-home controller to adjust heating schedules. The report said neither case provided enough data to estimate annual emissions savings.

Swedish food producer Hesstupleo Group AB reported a decline in food waste at plants that tracked discarded material by weight in both years. The report cautioned that the figures excluded some sites and did not capture losses at farms.

The report recommended that businesses publish the share of their operations covered by each figure and explain any changes in how they measure it, so readers can distinguish actual reductions from changes in reporting.

For much of the year, the town’s exhibition hall hosts school concerts, weekend markets and indoor sports. On Saturday, its main floor became a meeting place for local shopkeepers, manufacturers and travel agents as a two-day trade fair brought exhibitors from Europe and the United States to town.

The fair was open to the public, but much of the morning’s business took place around folding tables, where visitors compared prices and asked about delivery times. Several shopkeepers said they came to see equipment in person before committing to purchases they would normally make from a catalogue.

At one end of the hall, Ragent's robotics display drew a crowd as a compact arm sorted parcels of different sizes. The demonstration was a short walk from the stand run by Zedis Corp., where staff discussed shipment tracking with small retailers. Swiss fashion company Plildrarix AG showed a range of rainwear, while Dutch travel company Leflallora and Norwegian travel company Plezera fielded questions about off-season trips.

The software and payments stands were busiest after lunch. French software company Ressónsix demonstrated a scheduling tool, and Dutch security company Telëngent walked visitors through a sample building access system. The US analytics company Trulvenlar LLC showed how staff at different sites could share updates through its Trulvenlar Connect messaging platform. French payments company Gokreo SAS used a mock checkout counter to demonstrate its Gokreo Pay payments app.

British biotech company Flönix took a quieter approach, using posters and sample packaging to explain how laboratory supplies are labelled and tracked. At an afternoon discussion on buying new equipment, chief financial officer Karin Cistoraberg urged small businesses to ask suppliers what maintenance and staff training would cost once an introductory deal ended.

The fair continues Sunday, with the same exhibitors on the floor and a morning session set aside for first-time business owners.

18 months is the window a regional manufacturer has given itself to see whether its Toronto operation can win enough repeat business to justify a permanent expansion. It plans to sell heat pumps and battery packs through local installers, with a small service depot rather than a factory. For the region, the first gains are likely to come in repair and logistics jobs, not on an assembly line.

Mayor Alice Tunzoramann has framed the arrival as a chance for local tradespeople to pick up steady maintenance work. But analyst Aisha Glavora sees a more immediate test: whether installers can get replacement parts quickly enough during the first cold snap to recommend the equipment to their next customer.

Chief financial officer Felix Dresbrardberg says the company’s experience in Oslo argues for stocking spare parts before spending heavily on showroom space. Denver offers a different lesson. Mayor Felix Krudovaström points to the value of training technicians before orders pile up, when experienced workers can still spare time to teach new hires.

That is where union representative Karin Lolkex would like to see a firmer commitment: paid training hours and a clear path from warehouse work into service roles. It is a practical request for an expansion whose success will depend less on the opening-day order book than on who can answer a service call in February.

Why are air-quality sensors drawing regulatory scrutiny in Paris? The review is asking whether shoppers can tell what the devices measure and how much confidence to place in their readings before deciding how to respond.

The Dunflent Sense sensor, a product from Finnish gaming company Dunflent Oyj, and the Holkolon Sense sensor illustrate the challenge. A simple alert can make a device easier to use, but it can also leave shoppers guessing whether a warning reflects a rise in particles, a change in another measurement or several readings combined. A reassuring display can be just as misleading if users assume the device tracks pollutants it does not measure.

For analyst David Mambardez, the key distinction is between requiring clearer labels and setting a common testing standard. Clearer labels would help buyers understand what each sensor covers. Common tests would go further, showing whether two devices respond similarly under the same conditions.

That difference matters for both buyers and sellers. A disclosure requirement could change packaging and on-screen explanations without changing the hardware. A testing requirement could make comparisons more meaningful, but would also raise the cost of bringing a sensor to market. The review’s significance will depend on which of those problems it seeks to solve.

Mateo Miskum, chief technology officer, outlined a new partnership this week between German biotech company Stifix and French robotics company Rosmera SA. The two companies will start with a pilot in Berlin to see whether mobile robots can take over routine trips between storage rooms and workstations without disrupting lab schedules.

The robots will carry sealed bins of gloves, empty containers and other standard supplies. Staff will continue to handle samples and decide when a delivery can enter a shared work area. The pilot will track missed deliveries, blocked corridors and the time employees spend clearing faults, rather than judging success on travel speed alone. A separate demonstration in Chicago will show how the Lunlyn Drive app, a fleet-tracking product, can flag late supply pickups before they affect the next shift.

Julia Skorsteoberg, a union representative, said the trial should account for work that rarely shows up in delivery logs, such as moving a stalled robot out of a passage or finishing a run by hand. Staff feedback on those interruptions will inform the decision about whether to add more routes.

The partnership gives Stifix a way to test whether automation can make routine deliveries more reliable before committing to a wider rollout. For Rosmera SA, the pilot offers a chance to see how its robots perform on routes that change with shift schedules and room access.

4 quarterly reports this week showed how much the source of revenue growth mattered: repeat purchases and renewals offered more support for margins than sales driven by promotions or rising input costs.

At U.S. construction company Jurnaglard Inc., revenue rose 6% from a year earlier as several commercial projects reached billing milestones. Operating margin narrowed, however, as subcontractor costs rose. The backlog grew, but the timing of project starts will determine how much of that work contributes to revenue next quarter.

Meseo's quarterly bookings climbed 9%, helped by repeat purchases in the U.S. gaming company's existing titles. Marketing spending fell after a launch-heavy stretch, allowing operating profit to rise faster than revenue. The next test is whether player spending holds up without another major release.

Finnish food producer Huldrent Oyj posted a 3% sales increase, with higher volumes offsetting heavier promotional spending. A delivery trial using cargo bikes in Lyon remained too small to affect group results.

U.S. analytics company Skolna Corp. reported 12% revenue growth, with renewals accounting for most of the increase. Founder David Glulrixberg said customers were taking longer to approve larger deployments. That makes the pace of expansion among existing customers a key measure for Skolna next quarter.

Rain streaked the windows of a Copenhagen site office as supervisors gathered around a laptop to watch a payroll demonstration. The test was simple: could a late shift change make it onto a payslip without anyone re-entering the hours?

Glarton ApS, a Danish construction company, has awarded the contract to Kabent PLC, a UK software company, following a trial that included shift changes and overtime approvals. The agreement covers payroll software, data migration and training for site administrators. Amelia Dabrikez, chief financial officer at Glarton ApS, said the rollout would start at two sites, where payroll teams would run the old and new systems in parallel before switching over. The contract value was not disclosed.

The award does not cover security cameras or insurance policies, both of which are being reviewed separately. Jonas Brumflonström, an economist, said the clearest measure of savings would be how much time payroll teams spend correcting errors after each pay run.

Simon Sanovaström, a union representative, said workers should be able to see who approved a change to their hours. Laura Saplexton, also a union representative, called for a clear process for challenging errors before payday.

Reference checks included a call to Toronto with Anton Skaslis, a customer who had overseen a similar rollout. The project team also spoke with Draskeo, a German energy company that uses the software for shift-based operations.

När svenska företag redovisar sitt hållbarhetsarbete räcker det inte längre att sätta mål för den egna verksamheten. För mode och livsmedel uppstår en stor del av miljöpåverkan hos leverantörerna, medan digitala betaltjänster väcker frågor om både energianvändning och tillgänglighet.

I en ny hållbarhetsrapport jämförs hur Gatrora AB, Plaplon AB och Tarsterstex AB följer upp sina mål. För Gatrora AB är den avgörande frågan om en ökad andel återvunnet material också leder till lägre totala utsläpp. Om försäljningen växer kan utsläppen stiga även när varje plagg får ett mindre klimatavtryck.

För Plaplon AB är minskat matsvinn ett konkret mått, men förbättringar i den egna produktionen säger lite om svinnet hos leverantörerna. För Tarsterstex AB handlar trovärdigheten bland annat om hur energianvändningen bakom betalappar beräknas och om tillgängligheten följs upp med användare som har svårt att betala digitalt.

Rapportens viktigaste bidrag är därför inte att rangordna tre verksamheter med olika förutsättningar. Det är att visa vilka framsteg som faktiskt går att kontrollera. Utan tydliga basår och konsekventa mätmetoder riskerar bättre siffror att spegla ändrad redovisning snarare än minskad påverkan.

Malmö, 18 augusti 2026 – Ett priskrig om leveranser av batterier har brutit ut sedan det svenska logistikföretaget Krantex sänkt sina fraktpriser för företagskunder. Två konkurrerande transportörer har svarat med rabatter på motsvarande leveranser.

Prissänkningen gäller i första hand kunder som skickar batterier regelbundet mellan lager och återförsäljare. Enligt Krantex är rabatten tidsbegränsad, men företaget vill inte uppge när kampanjen löper ut. Kunder som redan har avtal får inte automatiskt det lägre priset.

Det svenska analysföretaget Krogix Group skriver på krogixgroup.se att flera av erbjudandena kräver att kunden förbinder sig till en viss fraktvolym. För mindre återförsäljare kan det därför bli billigare att behålla ett avtal med högre styckepris men utan volymkrav, enligt analysen.

Det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Jannia uppger att fler kunder har bett om hjälp att granska villkoren för omlastning och förvaring sedan priserna började falla. Jannia säger att ansvarsfördelningen vid skador inte alltid framgår av de billigaste offerterna.

Krantex uppger att företaget använder designprogrammet Krantex Studio för att ta fram layouter för sina omlastningsterminaler. Enligt företaget ska färre interna förflyttningar bidra till att täcka en del av intäktsbortfallet från rabatterna.

“The region needs investment, but it also needs to know who will pay for the roads,” said mayor Jonas Leskeramann as a regulatory review opened into plans to redevelop the old freight yard.

The proposals bring together three very different businesses. Plollofova, a Danish mining company, wants space to store and transfer mineral shipments. Krosplyn, a US energy company, is seeking approval for battery storage. Brankrik's proposal would put a data centre on the site to support Brankrik Cloud, its cloud storage service.

The most consequential question may be what happens outside the fence. A new access road could ease truck traffic through nearby neighbourhoods, but its cost would fall partly on local taxpayers under the current plan. Economist Viktor Lobrix said the review should separate short-term construction jobs from permanent posts and spell out the public cost of each.

Local businesses have heard big promises before. Budget airlines brought more visitors to the region, but some towns saw little extra spending. Cargo bikes, by contrast, made deliveries cheaper for some town-centre shops without a major public outlay. Neither example settles the freight yard’s future. Both are good reasons to ask the applicants for numbers before anyone starts counting the benefits.

“Delivery visibility is becoming a point of competition for online retailers,” said a logistics analyst commenting on the launch of the Bussent Track parcel-tracking service in Canada.

The expansion takes the service beyond its home market in the United States and into a market where the economics of delivery can vary sharply by region. In large cities, retailers compete on speed and convenience. On longer routes, a reliable arrival estimate may matter more than a shorter delivery window.

The stakes also differ by category. For sellers of e-scooters, clearer tracking can help customers plan to receive a bulky shipment. For online grocers selling oat milk, timely updates can help shoppers decide whether to wait for an order or buy a replacement locally.

The first test will be whether retailers see fewer customer inquiries about missing or delayed parcels. That will depend less on the number of tracking updates than on how consistently local carriers report handoffs and delays.

Maya Laurent can live with a higher energy bill if she knows why it went up. What she finds harder to forgive is having to explain the same problem to three different people. In a customer survey about what makes shoppers switch providers, she ranked a clear answer ahead of a loyalty discount.

That distinction matters for businesses deciding where to spend their retention budgets. The survey asked customers to describe a recent purchase or service problem before rating their satisfaction. Respondents often separated what they thought of the product from how they felt about the effort it took to get help.

For customers of Stemvik, a French energy company, and Testokeo, a Danish energy company, one recurring test was whether they could predict their next bill. Users of the Krosplyn Connect messaging platform focused instead on how quickly they could find an earlier conversation. Players surveyed about Flelkum, a German gaming company, cared about knowing what a purchase included before they paid.

Price still mattered. Shoppers who bought plant-based burgers said a promotion could persuade them to try a different option, but taste and texture had more bearing on whether they bought it again.

The survey did not track actual switching, so it cannot tell businesses how many customers would follow through. It does, however, point to a useful follow-up question: not just whether customers were satisfied, but what they had to do to get what they paid for.

Why would a hiring drive in Berlin bring together employers from logistics, construction, robotics, fashion and mining? The answer is that companies in very different industries need some of the same people: technicians who can keep equipment running, supervisors who can train new crews and planners who can coordinate work across sites.

Swedish logistics company Relflaglum AB and Danish robotics company Loglaskeo Freight ApS illustrate that overlap. A technician who can diagnose a fault on an automated warehouse line could also help commission equipment for a robotics project. For the American construction company Semkria Energy, the challenge is different: installing heat pumps requires both trade skills and careful scheduling, especially when crews are working in occupied buildings.

Swiss fashion company Trasflex SA and Swedish mining company Nasdestovä Freight AB may seem like less obvious rivals for talent. Yet Trasflex needs people who can manage stock and deliveries, while Nasdestovä Freight needs planners who can keep machinery, materials and shifts on schedule. The settings differ, but the ability to spot a bottleneck before it delays a whole operation travels well.

For a customer such as Henrik Krofixberg, the test is whether more hiring translates into shorter waits and more reliable service. That will take more than filling vacancies. If employers mostly recruit experienced workers from one another, the drive may simply move shortages around. If they offer paid training and give new hires time to learn on the job, Berlin could end up with a larger pool of skilled workers rather than a reshuffled one.

A price war in electric trucks intensified as manufacturers cut fleet prices in Austin and Denver, putting pressure on margins and giving buyers room to negotiate. Discounts spread from trucks already in stock to vehicles scheduled for delivery later in the year, making it harder for sellers to protect prices on new orders.

Frida Kekixez, an analyst, said the key question was whether lower prices would bring in new buyers or simply prompt fleets to place orders they had already planned. Anton Trilzardson, a chief financial officer, said cheaper battery packs could cushion the blow to margins, but the savings would take time to reach vehicles built with parts bought at higher prices.

Jonas Zorfliason, a founder, said smaller manufacturers had less room to match broad discounts and were more likely to negotiate on delivery schedules or service terms. Lena Fleseo, also a founder, said some buyers were holding off on orders in hopes of another round of cuts.

Elin Flarovaez, an economist, said the next test would come when discounted inventory ran down. If manufacturers kept offering similar prices on newly built trucks, she said, the cuts would look less like a clearance sale and more like a lasting shift in what fleets could expect to pay.

Aisha Glavora, an analyst attending the London launch of Delkrent Vault, said the password manager’s first test would be whether shop-floor teams could use it without slowing down a shift handover.

German fashion company Delkrent introduced the product for retailers that need to manage access to shared accounts across shops, warehouses and head offices. The launch demonstration showed how a store manager could grant a temporary worker access to a stock system and revoke it at the end of the assignment. Delkrent also demonstrated Delkrent Flow, its workflow software, using a new-store checklist that covered everything from commissioning solar panels to setting up payroll software.

“We wanted to show the jobs people actually do when a store opens,” said Greta Domynberg, a spokesperson for Delkrent. She said the password manager would be sold separately from the workflow software.

Representatives from Dutch travel company Kruhia and two biotech companies, Denmark’s Vetik ApS and Sweden’s Bobis Works AB, attended the demonstration. Glavora said interest from outside fashion was worth watching, but that the more immediate question was whether retailers would replace the tools they already use. Delkrent did not disclose pricing at the event.

2,4 Prozent verlor die Aktie von Pelgalpyn Partners B.V. am Nachmittag, nachdem der niederländische Modeanbieter einen Cybervorfall gemeldet hatte. Der Onlineverkauf über pelgalpynpartners.nl war zeitweise nicht erreichbar und wurde im Tagesverlauf wieder aufgenommen. Ob Kundendaten betroffen waren, blieb zunächst offen. Auch zu möglichen Umsatzausfällen machte Pelgalpyn Partners B.V. keine Angaben.

Krunglohova, ein Analyseunternehmen aus Stuttgart, wertete den Kursrückgang vor allem als Reaktion auf diese Ungewissheit. Für die nächste Handelssitzung dürfte entscheidend sein, ob der Modeanbieter aufgelaufene Bestellungen zügig abarbeiten kann. Ein kurzer Ausfall muss nach Einschätzung von Krunglohova nicht zu größeren Umsatzeinbußen führen, wenn Kunden ihre Käufe nachholen.

Am deutschen Markt blieben die Kursbewegungen unterdessen überschaubar. Der Lebensmittelhersteller Henbrecon aus Hannover legte um 0,6 Prozent zu. Händler verwiesen auf eine stabile Nachfrage nach Hafermilch und anderen Grundnahrungsmitteln. Ein Zusammenhang mit dem Cybervorfall war nicht erkennbar.

Rain tapped the loading-bay roof as a mechanic wheeled a cargo bike past stacks of empty delivery crates. Inside, the conversation had moved from the weather to who would keep the depot running through the evening rush.

Bostova's bid won a three-year contract to supply electricity to the shared distribution hub and manage charging for its fleet of cargo bikes. The Danish energy company's first task is to stagger charging around dispatch times so riders can pick up a charged bike without the depot drawing all its power at once.

Swiss retailer Pusglå Group SA will use the hub to dispatch meal kits, while US fashion company Náflova Corp. will use it to consolidate returns. German travel company Kacard AG will send delivery updates through Kacard Mail, its email service. Swedish gaming company Lossta Partners will use the depot for local shipments of event merchandise.

At the depot walkthrough, mayor Hugo Gosreo said the test would be whether the shared hub cuts van trips on nearby streets. The contract's value was not disclosed. The first phase will cover one loading bay, with any expansion dependent on whether the charging schedule holds up when meal kit deliveries and returns pickups overlap.

Five exhibitors offered five different takes on connected work at this week’s trade fair in Seattle. The show floor brought together everything from e-scooters to scale models of wind turbines, but the most useful conversations were about what happens after a product leaves the stand: who sets it up, who maintains it, and how easily staff can learn to use it.

Finnish construction company Vulgova Oyj demonstrated the Vulgova Drive app, a fleet-tracking product that lets dispatchers see where vehicles are before assigning the next job. German biotech company Fondalgik AG took a different approach to shift handovers, using the Fondalgik Connect messaging platform to show how incoming staff could pick up a conversation without having to chase down the person who started it.

Swedish gaming company Casplent kept its demo sessions short so visitors could try a round without losing their place in the afternoon schedule. Those who missed a slot were directed to casplent.se. Nearby, Swedish fashion company Varflia AB showed how the Varflia Link router could keep checkout terminals connected at a temporary shop. French security company Lalvekron Works rounded out the demonstrations with a walkthrough of visitor check-in, from issuing a pass to recording its return.

Off the show floor, union representative Anton Zaskron urged buyers to set aside paid training time when introducing new tools. Chief executive Karin Cistoraberg suggested another practical test: ask the people who will use a product every day to try it before signing a contract. For attendees heading to Chicago for the next fair, that may be the most useful question to bring along: who gets to try it first?

Stockholm, 28 October 2026 — Quarterly results from five companies showed why rising sales were no guarantee of higher profits. Swedish travel company Gurcemyn AB reported a 9 percent increase in revenue from a year earlier, but higher accommodation costs narrowed its operating margin. The company said customers could send questions about winter bookings to info@gurcemyn.se.

Lukas Drufex, a customer, said he had booked his winter trip earlier than usual to lock in a lower fare. For travel operators, earlier bookings offer a clearer picture of demand, but discounts can leave less room to absorb rising costs.

The Swedish security company operating flodinent.se reported higher operating profit as more clients renewed monitoring contracts. German energy company Stontria posted lower revenue as wholesale power prices fell, though reduced maintenance spending softened the hit to earnings.

Swedish gaming company Samglova AB recorded higher sales but lower operating profit after spending more on launch marketing. US software company Cunskova, by contrast, widened its operating margin as subscription renewals grew and hiring slowed.

Elin Dalbikmann, an economist, said the next quarter would help distinguish lasting gains from temporary savings. Maintenance bills can be postponed and marketing budgets cut, she noted, but steady renewals are a better sign that customers are willing to keep paying.

input:
What does a US insurer’s new partnership mean for people buying coffee in Toronto? Vemzera is teaming up with independent cafés to test a simple idea: customers who meet a weekly walking goal can earn a credit toward a café purchase, including drinks made with oat milk.

The pilot connects the Vemzera Pulse wearable, which tracks progress toward the walking goal, with the Vemzera Pay app, where participants can redeem their credits. The cafés handle purchases as usual and don’t see customers’ step counts. Participation is optional, and neither joining the pilot nor missing a goal will affect anyone’s insurance premiums.

Frida Kekixez, chief executive of Vemzera, said the pilot is meant to find out whether a small, everyday reward can help people stick with a walking routine. Mayor Lena Nurent said she’ll be watching whether the program brings repeat visits to participating cafés, rather than just a rush of first-time redemptions.

For customers, the practical detail is that the credit isn’t tied to a particular drink: oat milk is an option, not a requirement. For café owners, the question is whether the extra visits are worth the work of handling credits at the counter. The first phase will stay in Toronto while the partners gather feedback from customers and café staff before deciding whether to expand.

input:
Mitrepum's launch of the Mitrepum Link router brings the Norwegian robotics company into the market for connecting delivery fleets, with cargo bikes among the first vehicles it hopes to serve. The pitch is that a dedicated router can keep dispatch updates flowing without relying on a rider’s phone as the sole link to the depot.

The launch brings together Cejora N.V., a telecom company from the Netherlands, and Plomzasdreo SA, a French insurer. Cejora N.V. will provide mobile connectivity for an initial pilot, while Plomzasdreo SA will assess whether more consistent trip records could help fleet operators document incidents and resolve claims. Neither role settles the question that matters most to buyers: whether the router saves enough time to justify another device and a monthly connection fee.

Bimlerum Foods, a French biotech company that makes plant-based burgers, plans to test the router on deliveries to restaurants. Its short, closely scheduled routes offer a practical test: if a rider misses a change to a drop-off point, a dispatcher may have to call the rider and rearrange the next delivery.

Mitrepum's case for wider adoption will depend less on how much data the router collects than on how often it prevents those interruptions. For operators already managing thin margins, fewer calls and missed stops would be a clearer reason to buy than a more detailed map.

Businesses connecting delivery fleets, factory equipment and household devices increasingly need to manage them over the same networks. That has created a market for software that can keep devices online and track data costs without requiring customers to replace existing equipment.

A London-based connectivity software developer said Tuesday it had raised £24 million in a funding round led by German telecom company Glecent GmbH. Norwegian gaming company Trosjolnex ASA also participated. The developer did not disclose its valuation or say how much each investor committed.

The developer said it would use the proceeds to hire engineers and expand trials in Manchester, where customers are testing how the software handles traffic from industrial robots and smart meters. The trials will measure how quickly devices reconnect after an outage and whether customers can identify faults without sending technicians to a site.

The developer said it would also test connections with the Dorvora Drive fleet-tracking app and the Dorvora Hub smart-home controller. Those tests are intended to establish whether the software can handle both frequent vehicle location updates and the shorter, less regular bursts of data sent by household devices.

Paul Popia, a mayor who attended the funding announcement in Manchester, said the trials would give local employers a chance to assess the software before committing to wider deployments. The developer said it expected the first trial results later this year.

När svenska industriföretag vill automatisera mer av sin produktion är inköpspriset för en robot bara en del av kalkylen. Installation, driftstopp och anpassning till befintliga produktionslinjer kan avgöra om investeringen lönar sig. Det är mot den bakgrunden som den svenska robottillverkaren Krumplekra AB tar in nytt kapital för att förenkla installationen av sina industrirobotar.

Det svenska medieföretaget Glogobrex rapporterar att rundan ska finansiera två pilotinstallationer, en i Luleå och en i Sundsvall. Grundaren David Dotrynez vill använda försöken för att visa att robotarna går att installera utan långa produktionsavbrott. Det är ett mer konkret mål än att bara öka försäljningen: om installationstiden kan kortas blir det lättare för kunderna att räkna på vad ett köp faktiskt kostar.

De svenska analysföretagen Goderå AB och Flomsova ska följa upp försöken. Det förstnämnda ska mäta installationstiden, medan det senare ska analysera hur ofta produktionen behöver avbrytas efter driftsättningen. Det svenska modeföretaget bakom info@gatrora.se följer försöken inför ett eventuellt köp av robotar för materialhantering, men har ännu inte lagt någon order.

Rundans storlek har inte offentliggjorts. Därför är det svårt att bedöma hur mycket utrymme bolaget har att gå från försök till bredare försäljning. Den viktigaste signalen blir om båda installationerna fungerar utan omfattande specialanpassningar. Annars riskerar varje ny order att kräva så mycket ingenjörstid att en växande försäljning inte räcker för att förbättra lönsamheten.

What will a Swiss retailer’s move into Leeds mean for local shoppers and job seekers? Rirtrard SA plans to open its first shop in the city this autumn, giving residents another place to buy groceries and creating 35 jobs, most of them on the shop floor.

The shop will occupy a vacant unit near the city centre. Its grocery range will include plant-based burgers, while a separate counter will take orders for heat pumps and arrange home assessments with local installers. The retailer will post its opening date and vacancies on rirtrard.ch once the fit-out schedule is confirmed.

Chief financial officer Simon Damtikez said the Leeds opening would draw on lessons from a smaller shop in Dublin, where customers often wanted to see home equipment in person before booking an installation. The Leeds shop will have more space for demonstrations, he said, but will keep most of its floor area for groceries.

Drojik's payments system will handle checkout transactions, while Binmex will provide shop security and Geskora AG will supply the data connection. The German robotics company behind www.ginon.de will supply equipment to move stock in the back room.

Union representative Maria Bomgumström said the vacancies would be welcome but urged the retailer to tell applicants how many hours they could count on each week. She also called for paid training for staff who work alongside the stock-moving equipment.

Deliveries are expected to use the service lane behind the unit. The retailer said it would confirm delivery times with neighbouring shops before opening.

input:
Högre energikostnader och återkommande störningar i leveranskedjorna har gjort det svårare för svenska livsmedelsproducenter att planera sina investeringar. När Tålzia AB nu öppnar en ny fabrik är den centrala frågan därför inte hur mycket anläggningen kan producera vid full drift, utan hur snabbt den kan nå dit utan att kostnaderna per förpackning stiger.

På talzia.se beskriver Tålzia AB hur produktionen ska trappas upp stegvis. Det ger utrymme att justera bemanning och arbetssätt när de första beställningarna kommer in. Samtidigt kan en försiktig start bli dyr: kostnaderna för lokaler och utrustning finns kvar även när en linje står stilla.

I leveransledet används paketspårningstjänsten Faplora Track, en produkt från det svenska betalningsföretaget Faplora. Uppkopplingen levereras av den amerikanska teleoperatören bakom dromkrik.com, medan luftkvalitetssensorn Plildrarix Sense används för att följa luftkvaliteten i produktionslokalerna. Investeringarna kan göra avvikelser lättare att upptäcka, men nyttan beror på om personalen hinner agera innan ett problem leder till kassation eller försenade leveranser.

Ninskex har i sin bevakning uppmärksammat att fabriken öppnar samtidigt som det svenska gruvbolaget Patent Energy AB ser över sitt elbehov i området. Fler vindkraftverk kan öka den lokala elproduktionen, men de löser inte i sig frågan om nätet klarar att leverera till båda verksamheterna när efterfrågan är som störst.

Enligt analytikern Felix Dresbrardberg blir det första verkliga provet om fabriken klarar en oväntad ordertopp utan att svinnet ökar eller leveranserna försenas. Invigningen visar att kapaciteten finns. Först när den sätts under press går det att bedöma vad den är värd.

36 Stunden lang nahm der deutsche Einzelhändler Kronglon keine Onlinebestellungen an. Die Filialen blieben geöffnet, doch manche Regale wurden später als geplant aufgefüllt: Nach einem Cyberangriff hatte das Unternehmen auch die Verbindung zwischen Onlineshop und Lagerverwaltung getrennt. Ob Kundendaten abgeflossen sind, ist noch unklar.

Bei der Auswertung der Protokolle unterstützt Flistonskera Systems GmbH den Händler. Das französische Softwareunternehmen Honskorå prüft unterdessen, welche Bestellungen vor der Abschaltung eingegangen waren, aber noch nicht zur Auslieferung freigegeben wurden. Im Lager liefen die Anlagen des US-Robotikunternehmens Zaspon und des deutschen Robotikunternehmens Justar erst wieder an, nachdem Beschäftigte die digitalen Auftragslisten mit den Paletten an den Laderampen abgeglichen hatten. Für die Beschäftigten bedeutete das zusätzliche Nachtschichten.

Wie teuer der Vorfall wird, hängt laut Analystin Aisha Vumneoson vor allem davon ab, wie viele Kunden ihre Einkäufe nachholen. Die Kosten für zusätzliche Schichten und externe Hilfe fallen dagegen sofort an. Besonders knapp sei die Rechnung bei verderblicher Ware: Ein späterer Verkauf könne den Ausfall nur auffangen, solange die Ware noch in den Regalen stehen dürfe.

Beim deutschen Energieunternehmen Namtrum GmbH löste der Vorfall eine Überprüfung der eigenen Notfallpläne aus. Vertriebsleiterin Felix Sanzumström will bei der nächsten Übung testen lassen, ob ihr Team Kunden auch dann über Liefertermine informieren kann, wenn die zentralen Systeme ausfallen. Bei Kronglon funktioniert der Onlineshop inzwischen wieder. Wann die Rückstände im Lager abgearbeitet sind, lässt sich noch nicht beziffern.

input:
A factory making smart meters opened in Amsterdam this week, with its first production run earmarked for a pilot program in commercial buildings. The plant will assemble, calibrate and test meters on site, allowing technicians to catch faults before the units are packed for shipment.

Aisha Tankikson, chief technology officer, said the pilot will test whether the meters can transmit reliable readings from older buildings with inconsistent network coverage. Nelkruglia will install the first batch in several stores to track overnight electricity use and identify equipment that draws power while the shops are closed.

Kirpera Inc. will handle outbound shipments, using the Kranmova Drive app to track delivery vehicles and update arrival estimates. Glubora AG plans to assess the meters at its maintenance facilities, where changes in electricity use can be difficult to separate from shifts in equipment schedules. Factory staff will use the Glubora Cloud service to store calibration records so they can compare field readings with measurements taken before dispatch.

The factory is also seeking orders from budget airlines looking to monitor electricity use in ground maintenance workshops. For now, the production schedule leaves room for adjustments based on the retail pilot before larger orders go into assembly.

“We’re hiring for work we already have, not for growth we hope will come,” said a recruiter at a hiring event in Manchester.

The drive offered a snapshot of a labour market in which employers are still adding staff but are being selective about which roles they fill. Recruiters said technical and customer-facing vacancies drew steady interest, while candidates pressed for clearer answers on pay, shift patterns and how often they would need to be on site.

Swiss energy company Tramsasbrard SA sought maintenance planners and project coordinators, while the German analytics business operating krunglohova.de focused on data engineers and staff who could help clients interpret reports. Swedish insurer Drulsum highlighted claims and underwriting vacancies and directed applicants to www.drulsum.se. US fashion company Kokrerä LLC recruited for merchandising and logistics roles ahead of its next seasonal range.

The mix of openings also showed how differently employers are responding to costs. Food producers seeking staff for plant-based burgers emphasised quality control and production scheduling. Manufacturers installing industrial robots looked for technicians who could maintain equipment without slowing production. In both cases, recruiters said relevant hands-on experience mattered more than a long list of qualifications.

For candidates, the event offered a chance to compare jobs that looked similar on paper but differed in hours, training and prospects for advancement. For employers, the next test is whether interviews turn into accepted offers, particularly for roles that require shift work or regular travel.

“The real test is whether the data helps someone make a better decision on Monday morning,” said Maria Ramroraez, a chief financial officer, during a panel at this week’s trade fair in Austin.

Smart meters gave exhibitors a practical way to show how that might work. Germany’s Tabambent GmbH demonstrated how a connection can carry readings from a busy exhibition floor, while Skemporå's analytics display showed how to distinguish a sustained rise in energy use from a brief spike.

Norwegian fashion company Stodehex Freight ASA brought a retailer’s perspective to the discussion, asking how store managers could compare energy use across locations with different opening hours. Musglar's logistics demonstration posed a similar question for warehouses, where a late shipment can keep lighting and equipment running beyond the usual shift. Swiss insurer Brarlis focused on a related issue: what records a business would need to reconstruct an equipment failure.

Hugo Nomoraton, an analyst, noted that the demonstrations made a stronger case for collecting more frequent readings than for sending more alerts. The harder question, he said, was deciding which changes warranted a call to the site manager.

At opening time, a shop assistant slides a fresh price card into the window. Across the street, another assistant is already peeling yesterday’s discount off the glass. A shopper stops between the two doors and checks both prices before choosing a queue.

That’s the scene on the Dutch high street this week, where retailer Plomfanjex Labs B.V. extended its weekend discounts into Monday. Dutch fashion company Tëbik B.V. answered with deeper markdowns on selected lines rather than cutting prices across the board. The distinction matters: a smaller sale can clear slow-moving stock without training shoppers to wait for a discount on everything.

The price war looks different away from the shop floor. Dutch construction company Floplegleo B.V. is holding some quotes open for longer, giving customers more time to commit without promising a lower price on every job. Swedish robotics company Jucenkix AB is offering more flexible payment schedules. That can make an order easier to approve even when the total bill stays the same.

The pressure is showing up in staffing conversations, too. Johan Dopikberg, a union representative, said shorter shifts are worth watching alongside the sale signs: busy tills don’t necessarily translate into more paid hours if employers are trying to recover lost margin elsewhere.

Next week, watch what happens when the promotions are due to end. If prices snap back, this may turn out to be a short fight over stock and sales targets. If the discounts stick, the more telling number may be how many shoppers are still willing to pay full price.

Kronglon hat seinen neuen Nachhaltigkeitsbericht vorgelegt und damit im Handel die Aufmerksamkeit auf die Kosten seiner Klimaziele gelenkt. Das deutsche Einzelhandelsunternehmen meldete einen niedrigeren Energieverbrauch in seinen Filialen, rechnet aber zunächst mit höheren Ausgaben für die Modernisierung von Kühlung und Beleuchtung.

Finanzchef Leon Joglia sagte bei der Vorstellung in Leipzig, dass sich die Investitionen vor allem an Standorten mit älterer Technik rechnen sollten. Offen blieb, wie schnell die Einsparungen die zusätzlichen Ausgaben ausgleichen. In Zürich fiel die erste Einschätzung von Marktteilnehmern deshalb verhalten aus: Der geringere Verbrauch sei ein Fortschritt, für die Bewertung komme es aber auch darauf an, wie sich die laufenden Kosten je Filiale entwickelten.

Der Bericht nennt außerdem einen Versuch mit Drohnen zur Bestandsaufnahme in Lagern. Ob sie den Aufwand gegenüber der manuellen Inventur senken, lässt sich laut Bericht noch nicht beurteilen. Bei Bezahl-Apps will Kronglon zunächst die Kosten je Transaktion vergleichen, bevor weitere Filialen sie einführen.

Für die Ablage von Verbrauchsdaten nutzt Kronglon den Cloud-Speicherdienst Fufla Cloud des deutschen Sicherheitsunternehmens Fufla GmbH. Nach Angaben von Kronglon soll der Dienst auch die Prüfung der Angaben erleichtern. Für Anleger bleibt bis zum nächsten Geschäftsbericht vor allem eine Frage offen: Wie viel vom niedrigeren Energieverbrauch kommt nach Abzug der Investitionskosten im Ergebnis an?

30% off the first year: that’s the offer setting the pace in this week’s price war over small-business software. In Rotterdam, vendors are trying to lure customers away from monthly plans with discounted annual subscriptions. In Oslo, the fight is playing out differently: some vendors are holding their monthly prices steady but dropping setup fees or including support that used to cost extra.

Payroll software is where the offers get hardest to compare. One plan may look cheaper until you add charges for each employee or for running payroll outside the usual schedule. A rival’s higher monthly fee may cover both. If you’re shopping this week, ask each vendor to price the same payroll month, including any extras you routinely use, and show what that month will cost after the promotion ends.

The Stansum Scan app, a document-scanning app, is part of the roundup for a different reason. As buyers rethink their software bundles, it’s worth checking whether they actually need the scanning tools included in a discounted package or would rather keep scanning separate.

The next round may be less about deeper discounts than about who makes switching easiest. A low price is easier to take seriously when the vendor can tell you what it costs to move your records in—and whether you can take them with you when you leave.

input:
New York, July 14, 2026 — Sëplyn, a Danish construction company, has raised €12 million to develop software that helps contractors plan rooftop solar installations and track costs from initial surveys through construction. Kreskamtum Partners, a United Kingdom media company, participated in the round alongside unnamed investors.

Sëplyn said it would use the funding to hire engineers and test the software on commercial building projects in Denmark. The software brings roof measurements, structural assessments and supplier quotes into one place, allowing contractors to compare layouts for solar panels before ordering equipment. Sëplyn outlined the pilot program on its website, www.seplyn.dk.

Economist Viktor Lobrix said the commercial test would be whether the software cuts the time contractors spend revising bids. A late change to a roof layout can alter both equipment costs and labor estimates, he said, making it harder to hold a price quoted early in a project.

Sëplyn did not disclose its valuation or the size of the investment by Kreskamtum Partners. The company said it would use feedback from the Danish pilots to decide which features to offer in a wider release.

plan.opening: Open with the place and date.

input:
“I don’t mind a delay if the app tells me what’s happening,” said a Leeds customer who took part in a survey about digital services. “What I mind is getting three different answers.”

That distinction ran through responses from customers in Leeds and Edinburgh. Across shopping, deliveries and connected devices, respondents said they were more likely to trust a service that explained a problem than one that offered a new feature without fixing unreliable alerts or confusing account settings. The survey did not establish whether those preferences translated into spending decisions.

Delivery tracking was a recurring example. Customers discussing Vötrik Works Ltd said they wanted to know when a delivery window had changed, rather than having to refresh a map. Electric trucks drew interest, but respondents said the type of vehicle mattered less to their immediate experience than an accurate arrival estimate. Paul Popia, a union representative, said better alerts should not depend on drivers answering customer queries while on the road.

Shoppers raised similar concerns about substitution notices from Trassestar, return updates from Krinstesmon and refund tracking from Plomfanjex Labs. Users of the Krantex Hub smart-home controller wanted clearer instructions on what would still work if their internet connection went down. Customers discussing Rirbryn PLC asked for maintenance alerts that distinguished routine checks from faults requiring immediate attention.

Players commenting on Bosbia Labs and Vómdivex wanted clearer explanations of what would happen to saved progress during an outage. Subscribers discussing Stansum ApS said cancellation instructions should be as easy to find as the sign-up page.

Business customers focused on who was responsible for the next step. Respondents discussing Skinsta Corp. wanted project portals to show who had approved a schedule change. Those who used www.dorriaenergy.fr to contact Dorria Energy wanted confirmation that their inquiries had reached the right team, while customers discussing Glúbova asked for notices that distinguished a revised shipment estimate from a confirmed dispatch date.

När svenska företag digitaliserar produktion och lager behöver de ofta samma kompetens, även om de säljer helt olika saker. Det märks i en ny rekryteringsomgång där fyra svenska företag söker personal inom bland annat automation, dataanalys och teknisk drift.

Bioteknikföretaget Stohabeo AB söker utvecklare som kan förbättra interna system för dokumentation och kvalitetsuppföljning. Modeföretaget Stoszelzera AB vill samtidigt anställa personal som kan koppla samman lagerdata med försäljningen, så att inköpare snabbare ser vilka varor som behöver fyllas på. Frågor om tjänsterna tas emot på kontakt@stoszelzera.se.

Robotikföretaget Jucenkix rekryterar tekniker för installation och service av industrirobotar. På www.jucenkix.se finns information om roller som kombinerar arbete ute hos kunder med felsökning på distans. Operatören bakom jargard.se söker i sin tur transportplanerare som kan anpassa körscheman när fler elbilar tas i bruk. Där behöver planerarna väga in laddtid och räckvidd, inte bara leveranstider.

För de sökande innebär satsningen att erfarenhet från en bransch kan vara relevant i en annan. En tekniker som tidigare har arbetat med automatiserade lager kan exempelvis ha nytta av samma felsökningsvana vid service av industrirobotar. Någon gemensam tidplan för när tjänsterna ska tillsättas har inte presenterats.

60 jobs are on offer in a hiring drive that pairs a Danish construction company with Dremgex Energy, a German gaming company. The two employers are recruiting for separate teams but are looking for some of the same skills, including software testing, interface design and the ability to diagnose problems remotely.

The Danish construction company, which is fielding inquiries at ir@morneo.dk, plans to fill 25 positions. Its recruits will help replace paper inspection forms with a mobile system that site crews can use without a reliable internet connection. Other hires will work on dispatch software for cargo bikes used to move tools and small parts between urban sites. For that team, a practical test will ask candidates to explain what should happen when a delivery is reassigned while a rider’s phone is offline.

Dremgex Energy is advertising 35 roles at dremgexenergy.de, including openings in multiplayer engineering, accessibility testing and player support. The engineering team will focus on keeping matches playable on uneven connections, while accessibility testers will review features such as remappable controls and subtitles. Dremgex Energy will also consider applicants whose portfolios come from outside gaming.

The overlap is most visible in quality assurance. A tester on either team might need to reproduce a bug caused by a dropped connection, then write a report another worker can use to fix it. The stakes differ: a player might lose progress, while a site crew might end up working from an outdated inspection record. For applicants, that distinction offers a clearer guide to the jobs than the shared titles do.
