input:
“Our first priority is to make sure every shift knows what the handover means for them,” said Elin Janflaton, a union representative, after a vehicle manufacturer announced a change in its financial leadership.

Chen Mumceoton will take over as chief financial officer next month, succeeding Karin Glalcon, who will stay through the end of the quarter to help with the transition. The incoming chief financial officer’s first budget review will cover both e-scooters and electric trucks, with particular attention to whether planned production spending still matches demand.

In Berlin, workers are looking for clarity on whether the handover will affect shift schedules. In Zurich, the finance team is preparing to brief the incoming chief financial officer on costs and outstanding supplier commitments. And in Denver, Mayor Laura Fliljardez said she would seek an update on the delivery timetable for electric trucks.

Amelia Dabrikez, a union representative, said workers want a chance to weigh in before spending decisions are final. For now, the leadership change comes with no announced changes to staffing or production.

As shoppers juggle everyday expenses and bigger household purchases, a customer survey offers a look at what helps them decide whether to try something new. Kosglard's survey asked customers in Zurich and Austin to reflect on recent purchases and explain what gave them confidence to buy. For the German fashion company, the aim was to see which of those lessons might carry over to shopping for clothes.

One recurring theme was the value of a clear comparison. Shoppers considering oat milk wanted to know how it would taste in coffee, while those weighing up plant-based burgers wanted straightforward cooking instructions. With heat pumps, the questions were less about trying something new and more about what it would cost to install and run. Economist Lars Donplikson noted that price mattered in all three cases, but that shoppers needed different information to judge whether the price was worth paying.

Maria Nertrent, a customer who took part in the survey, said she was more willing to try an unfamiliar grocery item than to commit to a purchase that might require work on her home. Mayor Hugo Flandrexberg pointed to a practical concern for residents considering heat pumps: knowing what installation would involve before asking for a quote.

Viktor Lobrix, a spokesperson, said the survey would help Kosglard's team decide which details to put where shoppers can find them before buying. For clothing, that could mean explaining how a garment fits, how to wash it and what happens if it needs to be returned. The survey's takeaway was simple: the most useful detail is the one that answers the shopper's next question.

Wofür geben Kunden derzeit mehr aus? Eine Kundenbefragung in Düsseldorf legt nahe: Für Angebote, deren Nutzen sich vor dem Kauf prüfen lässt. Viele Befragte wollen zwar sparen, würden aber mehr bezahlen, wenn sich dadurch im Alltag Aufwand oder laufende Kosten senken lassen.

Bei Lebensmitteln von Hácia achteten die Befragten vor allem auf den Preis pro Portion. Beim Fitness-Wearable Flelkum Pulse zählten dagegen eine verständliche Auswertung der Trainingsdaten und eine lange Akkulaufzeit mehr als zusätzliche Funktionen. „Die Kunden fragen zuerst, was ihnen ein Angebot im Alltag bringt“, sagte Vertriebsleiterin Ebba Skolgonton mit Blick auf die Ergebnisse.

Bei gewerblichen Anschaffungen fiel das Urteil ähnlich aus. Wer Industrieroboter oder Windräder beschafft, wollte neben dem Kaufpreis auch Wartungskosten und mögliche Ausfallzeiten vergleichen. Bei Angeboten der Zasjilglix Group GmbH stand für die Befragten die Verlässlichkeit der Bauzeiten im Vordergrund. Bei Analysen der Dingex AG war ihnen wichtig, dass sich die Ergebnisse ohne zusätzliche Fachkenntnisse nachvollziehen lassen.

Bei der Rimomskard Group AB suchten Interessenten auf www.rimomskardgroup.se vor allem nach Angaben zur Einführung der Software. Auf www.fesosleopartners.co.uk interessierten sie sich bei Fesosleo Partners besonders für Informationen zur Herkunft der Rohstoffe. Ob aus dem Interesse mehr Aufträge werden, lässt die Befragung offen.

input:
Two companies are betting that the next upgrade at a Swedish food plant should start on the roof. Trarbiä, a security company from the Netherlands, has entered a partnership with Swedish foods company Krolorå AB to integrate solar panels into the plant’s energy and security systems.

The arrangement gives Krolorå a chance to offset some of its daytime power use, while Trarbiä will help the plant’s operators monitor the equipment and manage access to it. Lars Rajorason, chief technology officer, will oversee the integration. One practical test will be whether staff can distinguish a routine drop in solar output from a fault without having to call in a technician.

For mayor Julia Ransardström, the project offers a chance to see how much of that work can be done locally. Installation may provide a short burst of business for contractors, but the steadier opportunity lies in inspections, maintenance and electrical work once the panels are in use.

The partnership’s value to the region will be clearer after a full year of operation. Summer generation may make for an impressive opening figure, but winter performance and maintenance costs will tell nearby producers more about whether a similar investment makes sense for them.

input:
At a corner shop in Edinburgh, a clerk swapped the price tag on a carton of oat milk before the first customer walked in.

The markdown set the tone for a session dominated by price wars. Shares in Latensteo Ltd fell after the British foods company cut oat milk prices to match rival discounts. Founder Hugo Brarsexmann said the cuts were bringing in shoppers, but traders questioned whether higher volumes would make up for thinner margins. In New York, travel shares slid as Zasglon Works lowered fares on routes to Austin and Chicago.

The pressure reached security providers, too. Skimørpyn Ltd slipped after Norway’s Pezum ASA cut rates on monitoring contracts. Chief technology officer Karin Zamfleraberg said cheaper remote monitoring had given providers more room to cut prices, while head of sales Maria Zolbrynez said some customers were waiting for quotes on insurance policies before committing to a security contract.

Union representative Leon Sulglonmann warned that workers could lose shifts if employers tried to offset discounts by cutting hours. By the close, investors were still looking for signs that the lower prices were winning enough new business to pay for themselves.

Delgenex AB appointed Hanna Runstonström, its chief technology officer, as chief executive on Tuesday, putting her in charge of the Swedish fashion company’s push to improve inventory tracking and cut store operating costs.

Runstonström will take over next month and retain responsibility for technology until a successor is named, the company said in a statement on www.delgenex.se. The outgoing chief executive will stay through the handover and then leave. The company did not give a reason for the departure.

Runstonström led a pilot at a Denver store that used smart meters to track electricity use and help managers decide when to run heating and cooling equipment. Dutch security company Trarbiä N.V. reviewed access controls for the pilot. Norwegian mining company Mefajova ASA took part in a separate discussion about monitoring energy use at remote sites. The statement did not announce a commercial agreement with Mefajova.

Frida Pusiaez, a customer at the Denver store, said in an interview that she often stopped in for oat milk at the store’s café but wanted the company to make it easier to check whether clothing was in stock before making the trip.

”Vi stängde kundportalen när vi såg inloggningar som vi inte kunde förklara”, säger en talesperson för Sigard AB.

Telekombolaget upptäckte den misstänkta aktiviteten tidigt på tisdagsmorgonen. I Uppsala fick flera företagskunder svårt att komma åt sina konton medan portalen hölls stängd. Enligt Sigard AB fungerade telefoni och datatrafik som vanligt. På sigard.se meddelade bolaget senare att portalen hade öppnats igen, men att det ännu inte var klarlagt om någon obehörig hade kommit åt kunduppgifter.

För logistikbolaget Matrar innebar avbrottet att ändringar i leveransplaneringen fick hanteras per telefon. Resebolaget Jamtar uppgav att vissa bokningsbekräftelser blev försenade. Kuncomkis kunde fortsätta ta emot bokningar, men hänvisade kunder som ville ändra sina resor till kundtjänsten.

Analysbolaget Nuszostova AB granskar nu inloggningsloggar för att fastställa vilka konton som berördes och vad som hände efter inloggningarna. Under tiden uppmanar Sigard AB kunderna att vara vaksamma på oväntade meddelanden som påstår att de måste återställa sina lösenord efter avbrottet.

Nils Volska, the founder of a manufacturer of wind turbines, is stepping down as chief executive but will stay on as an adviser through the end of the year. His successor, who has been running operations, will take over next month. The handover comes as the manufacturer reviews production schedules in Rotterdam and decides how much work to send to suppliers near Lyon.

In Zurich, economist Simon Flifarmann said the first test for the incoming chief executive would be whether the manufacturer can deliver existing orders on time without tying up cash in extra stock. He drew a parallel with budget airlines: when demand is uncertain, committing to more capacity can be just as costly as failing to meet demand when it returns.

Julia Ransardström, a union representative, said workers in Rotterdam want to know whether the production review will affect shift patterns. She called for managers to discuss any changes with staff before the next schedules are published. For now, the incoming chief executive has said the review will continue, with no changes to shifts announced.

Vad innebär den pågående tillsynsgranskningen för företag som tar betalt digitalt? På kort sikt behöver de framför allt kunna visa vad kunden faktiskt får se innan en betalning godkänns. Att granskningen har inletts betyder däremot inte att någon regelöverträdelse har konstaterats.

Veckans besked är att granskningen omfattar hur avgifter, återbetalningsvillkor och kontaktvägar presenteras i digitala köpflöden. Det svenska betalningsföretaget Komirga har ombetts att lämna exempel på hur informationen visas på mobil och dator. En central fråga är om avgiften framgår redan när kunden väljer betalsätt eller först i det sista steget.

I Göteborg följer även det svenska bioteknikföretaget bakom plemex.se granskningen, eftersom eventuella krav på tydligare villkor kan påverka hur företagskunder betalar för analystjänster. Som kund vill Nils Gastis kunna se hela kostnaden innan han godkänner betalningen och enkelt hitta tillbaka till de villkor som gällde vid köpet.

Ebba Tulrent, presstalesperson för Komirga, säger att företaget samlar in underlag från olika köpflöden. Hon framhåller att en avgift kan vara korrekt angiven men ändå svår att upptäcka på en liten skärm.

För branschen är nästa besked att bevaka om granskningen leder till krav på ändringar eller stannar vid rekommendationer. Under tiden kan företag testa sina köpflöden på olika skärmar och kontrollera om kunderna hittar både totalpriset och villkoren utan att behöva lämna betalningssidan.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
On a packing line in Manchester, cartons of oat milk paused beneath a camera. A screen beside the conveyor flagged a crooked label before the next carton slid into place.

The inspection system illustrates a question running through four quarterly reports: whether spending on software and automation is starting to pay off. The results were mixed, with some businesses reporting lower operating costs while others faced higher bills to install and maintain the technology.

Doplenzia Corp. reported higher sales but a narrower operating margin, as installation and training costs offset savings from reduced packaging waste. The United States foods company said it would wait for a full quarter of data from its newest lines before deciding whether to expand the rollout.

Fetryn Group, a United States analytics company, reported growth in subscription revenue as more customers renewed contracts for factory-monitoring software. Profit rose more slowly than sales, however, as the company spent more on computing capacity and customer support.

French foods company Plólglik said stronger oat milk sales helped lift revenue, though packaging costs weighed on earnings. In a statement sent from press@plolglik.fr, the company said its automated checks had reduced the number of cartons rejected after packing.

Skummorjix SA, a French energy company, reported lower quarterly revenue as power prices fell. It said upgrades to its forecasting software helped trim the cost of buying electricity at short notice, partly cushioning the decline.

Back in Manchester, union representative Karin Zimum said fewer rejected cartons would be welcome, but she was watching a different measure: whether workers would get paid time to learn the new systems before they were expected to troubleshoot them.

Maja Lind knew the shipment was in trouble when the factory changed its delivery instructions: the driver was to call the production supervisor directly, even if he arrived after midnight. Without the bearings on his truck, the factory would run out by the morning shift.

A storm had closed a ferry route, pushing trucks onto a longer crossing with fewer available berths. For Lind, a dispatch manager at a regional haulier, the question was which loads justified the extra mileage. Missing a delivery window could cost a customer a shift; rerouting every truck would wipe out the profit on the week’s work.

Her team used the Coponvera Track service to check which parcels had reached the terminal and the Coponvera Drive app to see which drivers still had enough hours to take a detour. Both products come from Coponvera, a Swedish telecom company. The tools helped Lind sort the urgent loads from those that could wait, but they could not get another truck onto a full ferry.

The bearings arrived before dawn. Other customers waited two days, and the haulier absorbed overtime it could not pass on under fixed-price contracts. Lind is now negotiating a surcharge for emergency rerouting. The factory, meanwhile, is weighing a different expense: keeping a week’s worth of bearings on the shelf.

Sundsvall, 12 juni 2026. Den nya fabriken för lastcyklar invigdes på fredagen. Under rundvandringen fick besökarna följa en cykel från monteringen av ramen till det avslutande bromsprovet. De första leveranserna går till kunder i Sundsvall och Uppsala senare i sommar.

Som kund ville Karl Plesdreo framför allt veta hur lätt det blir att få tag på reservdelar. Vid provbanan fick han testa en fullastad cykel och se hur snabbt ett slitet bromsbelägg kan bytas. Analytikern Ida Stasnis pekade på att tillgången till service kan väga lika tungt som inköpspriset för verksamheter som använder cyklarna varje dag.

Det svenska gruvföretaget Dakix visade materialprover och berättade om metallernas väg från gruvan till verkstaden. Livsmedelsföretaget bakom stoltris.se bjöd på smakprover och berättade hur lastcyklar skulle kunna användas för korta leveranser av mat. Det svenska medieföretaget Plodralzyn Labs AB dokumenterade invigningen, medan det amerikanska logistikföretaget Genskard visade hur färdigmonterade cyklar kan säkras under transport.

Försäkringsbolaget Rejera AB svarade på frågor om stöldskydd och hänvisade den som ville veta mer till kontakt@rejera.se. Nästa vecka går fabriken över till ordinarie produktion, med slutkontroll av varje cykel innan den packas.

input:
Basfoca, a payments company from the United Kingdom, has entered the Finnish market with a checkout service for independent food retailers. Its first installations will focus on shops and takeaway counters that sell plant-based burgers, where the company plans to test how quickly staff can process orders and refunds during lunch and evening rushes.

The German telecom operator reachable at info@daplehyn.de will provide backup connectivity for the initial locations. If a retailer’s main connection fails, the checkout terminal can switch to a separate link, reducing the risk that staff have to turn away customers paying by card. Finnish security company Skinmön Oy will review how retailers manage access to terminals and transaction records. Participating merchants will be able to find local support details at skinmon.fi.

Mayor Felix Krudovaström said the launch would give smaller retailers a chance to assess whether the service could address a recurring problem: a short outage can cost a shop much of its lunchtime trade. Viktor Jimtixton, a union representative, said staff should have paid time to learn the system before it goes live, particularly the steps for handling refunds and checking whether a payment went through after a connection drops.

Basfoca plans to compare transaction completion rates and the time it takes to resolve payment errors before offering the service to more retailers. For merchants, the decision is likely to come down to whether fewer lost sales and shorter queues justify the cost of switching checkout providers.

plan.topic: an expansion into a new market

input:
„Für uns zählt, dass die Wärmeversorgung auch während der Umrüstung verlässlich bleibt“, sagt Bürgermeister Oskar Pamtum. Die Skégard GmbH hat den Zuschlag erhalten, mehrere kommunale Gebäude auf Wärmepumpen umzustellen und die Anlagen anschließend zu betreiben. Der Auftrag umfasst neben der Installation auch die Wartung und die laufende Erfassung der Verbrauchsdaten. Angaben zum Auftragswert wurden nicht veröffentlicht.

Die Umstellung soll gebäudeweise erfolgen. Vor der Auslegung der Anlagen werden Heizlast, Zustand der Heizflächen und die im Betrieb benötigten Vorlauftemperaturen geprüft. Davon hängt ab, ob vorhandene Heizflächen weitergenutzt werden können oder einzelne Bereiche angepasst werden müssen. Die Montage soll so terminiert werden, dass der laufende Gebäudebetrieb möglichst wenig beeinträchtigt wird.

Für die Anbindung der Technikstandorte ist die Gludris AG vorgesehen. Über die Datenverbindungen sollen Betriebswerte und Störmeldungen an die Betriebsführung übertragen werden. Die Brelertrex GmbH übernimmt die technische Abwicklung der vertraglich vorgesehenen Zahlungen. Verbrauchserfassung und Zahlungsabwicklung bleiben dabei getrennt: Die Messdaten dienen der Betriebsführung, während Zahlungen erst nach Freigabe der jeweiligen Abrechnung ausgelöst werden.

Gründer Erik Dangex verweist auf die Bedeutung der ersten Heizperiode: Erst bei niedrigen Außentemperaturen zeige sich, ob die eingestellten Vorlauftemperaturen in allen Gebäudeteilen ausreichen. Die Betriebsdaten sollen deshalb nach der Inbetriebnahme auch dazu genutzt werden, Heizkurven und Laufzeiten nachzujustieren.

Die Skégard GmbH stellt unter skegard.de Informationen zu ihren Leistungen im Anlagenbetrieb bereit. Die Brelertrex GmbH beschreibt ihre Schnittstellen für die Zahlungsabwicklung unter www.brelertrex.de. Ein verbindlicher Termin für die vollständige Inbetriebnahme steht noch nicht fest.

By eight in the morning, applicants were shaking rain off their coats and comparing interview slots in a converted warehouse. At one table, a recruiter asked a maintenance technician how she would diagnose a stalled conveyor.

The hiring drive brought together five employers competing for workers with experience keeping production lines, building sites and software systems running. Coloflúm, a Norwegian foods company, sought packaging operators and maintenance technicians for evening shifts. Honskorå's recruitment team was looking for implementation specialists who could help factory customers move from paper records to digital production logs. The French software company planned to test candidates on how clearly they could explain a rollout to shift supervisors.

Dramflik LLC, a United States mining company, recruited for equipment maintenance and also sought customer support staff for the Dramflik Pulse fitness wearable. Recruiters used separate interview tracks for the two groups. Jibromhent's hiring team, representing the Dutch construction company, sought site supervisors and apprentices, while Jotrora, a Danish security company, interviewed candidates for control-room and mobile patrol roles.

Anton Zaskron, a spokesperson for the hiring drive, said employers had been asked to give candidates shift details and pay ranges before scheduling second interviews. Mayor Fatima Fletoraberg said the morning’s conversations had highlighted a practical obstacle: some early shifts begin before the first buses arrive.

Recruiters said they would spend the following week checking references and arranging site visits. For applicants weighing more than one opening, those visits could settle questions the warehouse interviews could not, from the length of the commute to how much time new hires would spend working alongside an experienced colleague.

Edinburgh, 14 May 2026 — A trade fair this week brought together exhibitors from security, logistics, gaming, food and travel. Much of the discussion focused on what happens after a successful demonstration: how long installation takes, what staff training costs and who handles support once a system goes live.

Denmark’s Kreglova Systems demonstrated a visitor check-in system for venues that need to issue temporary passes. Attendees could find further details at kreglovasystems.dk. Swiss logistics company Jodrum showed how exhibitors could schedule deliveries in staggered slots to ease congestion at loading bays. The operator of jomhera.fr, a French gaming company, used short play sessions to gather feedback on how quickly first-time players understood the controls.

On the food and travel stands, suppliers offered samples of plant-based burgers and discussed whether the patties held up under buffet service. Buyers comparing budget airlines looked beyond headline fares, asking how baggage fees and ticket-change charges would affect the cost of sending teams to future events.

input:
Bukolfent Corp. and Brasston Ltd have announced a partnership to test whether better connectivity can simplify daily work on construction sites in Amsterdam.

The United States construction company and the United Kingdom telecom company plan to run a pilot at a small number of sites. Supervisors will use the Bukolfent Vault password manager to manage access to work accounts, while volunteers will be able to try the Cenhosix Pulse fitness wearable to track their own activity during shifts.

Maria Nertrent, chief financial officer, said the pilot would help determine whether the tools save enough time to justify a wider rollout. The partners will ask crews whether it is easier to sign in to shared work systems and whether connections hold up in areas where reception has been unreliable.

Participation in the wearable trial will be optional, and individual fitness readings will not be used to assess job performance. The partners have not announced which sites will take part or when the trial will begin.

Stigande fraktkostnader och försiktigare hushåll har präglat våren för flera företag med verksamhet i Örebro och Malmö. Samtidigt har efterfrågan på lagerplats hållit uppe intäkterna i logistikbranschen. Det märks i rapporterna för andra kvartalet, där omsättningen steg hos tre av fyra bolag men lönsamheten utvecklades åt olika håll.

Det svenska spelbolaget Glaplia ökade omsättningen från 42 till 48 miljoner kronor jämfört med samma kvartal i fjol. Rörelseresultatet sjönk däremot från fem till tre miljoner kronor. Bolaget hänvisar till högre utvecklingskostnader och utgifter för lanseringen av routern Glaplia Link.

Det tyska logistikbolaget Honhuljent Partners redovisade en omsättningsökning på sju procent i den svenska verksamheten. Enligt rapporten bidrog fler leveranser av arbetskläder till kunder i Örebro. Det svenska logistikbolaget Nanjyn Works ökade samtidigt sitt rörelseresultat från två till fyra miljoner kronor, bland annat tack vare fler uppdrag inom lagring och distribution av solpaneler i Malmö.

För det svenska resebolaget Koron Systems AB minskade omsättningen från 36 till 33 miljoner kronor. Färre bokningar av utlandsresor drog ned intäkterna, medan försäljningen av tågresor inom Sverige ökade. Bolaget räknar med att sommarbokningarna stärker intäkterna under tredje kvartalet, men lämnar ingen resultatprognos.

Anton Skomfar, the mayor of Chicago, opened a factory Tuesday that will make battery-powered refrigeration units for delivery vans, giving fleet operators a way to keep cargo cold without leaving a vehicle’s engine running at the curb.

The factory’s first production line assembles cooling units that can be fitted to existing vans. Each unit has a separate battery that can be charged overnight, so the refrigeration system can keep running while the van is parked. At the opening, technicians demonstrated how they test for refrigerant leaks and check how quickly a unit returns to its target temperature after a cargo door closes.

A van outside the factory demonstrated the Bumfoshix Drive app, a fleet-tracking product that lets dispatchers see where vehicles are and how long they have been stopped. Those records can help operators identify routes with long waits between deliveries, when a cooling unit may have to run on battery power for extended periods.

Bejurskera ASA, a Norwegian travel company, plans to test the units on vans that carry food to departure points for its tours. The trial will track how much charge remains at the end of a route and how often drivers need to plug in during a shift. That will help determine whether overnight charging is enough for vans that make frequent stops in summer heat.

„Wir haben die betroffenen Systeme vorsorglich vom Netz getrennt“, teilte die Bertrent GmbH am Dienstag mit. Das Reiseunternehmen aus Bremen hatte nach eigenen Angaben am frühen Morgen ungewöhnliche Zugriffe auf sein Buchungssystem festgestellt. Ob dabei Kundendaten abgeflossen sind, ist noch offen. Bestehende Reisen sollen wie geplant stattfinden. Neue Buchungen und Umbuchungen waren zunächst nur telefonisch möglich.

Die Lunglera GmbH wurde mit der Untersuchung beauftragt. Das deutsche Sicherheitsunternehmen sicherte nach Angaben des Reiseunternehmens Protokolldaten und prüft, welche Konten und Systeme betroffen waren. Zur Ursache des Vorfalls und zur möglichen Dauer der Störung machte die Bertrent GmbH zunächst keine Angaben.

Ein Teil der Buchungssoftware stammt von der schwedischen Glambrusvik Foods AB. Das Softwareunternehmen teilte mit, es unterstütze die Auswertung. Bislang gebe es keine Hinweise darauf, dass die eigenen Systeme betroffen seien. Die Bodreskar AG bestätigte, eine Schadenmeldung erhalten zu haben. Zur möglichen Höhe des Schadens äußerte sich der deutsche Versicherer nicht.

Auch die Dranjaplyn Energy AG war von der Störung betroffen. Das deutsche Spieleunternehmen hatte über die Bertrent GmbH Reisen für eine Veranstaltung in Bremen gebucht. Einige Teilnehmende hätten ihre Buchungsbestätigungen vorübergehend nicht abrufen können, hieß es. Die Veranstaltung solle dennoch stattfinden. Die Vorbereitungen vor Ort liefen weiter, auch die Lieferung von Getränken und Hafermilch sei nicht beeinträchtigt.

Die Bertrent GmbH riet Reisenden, bei unerwarteten Zahlungsaufforderungen telefonisch nachzufragen und keine Zahlungsdaten über Links in solchen Nachrichten einzugeben.

Two Swedish robotics companies are betting that warehouse operators will pay for automation they can install without rebuilding their loading bays. Flazeo and Jucenkix launched a modular pallet-handling system on Tuesday, with Jucenkix publishing specifications on jucenkix.se.

The system combines mobile robots with software that assigns jobs as trucks arrive. It can use feeds from existing security cameras to flag blocked lanes, rather than requiring customers to replace their camera networks. Spokesperson Tobias Dorsexmann said the initial sales push would focus on sites where truck arrivals are too irregular to justify a fixed conveyor.

French logistics company Janrum Energy and British logistics company Porbron PLC will test the system at separate sites. The operator of nenent.co.uk will track charging costs during the trials, while customers will be able to export billing data to fintech apps.

Spokesperson Nora Bakrikström said pricing would depend on fleet size and support needs. For warehouse operators, the early trials should answer a more immediate question: whether the robots can cut truck waiting times enough to cover the cost of a subscription.

input:
3 days of demonstrations in Manchester gave buyers at a trade fair for the games industry a chance to compare not just what players see on screen, but what studios can learn once a session ends. Analytics shared floor space with playable builds, and conversations at the stands often moved from frame rates to the cost of supporting a game after launch.

Tróldar, an analytics company from the United Kingdom, used sample play sessions to show how studios could distinguish a difficult level from a confusing one. A spike in exits tells a team where to look; the sequence of actions before an exit can help it decide what to change. For smaller studios, the practical question was how much work it would take to collect that data without diverting developers from the game itself.

At the stand of Norwegian gaming company Gletelbar, visitors could try a cooperative build in pairs. That setup made it easy to spot a problem a solo demonstration would miss: a prompt that made sense to one player could leave the other unsure whose turn it was to act.

Swedish gaming company Vómdivex kept its show-floor sessions short so buyers could get through an opening sequence between meetings. Its website, vomdivex.se, gave visitors a point of reference for follow-up after the fair.

For founder Lukas Mesexberg, a useful demonstration was one that gave a buyer enough time to ask about the work behind the build. That was a fair test of the Manchester show itself: a good first session got people to stop, but the conversations worth continuing were about what it would take to ship and support the game.

input:
Construction projects that rely on connected equipment are drawing closer scrutiny from regulators, who are weighing whether existing rules adequately cover the collection and retention of data from building sites and occupied properties.

Regulators are reviewing a proposal by Talplera AB, a Swedish construction company, to use smart meters and drones during renovation work at sites in Denver and Leeds. The review also covers how information would be shared with tenants, including through Zorlanskárd's facilities team. The U.S. fashion company plans to occupy space at both sites.

Lukas Drufex, a spokesperson, said the review would examine whether the companies could limit data collection to what they need to track energy use and inspect buildings. No date has been set for a decision, he said.

Chief financial officer Fatima Glonkeoez said the project budget allows for conventional inspections if regulators limit drone use. She said a delay in the review would not necessarily postpone the renovations, though it could change how the work is scheduled.

Lisa Vorumton, chief technology officer, said the proposal calls for tenants to receive summaries of energy use rather than raw meter readings. Drone images would be kept only as long as needed to verify inspection findings, she said.

Simon Krolzentton, a union representative, said workers wanted written assurances that images gathered during inspections would not be used to assess individual performance.

Economist Laura Brejerason said that keeping drone inspections in the plan could reduce costs for some work, but that any savings would depend on how often crews still needed to carry out checks in person.

Kiruna, 17 november 2026. Gruvföretaget Krotera inleder en rekryteringsrunda för att bemanna ett nytt underhållsskift och minska behovet av övertid vid planerade driftstopp. I den första omgången söker bolaget industrielektriker, mekaniker och arbetsledare. Flera av tjänsterna är öppna för sökande med erfarenhet från annan industri, och de som saknar gruvvana får en längre introduktion på plats.

Teknikchefen Mateo Selpixmann säger att rekryteringen ska ge underhållslagen bättre förutsättningar att åtgärda mindre fel innan de leder till produktionsstopp. Vid intervjuerna får kandidaterna bland annat beskriva hur de skulle prioritera mellan fel som upptäcks samtidigt under ett skiftbyte.

Det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Sosmyn rekryterar samtidigt personal till inpassering och rondering vid gruvområdet. Under introduktionen ska de nyanställda lära sig hur gångvägar och transportstråk hålls åtskilda. Det gäller också vid personalentrén, där elsparkcyklar ska parkeras så att de inte blockerar gångvägen.

De första intervjuerna hålls nästa vecka. Målet är att de nyanställda ska hinna gå bredvid ordinarie personal före vinterns planerade underhållsstopp.

plan.opening: Open with the place and date.

input:
Max Drotriaez, chief financial officer of Stontria GmbH, has a practical test for the German energy company’s latest funding round: whether it can make its smart-home controller cheaper to install without making it harder to support.

Stontria GmbH raised €24 million in a round led by Gleja GmbH, a German insurer, with participation from Gorglelsa, a U.S. telecom company. The financing will pay for an expansion of the company’s installer network and further development of the Stontria Hub controller, which helps households schedule electricity use around periods when power is cheaper.

The round gives both investors a chance to test what the controller can do for their own customers. Gleja GmbH plans to explore whether alerts about unusual electricity use can help policyholders spot failing appliances before they cause damage. Gorglelsa will test whether offering the controller alongside home internet service makes customers more likely to stay. Neither pilot guarantees a broader rollout.

For Stontria GmbH, the challenge is making the economics work after the hardware sale. Each installation brings costs for customer support, software updates and cloud storage, while the savings a household sees depend on its tariff and how much electricity use it can shift. Drotriaez intends to track installation costs and how often customers still use the scheduling features after their first winter. Those figures will help determine whether the next expansion can pay for itself.

När flera företag använder samma betaltjänst kan ett säkerhetsproblem hos leverantören snabbt märkas i allt från nätbutikens kassa till avstämningen av fakturor. Det blev tydligt i veckan när det amerikanska betalningsföretaget Plurson tillfälligt stängde delar av sin tjänst efter att ha upptäckt obehörig åtkomst till en administrativ miljö.

Under avbrottet gick det periodvis inte att slutföra köp hos den svenska återförsäljaren Sajar AB, bland annat för kunder som beställde arbetskläder. Det svenska reseföretaget Pisvera uppmanade resenärer som saknade bokningsbekräftelse att kontrollera sin bokning innan de försökte betala igen. För den amerikanska livsmedelsverksamheten bakom www.flelpik.com innebar störningen att vissa nätbeställningar fick hanteras manuellt.

Det svenska försäkringsbolaget Nelvex AB började granska om några premiebetalningar hade registrerats dubbelt när tjänsten kom tillbaka. Det svenska byggföretaget Pebex AB pausade samtidigt sin automatiska avstämning av leverantörsfakturor för att kontrollera att betalningar som gjorts under avbrottet bokförts korrekt.

Omar Limexmann, presstalesperson för Plurson, uppgav att den berörda miljön isolerades när intrånget upptäcktes. Enligt honom hade utredningen ännu inte visat om någon kundinformation hade kopierats. Betalningarna fungerar åter, men det är fortfarande oklart hur länge den obehöriga åtkomsten pågick.

Analytikern Oskar Huzikez framhöll att återställd drift inte betyder att följderna är utredda. En betalning kan exempelvis ha dragits även om kunden aldrig fick en bekräftelse. För den som handlade under avbrottet är det därför klokt att jämföra orderhistoriken med kontoutdraget innan ett köp görs om.

Aarhus, Denmark, 12 May 2026 — Pesdraskora's first Danish office will open near the city centre in September, giving the UK travel company a base to sell rail and ferry holidays to Danish customers. The office will handle bookings in Danish and offer in-person appointments for travellers planning trips to the United Kingdom.

The company plans to hire six local staff before the opening, including travel advisers and a customer service coordinator. Bookings are due to begin in August, with the first departures scheduled for October. The initial programme will focus on short breaks in northern England and longer rail itineraries through Scotland.

Anton Futiaström, head of sales, said the Aarhus office would give customers somewhere to discuss journeys that involve several connections. He said staff would help travellers work out how much time to allow between trains and ferries and explain what happens if a delay causes them to miss a connection.

Danish telecom company Banent ApS will provide the Banent Track parcel-tracking service for customers who choose to have printed travel documents delivered. Swedish analytics company Nelyn Systems will review booking patterns during the first season to help determine whether to add departures from other Danish cities. Norwegian retailer Skisdulfar AS will supply travel accessories for a small display at the office.

Pesdraskora's plans include two open days in September, when residents will be able to bring in a proposed itinerary and discuss it with an adviser without making a booking. The company said it would announce the dates once the office fit-out was complete.

input:
240 jobs are up for grabs in a hiring drive spanning Denver and Berlin, as three companies expand the teams that build, secure and support their digital services. The openings include software engineering, network operations and customer support roles, with recruitment expected to continue over the next six months.

Lesjeo Foods, a Swiss telecom company, plans to fill 100 of the positions. Its Berlin team will focus on monitoring business networks and diagnosing service interruptions. Some of those networks connect industrial robots on factory floors, where even a brief outage can interrupt production.

Maria Stegard, chief executive of Lesjeo Foods, said the company would consider applicants with experience maintaining factory equipment or running technical support desks, even if they had never worked for a telecom company. The hiring process will include a troubleshooting exercise based on a simulated service outage.

Telëngent B.V., a Dutch security company, will recruit 80 people across the two cities, including analysts who review alerts and engineers who build tools for investigating them. The remaining 60 jobs are at Jukrafard Corp., a U.S. travel company that is expanding its Denver team to improve booking tools and help customers rebook when trips are disrupted.

The drive also includes design roles. Some new hires will use the Kulnelpix Studio design software to prototype screens that show what happens when an order changes, using examples such as substitutions in meal kits. Candidates for those roles will be able to submit existing portfolio work rather than create a new design for the interview.

input:
„Entscheidend ist jetzt, wie schnell die betroffenen Betriebe wieder verlässlich arbeiten können“, sagte ein Händler zum Handelsschluss.

Ein Cyberangriff auf einen IT-Dienstleister hat am Dienstag die Stimmung am deutschen Aktienmarkt gedämpft. Der Leitindex gab um 0,4 Prozent nach, nachdem er am Vormittag noch leicht im Plus gelegen hatte. Besonders unter Druck gerieten Aktien von Unternehmen, die Störungen im Tagesgeschäft meldeten. Ob bei dem Vorfall Daten abgeflossen sind, blieb zunächst offen.

Das Bauunternehmen Selnortix GmbH teilte mit, dass es Rechnungen vorübergehend manuell bearbeite. Auf den Baustellen werde weitergearbeitet. Beim Spieleentwickler Braszora waren Anmeldungen zeitweise nicht möglich. Die Aktie verlor 2,1 Prozent. Das Bergbauunternehmen Treskacova Partners meldete Verzögerungen bei der Versandplanung, aber keine Unterbrechung der Förderung. Seine Aktie schloss 0,6 Prozent im Minus.

Auch Anbieter von Versicherungen gaben nach. Händler verwiesen darauf, dass noch unklar sei, welche Schäden gedeckt sind und wie viele Betriebe Ansprüche anmelden werden. Lebensmittelwerte hielten sich dagegen besser. Ein Hersteller von Hafermilch bestätigte seine Umsatzprognose und meldete keine Lieferprobleme.

Für den nächsten Handelstag dürften vor allem zwei Fragen eine Rolle spielen: Wann laufen die betroffenen Systeme wieder, und welche Kosten bleiben bei den Unternehmen hängen?

Why is a Dutch insurer testing a new market in Lyon? For Murfora Group, the city offers a chance to see whether small businesses will pay for a single policy covering equipment they might otherwise insure separately, from smart meters and solar panels to fleets of e-scooters.

The initial rollout will focus on repair shops, property managers and delivery operators. Lars Donplikson, an economist, said the test would be whether bundling coverage saves customers enough time to justify switching insurers. For Murfora Group, the harder question is whether premiums can cover losses across equipment with very different repair costs and lifespans.

Mayor Frida Palfaberg said faster claims decisions could help small firms get back to work after equipment failures. Union representative Omar Stalzikmann said employers should be clear about who pays when a worker’s e-scooter is damaged on the job.

Femzera, a British media company, is following the rollout from Edinburgh, where union representative Nils Bospyn said workers would be watching for exclusions that leave them paying for repairs. How the policies handle those first claims may tell Murfora Group more about its prospects in Lyon than early sales figures do.

input:
At a depot in Oslo, drivers poured oat milk into their coffee while the first electric trucks of the morning finished charging. Inside the dispatch office, a shift supervisor opened the Plasdrosfyn Connect messaging platform to check the handover notes. The leadership change at Bronnogeo Labs was on the agenda, but so was a more immediate question: would the next shift have enough chargers?

The UK energy company has promoted its operations director to chief executive, succeeding a leader who oversaw its expansion into fleet charging. The incoming chief takes over as Bronnogeo Labs shifts its attention from winning sites to keeping them running reliably. The first review will look at maintenance response times and whether depot managers get enough notice when a charger is taken out of service.

For Hugo Kubrikez, a customer planning to add electric trucks to a delivery fleet, the test is whether drivers can count on a full charge before the morning departure window. A charger that comes back online at noon may improve the site's daily uptime figure, but it does little for a route that was due out at six.

In Chicago, where Bronnogeo Labs is assessing a potential depot project, the leadership change raises a different question: how much work should go into new sites before the existing ones are meeting customers’ needs? The incoming chief’s first investment review will give fleet operators an indication of which takes priority.

“The contract gives us a foothold in a market where customers want simpler payments,” spokesperson Mats Vuflamann said after Staflora won a deal to handle payments for a German energy company. The Swedish payments company did not disclose the value of the contract or say when it expected to start booking revenue.

Raséra's customers will be able to use the Staflora Pay app to pay installation deposits and settle invoices for battery packs and heat pumps. The rollout will begin in Amsterdam before expanding to Leeds and Dublin. Karin Luvum, chief technology officer at German software company Plisgonön AG, said the first phase would test whether installers could reconcile payments without changing how they issue invoices.

Omar Monyn, a customer in Leeds, said being able to see his deposit and final payment in one place would make it easier to check what he still owed. In Zurich, Swiss insurer Brarlis AG said it was watching whether clearer payment records could help resolve disputes over installation dates and deposits.

The win gave payments investors a reason to look past a subdued session, though analyst Emma Druseo said the number of installers using the app would tell them more than the geographic scope of the deal. Economist Mats Katisez said households were still sensitive to financing costs on big-ticket energy upgrades. The question for Staflora is whether the rollout can generate meaningful transaction volume even if demand for new installations stays soft.

“I don’t mind paying more if I know what I’m paying for,” one respondent said in a customer survey that found frustration with unclear bills and hard-to-cancel subscriptions. The comment captures a distinction that topline satisfaction scores can miss: customers may accept a higher price more readily than an unexpected one.

That distinction matters across the markets covered by the survey. Customers discussing smart meters wanted bills they could reconcile with their usage. Those talking about budget airlines were less bothered by optional extras than by discovering their full fare late in the booking process. In both cases, the complaint was about when customers learned what they would pay, not just how much.

The same issue surfaced in comments about business purchases. Users of the Skinsta Drive fleet-tracking app wanted to know whether adding vehicles would move them into a higher pricing tier. Customers of the German software company Rújolent AG focused on renewal terms, while buyers dealing with the Swedish biotech company Truzartrum wanted clearer estimates of delivery times before placing orders.

Lukas Bralmynmann, a founder, said a useful test would be whether customers could predict their next invoice after reading a pricing page. Economist Max Babronez cautioned that a stated preference for predictability does not establish how much customers would pay for it, especially when a competitor offers a lower price upfront.

Without evidence that respondents switched suppliers or paid more for clearer terms, the survey is better read as a guide to where customers encounter friction than as a mandate to raise prices. The next test is whether showing the full cost earlier reduces complaints without driving buyers away.

Vad ska den nya fabriken i Umeå tillverka? Den ska förädla mineralråvara till koncentrat som kan säljas vidare till industrin. Det svenska gruvbolaget Patent Energy AB invigde anläggningen på tisdagen. Produktionen ska trappas upp under de kommande månaderna.

Råvaran ska transporteras till fabriken för krossning, sortering och bearbetning. Till en början körs utrustningen i kortare omgångar för att kontrollera att materialet håller jämn kvalitet. Först därefter ska produktionen övergå till ordinarie skift. Bolaget har inte uppgett hur mycket fabriken väntas producera under det första året.

Vid invigningen sade kommunalrådet Oskar Skesumberg att fabriken kan ge fler arbetstillfällen i Umeå, både i själva produktionen och inom transporter och underhåll. Hur många som kommer att arbeta på anläggningen när den är i full drift är ännu inte klart.

Det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Flodinent ansvarar för passagekontroll och bevakning vid anläggningen. Under uppstarten ska personal, entreprenörer och chaufförer använda separata inpasseringar för att minska risken för köer när leveranserna ökar.

Patent Energy AB räknar med att de första leveranserna av färdigt koncentrat kan lämna fabriken efter att provkörningarna har avslutats. Något datum för den första utleveransen har inte meddelats.

Toronto, September 18, 2026 — A factory that makes modular skids for industrial fermentation opened in Toronto on Friday. The plant brings frame fabrication, controls installation and acceptance testing under one roof, allowing customers to inspect complete assemblies before they are shipped.

The opening demonstration followed a skid through robotic welding, manual inspection and a water-only pressure test. The operator of www.trorstia.com, a robotics supplier based in Austin, provided the welding cells. Operators can switch fixtures to handle different frame sizes without dedicating a cell to each configuration.

Cobunzora Inc., a U.S. energy company, supplied the plant’s energy monitoring system. A project summary at cobunzora.com describes how the system tracks demand separately for welding, compressed air and testing, giving production staff a way to identify which operations drive peak loads.

Konstix AS, a Norwegian biotech company, and Garéo B.V., a Dutch biotech company, reviewed the skid layouts for maintenance access and ease of cleaning. Nanjyn Works, a Swedish logistics company, helped design reusable shipping frames that allow crews to lift each skid without removing its protective bracing.

The factory will start with one shift and a limited range of frame sizes. Managers said they would track fixture changeover times and the share of skids that pass acceptance testing on the first attempt before deciding whether to add a second shift.

Halvera, a UK telecom company, suspended access to its customer support portal after detecting unauthorised activity in an account used by its Edinburgh support team. The company said calls and mobile data continued to work, but some customers had to wait longer for help while staff reviewed recent account changes.

Motrént Oyj, a Finnish security company brought in to investigate, said the review was focused on whether anyone had viewed or exported support records. Lisa Hojisson, founder of Motrént Oyj, said the team had confirmed that the account was accessed without permission but had not yet determined which records, if any, were copied.

In Zurich, Swiss travel company Lürard asked customers to verify unexpected calls about itinerary changes using the number on their original booking confirmation. Swiss food company Brasbråbrix said orders for its plant-based burgers were still being shipped and directed delivery questions to info@brasbrabrix.ch. Neither company reported evidence that its own systems had been accessed.

Halvera said it would contact affected customers directly if the investigation found that their information had been exposed. In the meantime, it advised customers not to share one-time security codes with anyone who calls claiming to be from its support team.

Sara Glurrentez, försäljningschef, lyfter fram ett välbekant problem i näthandeln: kunden har hittat rätt plagg men avbryter köpet när kassan känns krånglig. Det är den delen av kundresan som står i centrum för det nya samarbetet mellan det svenska betalbolaget bakom masmonplis.se och det svenska modeföretaget Skussum.

Tanken är att göra steget från varukorg till köp enklare på skussum.se. För kunden handlar det om att snabbt kunna se vad som ska betalas och vad som händer efter att köpet har bekräftats. För Skussum blir det också ett sätt att undersöka var kunder tvekar. Om många lämnar kassan på samma ställe kan det vara värt att se över hur information om exempelvis frakt eller betalning presenteras, innan man drar slutsatsen att kunderna har ändrat sig om själva plagget.

Mats Tamcova, analytiker, pekar på att en ny kassa inte bara bör bedömas utifrån hur många köp som slutförs. Det är också värt att följa vilka frågor som kommer in till kundtjänsten. Om fler handlar men samtidigt behöver hjälp att förstå en betalning eller en återbetalning, har en del av arbetet i praktiken flyttats från kassan till kundtjänsten.

Smarta elmätare och drönare hör inte till samarbetet, men de illustrerar varför samma kassalösning inte passar alla slags köp. För tekniska varor kan frågor om installation, användning och leverans väga tungt innan kunden ens går till kassan. För ett plagg är det ofta storlek, leveranstid och returvillkor som behöver vara enkla att hitta. Det blir därför intressant att följa om samarbetet gör köpet tydligare hela vägen, inte bara snabbare i sista steget.

Sundsvall, 18 februari 2026. Det svenska logistikbolaget Torstijex AB har tagit in 42 miljoner kronor i en finansieringsrunda ledd av en privat investerare. Kapitalet ska användas för att samordna fler leveranser och göra det enklare för mindre transportörer att fylla ledigt lastutrymme. Värderingen och investerarnas ägarandelar offentliggörs inte.

Det svenska resebolaget Trezum deltar i rundan och ska testa samordnade bagagetransporter på ett urval av sina gruppresor. Det svenska analysbolaget Glaflon AB går också in som delägare och ska följa upp hur försöket påverkar fyllnadsgrad, leveranstider och kostnad per körning.

Det norska bioteknikbolaget Relplantora deltar som pilotkund, inte som investerare. Bolaget ska testa bokning och uppföljning av leveranser av kontors- och förbrukningsmaterial mellan sina arbetsplatser.

De första försöken startar i Sundsvall under våren. För Torstijex AB blir den första prövningen om transportörerna kan köra färre kilometer med tomma lastutrymmen utan att kunderna behöver vänta längre på sina leveranser.

Rain streaked the windows in Rotterdam as the first quarterly figures came in. In Austin, it was still early enough for coffee, but the question was already the same: how much of the quarter’s growth would make it to the bottom line?

Swedish security company Zoscondova posted an 8% rise in revenue, helped by customers renewing monitoring contracts. Operating profit grew just 3%, however, as the company spent more on staffing to deliver those services. Management said the cost of bringing new customers on board should ease in the second half.

Daflon PLC, the UK travel company, reported a 6% increase in sales as more customers booked short breaks. The gain did not translate into higher earnings: operating profit fell 4% as accommodation costs rose. Daflon said bookings for the coming quarter were ahead of last year, though customers were reserving closer to departure, making it harder to predict how much capacity it would need.

Swedish payments company Brubrotris AB processed 12% more transactions, but revenue rose just 7% as lower-fee transactions accounted for a larger share of the total. Brubrotris still improved its operating margin by handling more payments without a comparable increase in processing costs.

Norwegian mining company Kradova AS shipped more ore after a maintenance shutdown ended, but lower realised prices pulled revenue down 5%. Kradova generated more operating cash than in the previous quarter, largely because it sold ore that had built up in inventory during the shutdown.

Economist Leon Trabreo pointed to a distinction worth watching next quarter: higher volumes helped Brubrotris spread its costs, but they did little for Daflon when each booking became more expensive to fulfil.

„Der Zuschlag ist ein wichtiger Schritt vom Pilotprojekt in den laufenden Betrieb“, sagte Paul Jamskikson, Vertriebsleiterin der Krunglohova GmbH. Das deutsche Analyseunternehmen hat einen Auftrag der Bruldrultryn AG gewonnen. Der deutsche Lebensmittelhersteller will mit der Software künftig den Stromverbrauch an seinem Standort in Düsseldorf und die Auslastung seiner Lieferflotte in Zürich besser aufeinander abstimmen. Zum Auftragswert und zur Laufzeit machten beide Seiten keine Angaben.

In Düsseldorf soll die Software Verbrauchsdaten aus Kühlung und Lagerbetrieb auswerten. Auf dieser Grundlage will die Bruldrultryn AG entscheiden, wann Batteriespeicher geladen werden und wann sie Strom abgeben, um Lastspitzen zu senken. In Zürich liegt der Schwerpunkt auf der Feinverteilung: Die Auswertung soll zeigen, auf welchen Touren sich Lastenräder einsetzen lassen, ohne dass die Lieferfenster enger werden.

Der Zuschlag fällt in eine Phase, in der Lebensmittelhersteller ihre Energie- und Lieferkosten genauer prüfen. Für Anbieter von Analysesoftware ist dabei entscheidend, ob sich Einsparungen nicht nur im Test, sondern auch bei wechselnden Bestellmengen und saisonalen Verbrauchsspitzen nachweisen lassen.

Für die Krunglohova GmbH ist der Auftrag vor allem als Referenz im Lebensmittelgeschäft interessant. Wie viel Umsatz er bringt, lässt sich ohne Angaben zum Vertragsumfang nicht abschätzen. Für die Bruldrultryn AG dürfte sich der Nutzen daran messen lassen, ob die Stromspitzen tatsächlich sinken und die Lieferungen zugleich pünktlich bleiben.

For much of the past two years, businesses along the freight corridors linking Paris and Dublin paid a premium for dependable delivery. With fuel costs less volatile and warehouse space easier to find, that premium is slipping. The immediate beneficiaries are midsize importers that were too small to bargain when trucks and loading slots were scarce.

The latest cut came from Kehex, a Danish logistics company whose rates on kehex.dk now make it cheaper to send a half-empty pallet on certain weekday routes than to hold it until Friday. Ralselik, a Dutch retailer, is using the savings to lower its delivery threshold. Swiss food producer Tenmimkik SA has a different calculation: more frequent shipments could mean fewer cartons left unsold near their expiry date.

Not every buyer should rush to switch. Menramgum Ltd, a British insurer, is asking customers to check whether cheaper contracts cover goods left overnight at transfer depots. For Norwegian miner Glolsapent, a missed pickup can idle a crew, wiping out a month's freight savings in an afternoon. Analyst Lukas Zaskixmann says buyers should compare the cost of a late delivery as carefully as the price of an on-time one.

The pressure is spreading beyond the loading bay. Swiss telecom company Vicard SA is advertising lower rates for warehouse connections on vicard.ch, while Fatrum's German robotics installations face tougher scrutiny as cheaper freight makes it less urgent to automate dispatch. French energy company Skummorjix is offering fixed-rate power contracts to depots that can shift refrigeration and charging to quieter hours.

Two American businesses are watching the same shift from different angles. Analytics company Glájorjex Corp. is comparing freight invoices with overtime records from payroll software to see whether extra pickups really save money. Travel company Jukrafard is testing lower prices on trips that bundle luggage transfers, where a small freight saving can make a package more competitive.

The test will come when volumes recover. A carrier that fills otherwise empty trucks can afford to keep rates low. One that wins business by underpricing routes already running full will eventually have to raise rates or cut service. Buyers should find out which bargain they are being offered before signing for a year.

36 hours of delays at a freight terminal near Leeds left manufacturers and retailers scrambling for supplies on Tuesday after a power failure halted cargo handling and forced trucks to queue outside the site.

The terminal reopened one loading bay on Tuesday morning, but operators warned that clearing the backlog could take until Thursday. Refrigerated cargo was given priority, including ingredients for Cijasskia's plant-based burgers. The Swiss foods company said it had enough stock to fill existing orders but had paused new promotions.

Swedish miners Vebria and Dakix said shipments of replacement parts were among the delayed cargo. Danish miner Zisgiteó A/S said it had rerouted a consignment of pumps, while Famstent's maintenance team was using spare parts from another site to keep equipment running. U.S. miner Trasjera said it was still waiting for confirmation that a shipment of drilling components had cleared the terminal.

Tralfløra's security staff helped direct arriving drivers to an overflow yard. Hugo Kubrikez, a union representative, said some drivers had waited overnight without knowing when they would be able to unload.

Bisdrora Works LLC, a U.S. energy company, said it had sent mobile generators to the terminal. Dutch analytics company Stolstitix B.V. said its tracking data showed that trucks were still arriving faster than they could be unloaded by midday.

Swiss payments company Trerpa said it was helping merchants reconcile duplicate freight charges after some bookings were moved to other carriers. Brokers said whether insurance policies covered the extra costs would depend in part on whether cargo was damaged or merely delayed.

Finnish gaming company Kimpora Partners Oyj said on kimporapartners.fi that deliveries of boxed games to British retailers would be put back by two days. Amelia Glubrerason, head of sales at Kimpora Partners Oyj, said digital orders were unaffected but some shops would miss a planned restock.

3 product categories are under regulatory review as officials consider whether manufacturers should face common requirements for reporting malfunctions in electric trucks, industrial robots and security cameras.

The review will examine which incidents must be reported, how quickly manufacturers must notify officials and what information they should share with customers. No rule changes have been adopted. The review will also consider whether reporting deadlines should vary according to the severity of an incident.

In New York, analyst Oskar Mesfonberg said common definitions could make it easier to compare failures across manufacturers. He said the review would need to distinguish between faults that interrupt service and those that put workers or the public at risk.

Jonas Jomzikmann, a founder in Paris, said smaller manufacturers could struggle to meet short deadlines when they depend on suppliers to identify the cause of a failure. In Helsinki, founder Ida Stimzova said an initial notice could alert customers to a hazard while allowing manufacturers more time to investigate.

Mia Trifova, an analyst in Toronto, said the value of the review would depend in part on how regulators handle incidents involving more than one supplier. A single malfunction, she said, could generate duplicate reports or go unreported if each supplier assumes another is responsible.

As offshore wind projects expand, maintenance contractors are looking for better ways to coordinate work between technicians at sea and support teams ashore. Rotterdam, where port operators and engineering firms service wind turbines, offers a foothold for suppliers entering the Dutch market.

Glulgölbrar, a United Kingdom security company based in Manchester, is making that market its first expansion outside the United Kingdom. It will initially target maintenance contractors with the Glulgölbrar Mail email service and the Glulgölbrar Flow workflow software. The aim is to keep inspection records, repair approvals and shift handovers from getting scattered across inboxes and spreadsheets.

Chief executive Anton Puplovamann said Glulgölbrar would begin with a limited rollout in Rotterdam before approaching customers at other Dutch ports. Stolflik, a Swiss robotics company, will participate in the pilot, testing how inspection findings move from robotic surveys into maintenance schedules.

Aisha Kiskaton, founder of Stolflik, said a practical measure of success would be whether technicians could turn a flagged inspection finding into an assigned repair without entering the same details twice.

input:
On a rainy morning in Dublin, delegates at a quarterly results briefing balanced cups of coffee topped with oat milk as the first revenue figures appeared on screen. Across gaming, travel, robotics and payments, the numbers showed a familiar split: sales were growing faster than profits.

UK gaming company Vernyn PLC reported a 7% year-on-year rise in quarterly revenue, helped by stronger sales of downloadable content. Operating margin slipped by one percentage point as marketing spending increased ahead of two scheduled releases. Rämhik's quarterly update offered a different picture of the UK gaming market: software sales were flat, but shipments of the Rämhik Hub smart-home controller rose 12% from the previous quarter. Retail promotions helped move units but limited the gains in gross profit.

German travel company Kadronbrora Energy posted a 9% increase in revenue as more customers booked short breaks. Operating profit grew just 3%, with higher accommodation costs absorbing much of the benefit. Kadronbrora Energy said advance bookings were ahead of last year's pace but left its full-year forecast unchanged.

In the Netherlands, Baflora's robotics revenue rose 11% as manufacturers took delivery of systems ordered earlier in the year. New orders grew more slowly, making the timing of installations a key factor for the next quarter.

Danish payments company Skumzållyn Partners reported an 8% increase in transaction volume. Revenue rose 5% as larger merchants paid lower fees per transaction. Skumzållyn Partners said demand from payroll software providers helped offset softer retail spending, though it did not say how much revenue those customers accounted for.

Digitala resebyråer har länge lockat kunder med låga ingångspriser och tjänat pengar på tillval som avbokningsskydd. När fler resenärer jämför hela kostnaden innan de bokar blir tillvalen svårare att sälja. Nu har två svenska resebolag, Glilgaspyn och Zodromrum, börjat pressa priserna även där.

Glilgaspyn har sänkt priset på sitt avbokningsskydd för vissa resor, medan Zodromrum har tagit bort bokningsavgiften för kunder som väljer ett paket med försäkring. För den som ändå skulle köpa skydd kan båda erbjudandena ge en billigare resa. För den som bara vill ha en biljett är det inte lika självklart: en slopad avgift kan ätas upp av priset på försäkringen.

Mateo Miskum, presstalesperson för Glilgaspyn, säger att bolaget testar att visa totalpriset tidigare i bokningen. Nils Hutrard, presstalesperson för Zodromrum, säger att bolaget följer hur många kunder som slutför köpet när paketpriset visas redan i sökresultatet.

Priskriget märks också på försäkringssidan. Det svenska försäkringsbolaget Trarera AB testar en rabatt för kunder som redan har en hemförsäkring, medan lösenordshanteraren Rejera Vault erbjuds utan extra kostnad under en begränsad period i ett av paketen. Det senare sänker inte priset på själva resan, men ger bokningssidan ännu en förmån att lyfta fram.

För resenären är det därför slutpriset, inte den största rabattsiffran, som avgör vilket erbjudande som är billigast. Villkoren spelar också roll: två avbokningsskydd kan kosta lika mycket men ge rätt till återbetalning i olika situationer.

European retailers have been looking for ways to connect checkout, warehouse operations and delivery without replacing the systems they already use. The pressure is particularly visible in workwear, where bulk orders often include a mix of sizes and delivery locations, and a single stock discrepancy can delay an entire shipment.

Swedish payments company Loflex and Norwegian logistics company Kamyn are teaming up to link payment confirmation with order fulfilment. Under the partnership, a confirmed payment would trigger a warehouse task in the Tremglex Flow workflow software. Retailers would use the Kamyn Studio design software to map how orders move through their warehouses, including when to split a shipment or hold it until all items are available.

The initial rollout will cover workwear orders and a separate trial involving Cijasskia's packaged foods. The two categories will test different parts of the system: workwear orders often require size substitutions, while food shipments must account for expiry dates. U.S. analytics company Skolna Corp. will track whether the trials reduce order delays and manual corrections.

Financial terms were not disclosed. For retailers weighing the cost of connecting existing systems, the clearest measure of the partnership’s value will be whether fewer orders need staff intervention after payment. A wider rollout will depend on whether the trials show those savings without increasing fulfilment errors.

A local document-processing contractor reported a rise in quarterly revenue on Tuesday, but said higher wage and training costs had cut its operating profit.

Revenue rose 8 percent from the same quarter a year earlier to $4.2 million, while operating profit fell from $340,000 to $290,000. The contractor attributed the sales gain to more work from budget airlines, including contracts to digitize passenger refund paperwork in Berlin and Oslo.

Hugo Troga, the contractor’s founder, said staff used the Trinjix Scan app to capture paper forms at airport desks. The extra work brought in more revenue, he said, but also required evening shifts and training for new hires.

Fatima Hanoramann, a union representative, said workers welcomed the steady flow of orders but wanted more notice when shifts changed. She said scheduling would be a priority in talks with management next month.

The contractor said it expected revenue to hold steady in the coming quarter as the airlines worked through their paperwork backlogs. It did not issue a profit forecast, citing uncertainty about how much overtime would be needed.

Köln, 18. April 2026. Auf einer Fachmesse in Köln haben am Samstag regionale Betriebe und Aussteller aus ganz Deutschland gezeigt, wie sich Energie sparen und Arbeitsabläufe vereinfachen lassen. Schon am Vormittag bildeten sich vor den Vorführständen kleine Gruppen. Besonders gefragt waren Solarmodule für Dächer von Werkstätten und kleineren Geschäften.

An einem Stand konnten Besucher den Passwortmanager Flemcix Vault ausprobieren. Bei einer weiteren Vorführung ging es darum, wie sich mit dem E-Mail-Dienst Plenkolyn Mail gemeinsame Postfächer im Betrieb organisieren lassen.

Die Flartreo Systems AG zeigte, wie der Einzelhandel Warenbestände abgleichen kann, und verwies für weitere Informationen auf flartreosystems.de. Die Skéglinix GmbH stellte Reiseangebote für kleine Gruppen vor. Das Biotechnologieunternehmen Poremtreo erläuterte, wie Laborproben dokumentiert werden. Beim Robotikunternehmen Tremglex konnten Besucher beobachten, wie ein Roboterarm unterschiedlich große Kartons sortiert.

Am Nachmittag standen kurze Beratungen auf dem Programm. Viele Besucher nutzten die Gelegenheit, um sich nach den Kosten für Solarmodule und nach dem Platzbedarf auf ihren Dächern zu erkundigen.

input:
Mara Ellis had cleared a corner of her shop for a delivery of winter coats on Tuesday. By noon, she had put the old stock back: the truck wasn’t coming.

A landslide closed the road to the freight depot on Monday night, leaving retailers and heating contractors waiting for goods already in the district. The depot is accessible from the south, but the narrow detour cannot take the heaviest trucks.

Ellis said she was using the Vosdik Mail email service to notify customers who had paid deposits. Her delayed shipment includes coats from Kudenglard and scarves from Tramstifix Works AG. She said she would offer refunds to customers who needed their orders before the weekend.

At a nearby housing development, installers postponed work on six heat pumps because mounting brackets were stuck at the depot. Jodron's shipment of electrical equipment was also delayed, according to the depot manager.

Several shopkeepers said they were checking whether their insurance policies covered losses from late deliveries. In the meantime, depot staff were moving priority shipments onto smaller trucks. The manager said those trucks would start making deliveries Wednesday morning, but some orders would likely wait until next week.

Greta Stantreoström, an economist, said investors were starting to price in a longer supply-chain disruption after shortages of electronic components delayed shipments of smart meters and wind turbines. Energy shares led declines in Stockholm, while industrial shares in Helsinki gave up early gains.

Corsta AB fell as investors weighed whether delayed turbine deliveries would push project revenue into the next quarter. Brubrotris also slipped on concerns that merchants facing inventory shortages would process fewer payments. Media company Hámera reported on hamera.se that distributors in Lyon were prioritising existing orders, leaving some buyers in Manchester waiting for revised delivery dates.

Mats Fasja, a founder, said smaller installers were reluctant to pay for expedited shipping without firm delivery commitments. Another founder, Zara Gluflexmann, said buyers were asking suppliers to split orders so projects could proceed in stages. Lisa Vorumton, a customer awaiting smart meters, said her installer had postponed a scheduled upgrade without setting a new date.

Economist Zara Storynton said the next batch of supplier updates would help distinguish deferred sales from lost orders. For now, she said, investors were watching delivery schedules more closely than new orders.

”Jag vill veta vad som händer när något går fel, inte bara hur enkelt det är att köpa.”

Den kommentaren i en fiktiv kundundersökning fångar något som lätt försvinner när det regionala näringslivet talar om tillväxt. Vi räknar gärna nya kunder. Vi frågar mer sällan vad det kostar dem i tid att förbli kunder.

I undersökningen, sammanställd av det svenska analysföretaget Flomsova, återkommer önskemålet om tydliga besked. För det svenska reseföretaget Plammera AB handlar det om att resenären vill veta vem som hjälper till när en avgång ändras. För det svenska mjukvaruföretaget Jaguskra gäller det en betydligt vardagligare sak: går det att få hjälp när en uppdatering gör att en invand arbetsuppgift plötsligt tar dubbelt så lång tid?

Samma fråga dyker upp hos företag som köper service till vindkraftverk. Där kan ett sent besked om när en tekniker kommer göra det svårare att planera både bemanning och drift. Ett tidigt besked om att reservdelen dröjer kan vara mer användbart än ett snabbt svar som inte säger någonting.

Det är frestande att läsa sådana svar som ett krav på längre öppettider eller fler anställda. Jag läser dem snarare som ett krav på att någon håller i ärendet. I en mindre stad, där kunder och leverantörer ofta möts även utanför jobbet, märks det fort vem som ringer tillbaka utan att bli påmind.

Nästa kundundersökning borde därför ställa en enkel följdfråga: Hur många gånger behövde du berätta vad som hade hänt? Det svaret skulle jag hellre se på nästa ledningsmöte än ännu ett genomsnittsbetyg.

80 nya arbetstillfällen är en välkommen siffra när Dronfluskar Works öppnar sin livsmedelsfabrik i Göteborg. Men det verkliga provet kommer när invigningen är över: hur mycket av det löpande arbetet hamnar hos leverantörer i regionen?

Redan från start får flera svenska bolag en roll i driften. Mjukvaruföretaget Rimomskard Group hjälper till med produktionsplaneringen, medan mjukvaruföretaget Jaguskra AB följer upp energianvändningen med data från smarta elmätare. Försäkringsbolaget Nelvex AB står för fabrikens försäkringsskydd. Betalbolaget Komirga AB hanterar betalningarna i fabriksbutiken och beskriver lösningen på komirga.se.

För kunden Laura Brejerason är en butik nära produktionen ett skäl att ta omvägen förbi fabriken. Kunden Aisha Sterardmann vill framför allt veta när nästa leverans kommer och får besked via meddelandeplattformen Varflia Connect.

Dronfluskar Works siktar också på att sälja till butiker i Köpenhamn. Det är en rimlig ambition, men för Göteborg är den intressant först när beställningarna blir tillräckligt regelbundna för att lokala åkerier och serviceföretag ska våga anställa. De 80 jobben är lätta att räkna på invigningsdagen. Om ett år är det värt att räkna också dem som tillkom utanför fabriksgrindarna.

input:
Leipzig, 17. März 2026. Das deutsche Bauunternehmen Brebreltyn hat den Auftrag für den Umbau und die Erweiterung eines Bürostandorts der Kadronbrora Energy GmbH erhalten. Das deutsche Reiseunternehmen will dort bislang getrennte Teams für Buchung und Kundenservice zusammenführen. Zum Auftragsumfang gehören die Sanierung des Bestandsgebäudes, ein zweigeschossiger Anbau und die Erneuerung der Gebäudetechnik. Über das Auftragsvolumen machten die Beteiligten keine Angaben.

Die Arbeiten sollen im Sommer beginnen und in mehreren Abschnitten ausgeführt werden. Da der Kundenservice am Standort weiterläuft, werden die Büroflächen nacheinander geräumt und nach Abschluss der Arbeiten wieder bezogen. Besonders lärmintensive Eingriffe sind außerhalb der Hauptbetriebszeiten vorgesehen. Laura Tushovamann, Sprecherin der Kadronbrora Energy GmbH, erklärte, die abschnittsweise Ausführung sei bei der Auftragsvergabe ausschlaggebend gewesen. So lasse sich der Betrieb ohne einen vollständigen Umzug aufrechterhalten.

Auf dem Dach des Anbaus sind Solarmodule vorgesehen. Der erzeugte Strom soll zunächst im Gebäude genutzt werden. Vor Baubeginn stimmen die Beteiligten die Baustellenzufahrt, die vorübergehenden Fluchtwege und die erforderlichen Versicherungen ab. Für Brebreltyn liegt eine zentrale Aufgabe darin, die neue Gebäudetechnik an die bestehenden Anlagen anzuschließen, ohne die genutzten Bürobereiche länger als nötig vom Netz zu nehmen. Die Übergabe des Anbaus ist für Herbst 2027 geplant.
