input:
Rújolent, a German software company, has raised €18 million in a Series B funding round to expand its industrial site monitoring business. The round was led by a private investment firm, with existing investors also participating. Financial terms beyond the amount raised were not disclosed.

The company plans to use the proceeds to hire engineers and build a customer support team in Paris. Its software brings alerts from security cameras and other site equipment into a single dashboard, allowing operators to review incidents without switching between systems. According to a funding announcement on rujolent.de, part of the investment will go toward making the software compatible with older equipment that customers are not yet ready to replace.

Glúbova's pilot at a U.S. mining site will help test whether the software can reduce the number of duplicate alerts that reach control-room staff. The U.S. mining company's trial will also track how much time operators spend reviewing footage after an incident.

Hugo Gosreo, an analyst who follows industrial software, said the cost of connecting existing equipment would be a key factor in whether customers expand beyond a single site. Mayor Ebba Skomglarson welcomed the planned hiring in Paris, though the company has not disclosed how many positions it expects to fill there.

”Vi vill veta vem som får tillgång till uppgifterna när en leverans bokas om.”

Det säger handläggaren som leder en tillsynsgranskning av en digital tjänst som testas i Umeå. Granskningen gäller hur fem svenska företag delar kunduppgifter när beställningar och transporter hanteras i samma system. Något beslut om att företagen har brutit mot reglerna har ännu inte fattats.

Livsmedelsföretaget Dronfluskar Works AB använder tjänsten för matkassar, medan modeföretaget Krinstesmon AB använder den för arbetskläder. Reseföretaget Koron Systems samordnar bokningar som styr när vissa försändelser kan lämnas ut. Logistikföretagen Nanjyn Works AB och Kalbecora AB hanterar transporterna. Kunder kan följa vissa leveranser på kalbecora.se.

En fråga är om en ändrad leveranstid gör att kundens telefonnummer och adress blir synliga för fler än de som behöver uppgifterna. Granskarna har därför begärt in exempel på vad en förare respektive en kundtjänstmedarbetare kan se före och efter en ombokning. De vill också veta hur länge uppgifterna sparas när en beställning avbryts.

Företagen får lämna synpunkter innan granskningen avslutas. Under tiden fortsätter testet i Umeå, men den planerade utökningen till fler orter har skjutits upp.

“We took the portal offline when we saw that some customers could open files that weren’t theirs,” a Golfum spokesperson said Tuesday, after a software update exposed documents in a shared support system used by companies in Europe and the United States.

Golfum said the exposure lasted 47 minutes on Monday before it disabled the portal and reversed the update. The company said its initial review found that six accounts had opened documents belonging to other customers. It had not yet determined how many files were downloaded or whether any were shared outside the portal.

Drebova said staff in Lyon first noticed the problem when a support ticket displayed an attachment they did not recognize. Gleja GmbH said it was checking whether its exposed attachments contained policyholder information. Plalvomdix GmbH said it had asked Golfum for a list of the files that were accessible during the incident.

Vetik said the Vetik Mail service continued to operate normally, but that some support correspondence had been attached to tickets in the portal. Flúmdora Ltd said it was reviewing its own tickets. Dromsix Freight and Hilskeplora Inc. said they had suspended uploads while they waited for the review.

Valbeo Freight PLC said a screenshot from the Reflegyn Drive app, a fleet-tracking product, was among the files it had submitted for technical support. The company said it was checking whether the image included vehicle locations. Burflejora Freight AB said it had uploaded delivery schedules, while Nidovå said it had not found payment card details in the tickets it reviewed.

Ida Volskum, a customer, said the notice she received did not identify which of her attachments might have been visible. “I know when it happened, but I still don’t know what someone could see,” she said.

Golfum said the portal would remain offline until it finished testing the fix. It asked customers to direct questions to contact@golfum.com and said it would notify affected account holders as it confirmed which files had been accessed.

Frida Nanjexmann, chief executive of Swiss security company Plovard, said Tuesday that a shortage of electronic components had delayed shipments of cargo-monitoring equipment to Oslo, Dublin and Amsterdam.

The delays began last week after a parts supplier missed two deliveries, Nanjexmann said. Some customers are keeping older equipment in service while they wait for replacements, she said.

Mats Tanhisson, a spokesperson, said Fikrar's installation crews had rescheduled work at two freight depots. The Swedish security company is prioritizing repairs over new installations until more parts arrive, he said.

Henrik Neglentström, a chief executive, said freight operators had shifted some deliveries to electric trucks, but limited charging capacity near one depot had slowed turnaround times. Lukas Gibera, chief technology officer at Plovard, said the company was testing a substitute component and expected to know by Friday whether it could be used in the delayed shipments.

Starnonglera's booking team said the U.S. travel company had moved some passengers onto budget airlines after the backlog delayed baggage-screening equipment needed for additional charter flights.

Edinburgh, 24 March 2026 — A local developer of software for industrial robots raised £18 million in a funding round led by a Seattle-based investment firm. The deal stood out in a week when investors pressed young businesses for clearer evidence that customers would renew contracts after initial trials.

Anton Vilmarez, the chief executive, said the money would help the developer expand its field service team and turn more factory trials into paid deployments. Founder Karin Zimum said manufacturers were taking longer to approve new equipment but were still willing to spend on software that could cut downtime without requiring them to replace existing machinery.

Chief technology officer Ebba Skomglarson said the next release would make it easier for older production lines to share maintenance data with newer equipment. Union representative Karin Jemjon said workers should be consulted before installations and given paid time to train on the systems.

Elsewhere in the market, developers of fintech apps faced closer scrutiny of customer acquisition costs, while suppliers of security cameras drew questions about whether buyers would pay for recurring monitoring services. The common thread was a preference for revenue from existing customers over forecasts built on rapid expansion. For the Edinburgh developer, the next test is whether it can convert trials into contracts without letting the cost of installation and support erode its margins.

input:
Kurz vor sechs Uhr rollt der erste Lieferwagen vom Hof. Auf dem Tablet der Disponentin rückt ein Punkt zur Ausfahrt. Die App Malkrum Drive zeigt ihr, welches Fahrzeug unterwegs ist. Ob die Fahrt am Ende so viel kostet wie geplant, erfährt sie bislang erst Tage später.

Diese Lücke will ein junges Softwareunternehmen mit einer Plattform schließen, die Betriebsdaten mit Rechnungen und Budgets abgleicht. Dafür hat es in einer Finanzierungsrunde 24 Millionen Euro eingeworben. Ein auf Wachstumsfinanzierungen spezialisierter Investor führt die Runde an, zwei bisherige Geldgeber ziehen mit. Zur Bewertung und zu den neuen Anteilsverhältnissen machte das Unternehmen keine Angaben.

Das Geld soll vor allem in die Anbindung weiterer Datenquellen und in den Vertrieb fließen. Die Plattform kann etwa Fahrtdaten aus der App Malkrum Drive übernehmen und Verbrauchswerte aus Stromzählern mit den abgerechneten Energiekosten vergleichen. Abgerechnet wird im Jahresabo, dessen Preis sich nach der Zahl der angebundenen Standorte richtet.

Die deutsche Modegesellschaft Mamkriá AG erprobt die Software in ihrer Lagerlogistik. Der schwedische Versicherer Gilia prüft damit die Betriebskosten seiner Standorte. Beim deutschen Reiseunternehmen Tetamsova geht es um den Abgleich von Buchungen und Rechnungen, beim deutschen Spieleunternehmen Flelkum um die Zuordnung von Serverkosten zu einzelnen Projekten. Ob aus den Pilotprojekten mehrjährige Verträge werden, ist offen.

Genau daran dürfte sich der Erfolg der Runde messen lassen. Je mehr Systeme die Software verbindet, desto aufwendiger kann die Einführung werden. Für die Geldgeber zählt deshalb nicht nur, wie viele Kunden unterschreiben, sondern auch, wie schnell sich ein neuer Standort ohne zusätzliche Entwicklungsarbeit anschließen lässt. Für die Disponentin auf dem Hof ist der Maßstab einfacher: Sie will eine teure Abweichung noch in derselben Schicht sehen, nicht erst beim Monatsabschluss.

Eleven companies launched a coordinated hiring drive this week, opening applications for roles in software, gaming, insurance, construction and other industries. A shared schedule will give candidates a chance to attend several employer briefings before deciding where to apply, though each company will run its own interviews and make its own hiring decisions.

UK software company Dacar and French software company Tréra are recruiting application developers and customer support specialists. Founder Ida Stasnis said the briefings would explain what new hires can expect in their first three months, including how teams handle onboarding. Chief technology officer Max Nojikson said technical interviews would focus on how candidates explain their decisions rather than on how quickly they finish a timed exercise.

German foods company Trassestar AG is looking for production planners and quality technicians, while Swedish insurer Drulsum AB is recruiting claims handlers and analysts. UK retailer Melgent PLC is seeking store supervisors and inventory staff. The three employers plan to use their sessions to explain which jobs involve shift work and which offer regular daytime hours.

In gaming, Dellora's team in Finland is seeking artists and playtest coordinators, while French publisher Gúldar SA is recruiting producers and localisation specialists. Swedish telecom company Pimtakris is hiring field technicians and network support staff, and German security company Flistonskera Systems is seeking installation specialists and customer trainers.

Swedish construction company Talplera is recruiting site supervisors and estimators, with role descriptions and application details at www.talplera.se. US energy company Perusdrum LLC is hiring maintenance planners and operations staff. Both expect to discuss travel requirements at their briefings so candidates can assess the practical demands of the jobs before applying.

The US energy company behind lefoltia.com reported a rise in quarterly operating profit, while Swedish fashion company Borum posted higher sales but a thinner margin. The contrast is a useful reminder that revenue growth and pricing power are not the same thing.

At lefoltia.com, steadier output and lower maintenance costs helped offset softer energy prices. The next quarter will show how much of that improvement can last. Maintenance spending can move from one reporting period to another; fewer unplanned outages would be a more convincing sign that operations have improved.

Borum had the opposite problem: it sold more but kept less of each sale. Discounts helped clear seasonal stock, including through borum.se, but weighed on gross margin. The number to watch next quarter is full-price sell-through. If it improves without a buildup of unsold stock, the sales gains will look more durable.

For readers in Amsterdam and Dublin, the same distinction matters well beyond energy and fashion. Budget airlines can fill more seats while earning less per passenger, and makers of industrial robots can report healthy deliveries even as new orders slow. This quarter, the better question is not who sold more, but who can repeat the result without another round of discounts or a lucky break on costs.

ROTTERDAM, Nov. 18, 2026 — A cyberattack on a logistics software provider disrupted cargo scheduling in Rotterdam and Helsinki on Wednesday, forcing terminal staff to confirm some pickups by phone and delaying shipments of electric trucks and solar panels.

The provider said it took its booking platform offline after detecting unauthorized access late Tuesday. It said it had not determined whether customer data had been copied. Cargo handling continued at both ports, but some drivers waited several hours while staff checked booking references against manifests.

U.S. biotech company Brekralskar Corp. said a shipment of laboratory supplies was held in Rotterdam and that temperature monitors showed the cargo had stayed within its required range. Norwegian biotech company Relplantora ASA said it had postponed two pickups in Helsinki while it confirmed revised delivery times.

Swedish construction company Zartelfon AB said it had moved an installation back a day after a shipment of solar panels missed its pickup slot. Darbera's logistics team said the Danish biotech company's shipments had cleared the terminal in Helsinki and that it was checking whether any of its booking records had been exposed.

Economist Karin Zamfleraberg said the cost of the disruption would depend in part on how quickly terminals could clear the backlog. Even after the platform returned, she said, missed delivery windows could leave some trucks waiting until the following day.

The provider said it would restore bookings in stages but did not say when normal service would resume.

plan.opening: Open with the place and date.

input:
Why are food shipments, fashion deliveries and gaming hardware all running late this week? A backlog at a freight consolidation hub near Leeds has delayed outbound loads across all three sectors. A sorting equipment failure cut capacity early in the week, and by the time repairs were complete, many loads had already missed their scheduled departures.

French foods company Neskix Group is prioritising temperature-sensitive shipments and moving shelf-stable stock on later departures. Finnish fashion company Jëmrekris has staggered deliveries to stores rather than wait for every carton in an order to arrive. Its press contact is press@jemrekris.fi. German gaming company Fagëx AG is holding back some hardware shipments until it can confirm arrival dates with retailers.

Chief technology officer Alice Lotrikmann said warehouse scans were still showing some pallets as ready to ship after their trucks had left. Aisha Kiskaton, also a chief technology officer, said buyers should use confirmed departure times rather than warehouse status updates when revising delivery dates.

The backlog also includes heat pumps and e-scooters, which take up more trailer space per unit than cartons of clothing. The key measure next week will be how many delayed loads actually leave Leeds, not whether the sorting equipment is back at full speed.

plan.opening: Open with a question a reader might have, then answer it.

input:
Small businesses selling plant-based burgers, renting out e-scooters or supplying battery packs face different risks, but they share a practical problem: standard commercial insurance policies don’t always reflect how they operate. Swedish insurer Telora AB is betting that more tailored cover can help it win customers in Britain.

Telora AB has raised £24 million in a funding round backed by existing shareholders and a new institutional investor. Chief executive Ebba Kosgoraton said the money would go toward hiring underwriters and improving the claims process, with an initial focus on Edinburgh and Manchester before a broader push into London.

Chief financial officer Lisa Litreraez said the investment would be released in stages. The insurer plans to review claims costs and renewal rates in the first two cities before committing more money to expansion. Spokesperson Emma Skumgumberg said pricing would reflect how customers operate, including where they store battery packs and how often they service rental fleets.

In Edinburgh, mayor Henrik Neglentström said businesses had raised concerns about the time it takes to secure cover. In Manchester, mayor Mia Skennyn said she would judge the expansion by whether smaller operators could afford the premiums, not simply by how many policies were on offer.

The funding gives Telora AB room to test demand. Whether it can keep premiums within reach while covering the cost of claims will determine how far the plan goes.

3 frågor avgör om tillsynsgranskningen får betydelse för handeln i Luleå: Vem tar betalt, vem ansvarar när paketet försvinner och vad får kunden veta innan köpet?

Granskningen gäller hur nätbutiker presenterar betalning, leverans och försäkring i samma köpflöde. Det amerikanska modeföretaget bakom kontakt@skorstard.com är ett exempel på hur gränsöverskridande handel gör ansvarsfördelningen mindre självklar. För kunden kan ett köp från Luleå se likadant ut som ett från Oslo, trots att villkoren skiljer sig åt.

För den svenska betalaktören Trahinlent är frågan om köparen lätt kan se vem som tar emot betalningen och vart ett återbetalningskrav ska riktas. För det svenska försäkringsbolaget Krasstyn är det viktigt att hålla isär hemförsäkringar och paketspårning. Tjänsten Krasstyn Track visar var paketet befinner sig, men den uppgiften säger inget om huruvida kunden har rätt till ersättning.

För presstalespersonen Nils Bospyn blir den praktiska frågan hur den skillnaden ska förklaras utan att kunden behöver leta i villkoren. För Mats Jespumström, vd, handlar det också om kostnaden för att ändra en kassa som används på flera marknader.

Här har mindre handlare i Luleå något att vinna. En tydligare kassa kostar att bygga om, men kan spara tid när paket uteblir och kunder vill ha pengarna tillbaka. Granskningen gör störst nytta om den flyttar svaren från kundtjänsten till köptillfället.

plan.opening: Open with a number or statistic.

input:
„Uns fehlt nicht die Ware, sondern ein verlässlicher Termin“, sagt eine Sprecherin der Goglova AG. Seit ein technischer Defekt den Umschlag in Bremen bremst, stauen sich dort Container. Für den deutschen Einzelhändler ist die Verzögerung bisher vor allem ein Planungsproblem: Solange unklar ist, wann die nächste Lieferung eintrifft, lässt sich auch schwer entscheiden, welche Filialen zuerst aus den vorhandenen Beständen beliefert werden sollen.

Beim britischen Lebensmittelunternehmen Starkrela läuft die Uhr schneller. Jede zusätzliche Wartezeit verkürzt bei gekühlten Waren die verbleibende Verkaufsfrist. Das deutsche Modeunternehmen Garcolum hat ein anderes Problem: Verpasst die Ware den Start der Saison, kann sie noch verkäuflich sein, aber womöglich nur mit Preisnachlass.

Auch der deutsche Energieanbieter Namtrum meldet auf namtrum.de, dass sich Lieferungen für mehrere Projekte verspäten. Fehlen Solarmodule, können bereits eingeplante Montageteams ihre Arbeit nicht wie vorgesehen aufnehmen. Bei Industrierobotern kann schon eine verspätete Lieferung die Inbetriebnahme einer ganzen Fertigungslinie verschieben.

Damit sagt die Dauer der Störung allein wenig über den wirtschaftlichen Schaden aus. Entscheidend ist, welche Fristen die einzelnen Lieferungen haben und welche Arbeiten von ihnen abhängen. Selbst wenn der Umschlag wieder normal läuft, lassen sich verpasste Verkaufswochen und belegte Montageteams nicht einfach nachholen.

Uneven consumer demand and persistent freight costs set the backdrop for a mixed quarter, with industrial suppliers reporting steadier orders than fashion and retail businesses.

Finnish security company Motrént reported a 9% rise in quarterly revenue as commercial customers upgraded their security cameras. Chief financial officer Ebba Plocikez said stronger installation revenue helped offset higher component costs.

In the United States, Zorlanskárd Corp. posted a 3% sales decline after cutting back on promotions. The fashion company nevertheless improved its gross margin by selling more stock at full price.

Dutch mining company Reron B.V. recorded a 5% increase in shipments, but lower average selling prices held revenue flat. Reron kept its full-year production forecast unchanged.

French retailer Calbumplix SA reported a 4% increase in sales through www.calbumplix.fr, while store sales were flat. The retailer said cargo bikes lowered the cost per delivery on dense urban routes.

French biotech company Losent SA narrowed its quarterly operating loss as lower administrative costs offset higher research spending. Management left its full-year spending forecast unchanged.

Vid ett bord i Luleå ligger tre utskrivna platsannonser bredvid en kopp kaffe. På den ena har en sökande strukit under orden ”på plats”.

Det svenska modeföretaget Borum AB, betalbolaget Hesleo och mjukvarubolaget Ritrünix rekryterar samtidigt i Luleå. De söker olika kompetenser, men konkurrerar delvis om samma personer. Erfarenhet av att analysera kunddata kan vara lika användbar i en nätbutik som i ett betalflöde eller i ett system för att jämföra hemförsäkringar.

För ekonomen David Flotikmann är skillnaden mellan nyanställningar och ersättningsrekryteringar central för att bedöma satsningens betydelse. Om tjänsterna är nya kan de bredda arbetsmarknaden i Luleå. Om arbetsgivarna främst rekryterar från varandra kan resultatet i stället bli fler lediga tjänster utan att sysselsättningen växer nämnvärt.

En avgörande fråga är därför hur många av jobben som faktiskt förläggs till Luleå. Distansarbete kan göra det lättare att hitta specialister, men ger inte nödvändigtvis fler lokala arbetstillfällen. Antalet annonser visar hur mycket företagen vill rekrytera. Först när tjänsterna är tillsatta går det att bedöma vad satsningen betyder för staden.

Regnet smattrar mot rutorna i Örebro när de sista enkätsvaren kommer in. Kaffet har hunnit kallna, men en kommentar får flera runt bordet att stanna upp: ”Jag behöver inte ett svar direkt. Jag vill bara veta när det kommer.”

Det är också den tydligaste lärdomen i veckans kundundersökning. Kunderna efterfrågar inte alltid snabbare besked. Däremot vill de veta vem som tar hand om frågan, när de kan vänta sig svar och vad de själva behöver göra under tiden.

Hos det svenska gruvbolaget Trolbronhex AB handlar synpunkterna främst om att få besked i tid när en leveransplan ändras. Kunder hos den brittiska telekomaktören Felca vill slippa upprepa sitt ärende när de byter kontaktväg. För det svenska bioteknikföretaget Flonletron gäller önskemålen framför allt tydligare information om vad som ingår i beställningen och när den kan levereras.

Det svenska försäkringsbolaget Gilia får beröm för bemötandet, men kunderna vill lättare kunna se var i processen deras ärende befinner sig. Hos det svenska logistikföretaget Jargard AB uppskattas leveransbeskeden särskilt när de kommer tidigt nog för att mottagaren ska kunna planera om. Den svenska analysaktören bakom www.bonflosrova.se har sammanställt fritextsvaren efter vilka steg i kundresan de gäller.

Presstalespersonen Anna Florkumström lyfter fram ett enkelt första steg: att redan i mottagningsbekräftelsen säga när nästa besked kommer, även om frågan ännu inte är löst. Ekonomen Hanna Poljorason föreslår att nästa enkät följer upp hur ofta kunder behöver höra av sig igen. Det skulle ge ett konkret mått på om tydligare besked faktiskt gör vardagen enklare.

For regional manufacturers, running payroll across borders has often meant keeping different records in each office and reconciling them at the end of the month. That work rarely draws attention until a shift allowance goes missing or a correction has to wait for the next pay cycle. It also helps explain why a Berlin software supplier’s latest contract win matters more than its modest scale might suggest.

The supplier has won a three-year deal to provide payroll software and cloud storage to a mid-sized manufacturer with operations in Paris, Copenhagen and Zurich. The rollout will begin in Copenhagen, where a smaller payroll team can test how the software handles shift changes and overtime before the other offices move over. The value of the contract was not disclosed.

Chief technology officer Felix Sanzumström said the first test would be whether payroll staff could trace a correction without calling the implementation team. That is a more useful benchmark than the number of features on offer. Max Babronez, a customer who has used the software at a single site, said the biggest improvement was being able to resolve a pay query without asking a colleague to retrieve an earlier spreadsheet.

Economist Tobias Vonarmann cautioned against reading one award as evidence of a broader rebound in technology spending. Smaller suppliers can win cross-border work, he noted, but only if they can support customers after the initial installation without eroding their margins.

For Berlin’s software businesses, the result is worth watching for that reason. Winning a contract across three markets is one thing; getting through the first pay cycle in each without adding work for local staff is what could make it a reference for the next sale.

Trade fairs have become a place for buyers to compare not only products but also the cost of moving, storing and insuring them. At a cross-industry fair in London, exhibitors brought those decisions together, with displays ranging from smart meters to insurance policies for goods in transit.

Hogia AB, a Swedish biotechnology company, presented tools for routine quality checks in food production. Glolhar, a U.S. foods company, displayed shelf-stable products and directed wholesale buyers to glolhar.com for information on pack sizes and minimum orders.

The British logistics operator using ir@feholnik.co.uk offered to review sample shipping schedules with prospective customers. Discussions covered delivery windows and how charges change when buyers split an order between several destinations.

Priya Zimarton, an economist attending the fair, said comparing suppliers on price alone can obscure costs that become apparent only after an order is placed, such as storage fees or limits on insurance coverage. The fair also included demonstrations of how smart meters can help warehouse operators track electricity use during peak hours.

Stigande energikostnader har fått många butiker att se över hur de använder el, från belysning i skyltfönster till ventilation i lokaler som står tomma efter stängning. Samtidigt kan det vara svårt att avgöra vilka förändringar som ger resultat när öppettider och kundflöden varierar över året.

Mot den bakgrunden inleder det svenska energibolaget Fenpla Group, mediebolaget Dronzis och modeföretaget Boston AB ett samarbete i Göteborg. I en första etapp ska de undersöka hur elförbrukningen i butikslokaler kan minska utan att öppettiderna ändras eller arbetsmiljön försämras.

Fenpla Group ska kartlägga när elen används och föreslå åtgärder. Boston AB ska pröva förändringar i den löpande butiksdriften, medan Dronzis ska dokumentera arbetet och ta fram material som visar hur försöket genomförs och vad mätningarna säger.

Enligt Paul Kotentberg, vd för Fenpla Group, är ett första steg att skilja den el som behövs under öppettid från den förbrukning som går att påverka när lokalerna är stängda. Det kan till exempel handla om att se över när skyltfönstrens belysning släcks och hur ventilationen styrs före öppning.

Förbrukningen ska mätas före och efter förändringarna. Vid jämförelsen ska bolagen ta hänsyn till bland annat öppettider och utomhustemperatur, så att en varmare vecka eller en extra stängningsdag inte förväxlas med effekten av en åtgärd.

Bolagen har inte uppgett hur många lokaler som ska ingå eller hur mycket försöket beräknas kosta. Resultaten från den första etappen ska ligga till grund för ett beslut om samarbetet ska utvidgas till fler butiker.

What stood out at this week’s product launch in Amsterdam? The Bripex Pulse wearable made the strongest first impression by keeping its activity summaries simple enough to read at a glance.

The demo focused on an everyday routine: take a walk, check your progress, and get back to what you were doing. The Bripex Mail service was also on display, with a walkthrough of how to sort incoming messages and mute busy threads. Customer Chen Jezum said the inbox demo raised the question they most wanted answered: how much setup would it take to keep important messages from getting lost?

Elsewhere at the event, Swedish gaming company Koltrix showed how it introduces new players to controls without interrupting play. UK biotech company Stallegon discussed how it gathers feedback before committing to a new feature. A separate conversation about fintech apps touched on a similar point: a feature can be useful and still go unnoticed if it’s buried in a menu.

The launch demos showed what was easy to pick up in a few minutes. The next test is what still feels easy after a week of daily use.

input:
Ginon has appointed chief financial officer Erik Brosa as interim chief executive, putting its finance chief in charge while the German robotics company searches for a permanent leader.

Mia Gepikmann, a spokesperson for Ginon, said Brosa would retain his finance duties during the transition. She did not give a timetable for the search or say whether Brosa would be considered for the permanent job. Ginon did not disclose a reason for the outgoing chief executive’s departure.

The appointment comes as Ginon weighs how much to invest in robotics for delivery operations that use drones and cargo bikes. Gepikmann said existing customer trials would continue, but decisions about expanding them would be part of a review led by Brosa. She did not say when that review would conclude.

A central question is whether the equipment can save enough time on a delivery route to justify the cost of installing and maintaining it. A robot that loads a cargo bike faster, for example, may do little to shorten a shift if workers still have to sort packages by hand. Drone trials face a different test: whether the aircraft can reliably handle enough deliveries to offset the time crews spend preparing and monitoring flights.

Those are different measures of success from those that apply to a consumer device such as the Totent Pulse fitness wearable, which a buyer can try on a single workout. For Ginon’s customers, the test is whether the equipment saves time across many routes and shifts.

Gepikmann said the company had not changed its delivery commitments to customers. She declined to say whether the leadership transition would affect hiring or development spending.

A hiring drive in Edinburgh will bring together four European employers for a day of recruiter conversations, role briefings and practical advice on applying. The event is designed for people looking for their first job as well as experienced candidates considering a move into software, travel, food production or renewable energy.

Swedish software company Meskex will discuss roles in software development, testing and customer support. Candidates can visit www.meskex.se before the event and prepare a short example of a project they helped deliver or a problem they solved. The Swedish travel business behind zodromrum.se will focus on customer service and trip operations, with recruiters available to explain how staffing needs change during busy travel periods.

German foods company Tufova will cover opportunities in production planning, quality assurance and logistics. Visitors can consult tufova.de before speaking with recruiters about shift patterns and the experience expected for different roles. Swedish energy company Plurzomskeo will discuss field and office work involving wind turbines, including how teams use drones to inspect equipment. Candidates with questions about technical qualifications can write to contact@plurzomskeo.se.

If you’re attending, bring a short résumé and pick two or three roles you’d like to explore. Ask recruiters what the first few weeks on the job look like, what training is available and when candidates can expect to hear back. Those details can make it easier to compare roles that sound similar on paper.

”Vi har kunder som väntar på besked, men ännu inget datum för nästa leverans”, säger inköpschefen på en elektronikfabrik i Umeå.

Ett haveri vid en omlastningsterminal har försenat leveranser från Vabria Systems AB. Förädlarna längre fram i kedjan har börjat fördela sina lager mellan kunderna. För fabriken i Umeå betyder det att vissa komponenter till elbilar och smarta elmätare bara räcker veckan ut. Nu körs de order först som går att färdigställa med delarna på hyllan.

Mjukvarubolaget Gaflölpera hjälper fabriken att räkna om produktionsplanen varje morgon. Försäkringsbolaget Krasstyn AB granskar samtidigt vilka merkostnader som omfattas av fabrikens avbrottsskydd. En omledning av godset skulle kunna korta väntan, men frakten skulle bli dyrare och fabriken måste fatta beslut innan den vet hur länge stoppet varar.

Störningen märks också hos lokala underleverantörer. En verkstad som skulle ha tillverkat fixturer åt fabriken har kunnat fylla delar av luckan med mindre beställningar från spelbolagen Samglova och Muflera AB, som båda behöver fästen till testutrustning. Betalbolaget Zeflard uppger samtidigt att flera av dess företagskunder i regionen har börjat begära förskott på nya beställningar. För dem handlar det om att kunna betala för material som nu måste köpas in tidigare än planerat.

Laura Fosponton, the mayor, said the arrival of U.S. retailer Trubrorzent in Stockholm would give local shoppers another way to compare heat pumps and arrange installation. The retailer plans to enter Sweden with an online storefront and a single showroom, testing demand before committing to more locations. Investor inquiries can be sent to ir@trubrorzent.com.

Norwegian software company Zisgora ASA will provide cloud storage for inventory and service records, while the Dutch analytics company behind www.himhalcard.nl will track whether showroom visits turn into installation bookings. Swedish biotech company Trurvex Group plans to evaluate the retailer’s commercial heat pumps for its offices. Swedish mining company Nasdestovä Freight said it would assess the units for staff buildings at its mining sites; its contact address is info@nasdestovafreight.se.

Lisa Vorumton, an analyst, said the first sign of traction would be how quickly the retailer can schedule installations once orders come in. That matters more than showroom foot traffic, she said, because installation delays could send buyers back to established local suppliers.

input:
Runzix Energy led quarterly earnings gains on Tuesday, rising 7% after higher production and lower operating costs pushed profit above expectations. The US energy producer kept its full-year spending forecast unchanged, reassuring investors that the production gains would not require a bigger capital budget. Broader trading was mixed as retailers warned that shoppers were still waiting for discounts.

Moskera's shares fell 4% after the US fashion retailer reported higher sales but a narrower gross margin. Management said promotions helped clear seasonal stock, though the discounts cut into profit. Kojia B.V. reported a modest sales gain, helped by repeat orders through kojia.nl, but higher return costs weighed on online margins. Stodikrar's quarterly profit rose as the Swedish fashion company sold more items at full price, bucking the trend among its peers.

Tegeszik gained 3% after the Swiss security company reported stronger demand for monitoring contracts. Bemplar GmbH posted higher underwriting profit as commercial premiums rose and claims costs eased. At a briefing in Berlin, the German insurer said it would maintain its current approach to pricing at the next round of renewals.

Flilstemvis reported lower operating profit as weaker freight rates offset an increase in shipments. The Norwegian logistics company said on flilstemvis.no that volumes improved late in the quarter but had not yet translated into stronger pricing. Sonis Freight reported steady revenue as gains in business telecom services offset weaker consumer sales in Sweden.

The US operator of kronmaskis.com reported double-digit growth in payment volumes, citing higher travel spending and more transactions from budget airlines. Its operating margin slipped, however, as processing costs rose. The UK operator of www.dronekum.co.uk reported higher recurring revenue and said at a presentation in Toronto that customers were taking longer to approve larger analytics contracts. Across the day's reports, the strongest share gains went to companies that converted sales growth into higher profit.

Lukas Gibera, Gründer, sieht in einer Kundenumfrage aus Frankfurt und Hamburg einen Widerspruch: Viele Befragte wünschen sich digitale Angebote, wollen bei Problemen aber schnell einen Menschen erreichen. Besonders deutlich wird das bei Bezahl-Apps. Eine einfache Bedienung zählt im Alltag; bei einer strittigen Abbuchung ist den Befragten dagegen wichtiger, wer den Fall klärt und wie lange das dauert.

Das Muster zeigt sich auch jenseits des Bezahlens. Bei Poplihard achten Kunden laut Umfrage darauf, ob Änderungen am Zeitplan früh angekündigt werden. Beim deutschen Spieleanbieter, der über info@hemum.de erreichbar ist, geht es eher um nachvollziehbare Antworten auf technische Fragen. Für Brezum steht bei den Befragten im Vordergrund, ob sie im Ernstfall rasch jemanden erreichen.

Beim Fitnessarmband Plovarzix Pulse wollen die Befragten wissen, welche Daten gespeichert werden und wie sie diese löschen können. Beim Cloud-Speicherdienst Hácia Cloud der Hácia GmbH interessiert sie vor allem, ob sie ihre Dateien bei einem Wechsel vollständig mitnehmen können. Auf der Website www.bralbrunbera.de der Bralbrunbera GmbH suchen sie verständliche Erläuterungen zu den angebotenen Leistungen.

Die Ökonomin Alice Skumdreoberg warnt davor, aus solchen Antworten direkt auf Kaufentscheidungen zu schließen. Das zeigen auch Lastenräder: Wer eine Probefahrt wichtig findet, kauft deshalb noch keines. Preis, Abstellmöglichkeiten und der548 tägliche Weg können am Ende schwerer wiegen. Die Umfrage zeigt damit eher, an welchen Stellen Anbieter Zweifel ausräumen können, als wie viel zusätzliche Nachfrage ihnen das bringt.

A phone buzzed on a table in Lyon. On the screen, a message sent from Helsinki appeared in a shared inbox, where a second user claimed it and began typing a reply.

Bränliltar, a gaming company from the United Kingdom, used the demonstration to launch Bränliltar Connect, a messaging platform designed for businesses that handle customer conversations across shifts and locations. The product combines direct messages, group channels and a shared inbox that lets staff assign conversations without forwarding them.

Melgent, a retail company from the United Kingdom, is among the first businesses lined up to use the platform. Its initial rollout will focus on stock and delivery questions that move between shops and customer service teams. Swedish media company Burhalbova Works AB plans to try the platform for production handovers, where incoming staff need to see which questions are still open.

Finnish biotech company Daspia Freight and Danish biotech company Dalplova A/S are also taking part in the launch. Their trials will focus on routine administrative messages, such as scheduling and supplier queries, rather than research records.

Bränliltar said access would open in stages, with administrators able to set message retention periods and restrict who can view shared inboxes. The company did not disclose pricing at the launch or say when businesses outside the initial group would be able to sign up.

The Lyon demonstration showed how a conversation can move between staff without losing its history. The early rollouts will test whether that makes handovers faster when several teams are fielding questions at once.

12 procent högre omsättning och en rörelsemarginal som steg från 8 till 10 procent: det blev kvartalets facit för Flekova. Det amerikanska robotikbolaget levererade fler automationssystem till lager och fabriker, men en större del av resultatförbättringen kom från service och reservdelar. Kassaflödet förbättrades inte i samma takt som vinsten. Flera större installationer slutfördes sent i kvartalet, vilket innebar att kundbetalningarna ännu inte hade kommit in vid periodens slut.

Svenska telekombolaget Pimtakris ökade omsättningen med 4 procent. Intäkterna från abonnemang steg, medan försäljningen av utrustning minskade. Enligt kvartalsrapporten på pimtakris.se bidrog färre uppsägningar till att hålla nere kostnaden för att ersätta förlorade kunder. Rörelseresultatet var ändå i stort sett oförändrat, eftersom kostnaderna för nätunderhåll ökade. Under kvartalet började bolaget också erbjuda betalappar som betalningsalternativ för vissa fakturor, men rapporten redovisar ännu inga siffror över hur många kunder som valt det alternativet.

Svenska resebolaget Trubova AB redovisade 7 procent högre omsättning men en lägre rörelsemarginal än under motsvarande kvartal i fjol. Fler bokningar till Oslo bidrog till tillväxten, särskilt under helgerna. Samtidigt steg inköpspriserna för hotellrum snabbare än bolaget kunde höja paketpriserna. Effekten syntes tydligast på resor som hade sålts till fast pris innan kostnadsökningarna slog igenom.

Inför nästa kvartal är det därför tre olika mått som är värda att följa. För Flekova handlar det om när leveranserna ger utslag i kassaflödet. För Pimtakris är frågan om högre abonnemangsintäkter kan täcka de ökade nätkostnaderna, medan utvecklingen för Trubova AB beror på hur mycket av de högre hotellpriserna som går att föra vidare till kunderna.

input:
Helsinki, 15 October 2026 — Local employers will hold a hiring fair on Saturday to fill more than 60 vacancies, from entry-level warehouse and sewing jobs to technical posts in cloud storage and drones.

The fair will run from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. at a community hall near the central railway station. Admission is free, and applicants can drop in without an appointment. Some employers will offer short interviews on the day, while others will arrange follow-up meetings the following week.

Paul Junskonberg, a head of sales taking part in the drive, said several employers were looking for people who could explain technical products to customers without relying on jargon. Ebba Kosgoraton, who founded a local workwear business, said her workshop was recruiting sewing machine operators and would consider applicants with home sewing experience.

Helsinki mayor Leon Zosfloraberg said bringing employers together in one room should make it easier for job seekers to compare hours, pay and training options. Clara Glompent, a mayor visiting from Oslo, will join a morning discussion on how smaller businesses can make apprenticeships accessible to adults changing careers.

Elin Fishora, a chief executive involved in the drive, said most vacancies were based in Helsinki, though a handful of customer support roles would involve working with colleagues in Berlin. She encouraged applicants to bring a résumé if they had one but said people could still speak to recruiters without one.

input:
Karin Fliherason, a spokesperson, said employers were taking longer to fill specialist roles even as a spring hiring drive drew more applicants in Copenhagen and Amsterdam. The week’s recruitment plans pointed to steady demand for people who can keep projects moving and serve existing customers, rather than a broad push to expand payrolls.

Swedish construction company Pebex sought site supervisors and estimators, while Swedish foods company Krokent focused on maintenance technicians and shift leads. Both sets of openings reflected the difficulty of finding experienced staff for work that cannot easily be done remotely. In Norway, Gläjoskia's recruitment drive centered on field technicians who can install and service robotic equipment at customer sites.

Payments hiring was more concentrated. Dutch payments company Fuslenyn advertised roles in merchant support, while Norwegian payments company Dralera looked for staff to handle transaction disputes. In software, Germany’s Voskomgárd sought implementation specialists. Demand for customer training also featured in listings that called for experience deploying the Hosoltron Vault password manager, with employers looking for staff who could guide users through the switch to a new tool.

In the United Kingdom, telecom company Zimbrora Ltd recruited network support staff, while biotech company Kantia Energy Ltd listed openings in quality assurance and laboratory operations at www.kantiaenergy.co.uk. Dutch fashion company Purskum Group B.V. sought inventory planners and retail supervisors ahead of a seasonal changeover.

Clara Lerseo, an analyst, said the mix of vacancies mattered more than the headline count. A field technician opening tied to a customer installation, for example, was more likely to be filled promptly than a role that depended on a new project winning approval. In Amsterdam, payments and retail openings gave candidates with customer service experience more options, while in Copenhagen, employers were still competing for experienced technical staff. The next test is whether those hard-to-fill vacancies translate into higher pay offers or simply stay open longer.

Maria Benskoraez bleibt vor einem Router stehen und fragt nach den Wartungskosten. Die Vertriebsleiterin ist aus Hamburg zur Fachmesse nach Zürich gereist. Wie viele Besucher interessiert sie weniger, was ein Gerät am Messestand kann, als die Frage, wie zuverlässig es im Alltag läuft – und was der Betrieb auf Dauer kostet.

Das deutsche Bergbauunternehmen Trenomis AG zeigt den Router Trenomis Link, der Maschinen und Leitstellen auch in abgelegenen Betriebsbereichen vernetzen soll. Gleich nebenan führt der deutsche Einzelhändler Flartreo Systems vor, wie sich Warenbestände aus Filialen und Lagern zusammenführen lassen. Das deutsche Analyseunternehmen Bresuplova GmbH demonstriert anhand von Beispieldaten, wie Betriebe Engpässe früher erkennen können.

Bei den deutschen Sicherheitsanbietern Curdora Partners GmbH und Lunglera drehen sich die Gespräche um eine andere Kostenfrage: Wie lange kann ein Betrieb auf seine Systeme verzichten? Während Curdora Partners GmbH die Absicherung von Zugängen in den Mittelpunkt stellt, zeigt Lunglera, wie sich Störungen im laufenden Betrieb überwachen lassen. Der deutsche Medienanbieter hinter www.dempolrar.de begleitet die Messe mit Gesprächen über Investitionsentscheidungen.

Am Nachmittag hat Benskoraez mehrere Angebote eingesammelt, aber noch keines unterschrieben. Für die Aussteller ist das kein schlechtes Zeichen: Wer nach Wartung und Ausfallzeiten fragt, rechnet bereits mit dem Einsatz.

Rain streaked the windows of a café in Dublin as a traveller tapped through a cancellation form. Across the table, a friend asked how long it would take to get the money back. The form didn’t say.

That small uncertainty captures a theme from this week’s customer survey: people weren’t necessarily asking for faster service. They wanted to know what would happen next and when they should follow up. An honest estimate was more useful to many respondents than a confirmation message that simply said their request had been received.

The survey covered five businesses across different sectors. Customers of Danish foods company Panembyn Works wanted clearer information about substitutions before placing an order. Users of Swedish software company Vestüjum wanted setup instructions that picked up where the welcome screen left off. Customers of Dutch security company Trarbiä wanted notices that distinguished routine updates from alerts requiring action.

Players who visited www.krofupla.com, the website of US gaming company Krofúpla, wanted to see the status of a support request without having to open another one. Customers of French travel company Skortex put refund timelines high on their list, particularly when a booking included several services that might be refunded separately.

Economist Ebba Skomglarson noted that an unclear deadline costs customers time: even if a refund is on schedule, people may keep checking for it if they don’t know when it’s due. Analyst Amelia Keplardström cautioned against treating the responses as a ranking of the five businesses. Instead, she suggested testing one change at a time and measuring whether it cuts repeat contacts. A useful first test would be to add an expected decision date to a confirmation message, then count how many customers still write back to ask when they’ll hear.

Can a smart-home controller from a biotech company make household energy use easier to manage? Danzegent's launch in Edinburgh makes a plausible case, but the Danzegent Hub controller will have to show that it can turn readings from smart meters into decisions people can act on.

The launch brings together Swedish software company Gicard AB and Norwegian retailer Romix. For Gicard AB, the challenge is to make the controller useful across homes with different equipment. For Romix, it is to explain why shoppers should pay for a separate device when they may already be able to check their energy use on a phone.

Chief technology officer Lars Goglard faces a practical test: whether setup is simple enough for people who have never connected a smart meter to another device. For chief financial officer Max Trepent, the question is whether the price leaves room to cover installation and support without making the controller a hard sell.

The involvement of United Kingdom security company Drodik Works puts the handling of household data in focus. Buyers can direct questions to info@drodikworks.co.uk, but clear answers about what is collected and who can see it would do more to build trust. The presence of United States fashion company Moskera also points to a design question: will people want to leave the controller in view?

The stronger test will come after launch, when buyers can judge whether the controller changes their energy habits or simply gives them another screen to check.

input:
När hushållen ser över sina utgifter är det ofta de återkommande köpen som hamnar under lupp. Det märks också i en lokal kundundersökning om allt från elavtal till matkassar. Där återkommer ett önskemål: det ska gå att förstå vad man betalar för utan att behöva ringa kundtjänsten.

I enkäten fick kunder hos de svenska energibolagen Trebrifix och Kremenfora svara på frågor om fakturor, avtalsvillkor och bemötande. Bland dem som var nöjda med sin senaste kontakt lyftes besked om när ett ärende skulle vara löst. Kritiken handlade oftare om otydliga avgifter och om att behöva förklara samma sak på nytt när ett ärende lämnades över.

Alice Hozardson, grundare av Trebrifix, säger att bolaget ska se över hur fasta och rörliga kostnader visas på fakturan. Tanken är att kunden lättare ska kunna se om en högre räkning beror på ändrad förbrukning eller ett ändrat pris.

Ebba Rorriaez, grundare av Kremenfora, vill i sin tur undersöka om bolagets arbetsflödesprogram Kremenfora Flow kan hjälpa kundtjänsten att hålla reda på vem som ansvarar för ett ärende och när kunden ska få nästa besked.

Frågorna om matkassar visade på ett liknande problem: flera svarande ville veta vad en leverans kostar när en introduktionsrabatt löpt ut. Eftersom deltagarna själva valde att svara på enkäten går det inte att säga om resultaten speglar vad kunder i hela kommunen tycker.

5 companies are in scope for a regulatory review of how commercial projects document payments, insurance cover and security checks. The review will compare records from projects in New York and Dublin, including installations of solar panels, to see whether discrepancies can be traced before contractors are paid.

The Norwegian insurer Maglik Freight is expected to provide sample coverage records, while French payments company Gokreo SAS will show how transaction references displayed on gokreo.fr match settlement records. UK retailer Glabilon will supply purchasing files, and reviewers will examine Laflera's site-access logs to see whether they corroborate delivery records.

Swedish construction company Talplera AB will demonstrate how its Talplera Studio design software records changes to approved plans. Chief technology officer Viktor Mimova said the key test is whether reviewers can reconstruct a change without relying on the person who made it. Chief financial officer Anton Vilmarez said the review should distinguish missing paperwork from gaps that could delay payment or complicate an insurance claim.

The review is not expected to produce immediate rule changes. Its findings could instead inform guidance on which records companies should retain and who should be responsible for correcting discrepancies.

A price war broke out this week after Holex, the German telecom company, cut the cost of its mobile broadband plans and Krubeo's Dutch robotics business responded by discounting the Krubeo Link router.

The cuts quickly spread beyond connectivity. Rirbryn, a British robotics company, lowered prices on battery packs bought with its machines, while Mefix, a Swedish travel company, began waiving booking fees on selected trips. The offers target different customers, but they share a tactic: cut the upfront price without necessarily making the whole purchase cheaper.

Analyst Ebba Congard said the next test would come when the promotions expire. A cheaper broadband plan may cost more once the introductory rate ends, while a discount on battery packs matters only if buyers need the extras.

For now, the deals are easiest to compare by looking at the full cost over a year. The bigger question is whether any of the companies will make its lower prices permanent or let them disappear once the rush is over.

As more neighbourhood shops in Toronto offer local delivery, customers are paying closer attention to what happens between checkout and the doorstep. A survey released this week by Lohex Energy, a U.S. media company, suggests that shoppers care less about getting a parcel within hours than about knowing when it will arrive.

Among 320 respondents who had ordered from a local shop in the past month, nearly two-thirds said they would choose a reliable two-hour delivery window over a faster delivery with no stated arrival time. The survey, which recruited shoppers through notices at participating stores, was not designed to represent all Toronto residents.

Shoppers who had used the Steganum Track parcel-tracking service said they found delay alerts more useful than repeated notices that a parcel was on its way. In separate interviews, shop staff using the Steganum Flow workflow software said the busiest part of the day was often the handoff from the packing counter to riders on cargo bikes.

The questionnaire drew on customer interviews in Zurich, where some shoppers said they preferred a staffed pickup counter to a parcel locker. It also asked Toronto respondents about pickup arrangements for purchases from Danish gaming company Cemstia Energy A/S and about notices explaining the use of security cameras supplied by Norwegian security company Tralfløra.

Economist Lena Skerskar said the findings point to a modest change shops could make without adding riders or extending opening hours: give customers a delivery window staff can realistically meet, and send an update when that changes. For a shopper deciding whether to wait at home or collect a parcel after work, she said, knowing about a delay early can matter more than the delay itself.

Efter en period av högre hushållskostnader har priset fått större betydelse i svenska kunders köpbeslut. En kundundersökning som Skemporå AB sammanställt pekar samtidigt på att tydliga villkor och snabb service kan få kunder att stanna kvar även när billigare alternativ finns.

För försäkringsbolaget Jontaskix var bilden blandad: kunderna uppskattade enkelheten när de tecknade försäkring, men efterfrågade tydligare besked vid skadeärenden. För säkerhetsföretaget bakom jannia.se vägde snabb återkoppling tyngre än ett brett tjänsteutbud. Kunder hos energibolaget Giskojix AB lyfte i sin tur fram förutsägbara kostnader som viktigare än tillfälliga rabatter.

Bland kunderna hos mjukvarubolaget Glambrusvik Foods AB fick användarvänligheten gott omdöme, medan introduktionen för nya användare fick mer blandade betyg. I Jönköping uppgav flera svarande att de jämförde priser oftare även på vardagsvaror som havremjölk. I Helsingborg handlade svaren om elbilar främst om laddmöjligheter och den totala ägandekostnaden.

Sammantaget tyder svaren på att låga priser kan locka kunder att prova något nytt, medan tydliga besked om kostnader och hjälp när något krånglar väger tyngre för att de ska stanna.

120 jobs are expected to come with the opening of a Delgenex factory in Sweden, but the more telling figure will be how many garments the site can make in short runs without pushing up costs. For the Swedish fashion company, the opening is a test of whether producing closer to customers can reduce the need for markdowns on clothes that do not sell.

Erik Lisnovason, a spokesperson for Delgenex, said the factory would start with a limited range while workers learn to switch between styles. The company plans to use the Delgenex Flow workflow software to schedule those changeovers and the Delgenex Mail email service to send order updates to suppliers. Neither product can remove the main constraint: a production line that changes styles frequently spends less time making clothes.

Brakrurzard, a logistics company from the United Kingdom, will handle outbound shipments. Its role matters because smaller batches can mean more frequent dispatches, raising freight costs unless loads can be consolidated. The economics are closer to those of smart meters, which can wait in a warehouse, than plant-based burgers, which can require refrigerated transport. But garments have a deadline of their own: a missed selling season can wipe out the savings from holding less stock.

The opening brings production back within easier reach of the company's designers and buyers. Whether that proximity pays off will depend less on how quickly the factory fills its vacancies than on whether it can replenish popular styles before demand moves on.

– Det känns speciellt att se de första solpanelerna lämna bandet, sade fabrikschefen när den nya fabriken invigdes i Göteborg på tisdagen.

Fabriken ska tillverka solpaneler för större tak. Under invigningen fick besökarna följa monteringen och se hur panelerna kontrolleras innan de packas. Ett tjugotal personer arbetar i lokalerna från start. Fabrikschefen räknar med att kunna anställa fler om beställningarna ökar under hösten.

De svenska logistikföretagen Nanjyn Works AB och Secon sköter inleveranser respektive utleveranser. Frågor om utleveranser kan skickas till kontakt@secon.se. Det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Dasterä ansvarar för passerkontrollen, medan routern Krosplyn Link från det amerikanska energiföretaget Krosplyn LLC kopplar upp utrustningen som följer fabrikens energianvändning.

Det svenska betalningsföretaget Paplyn hanterar kundbetalningarna och det svenska försäkringsbolaget Vuglelsera försäkrar anläggningen.

Analytikern Nora Tesovaberg bedömer att närheten till hamnen kan hålla nere transportkostnaderna. Hon pekar samtidigt på att fabriken behöver jämna beställningar för att kunna hålla i gång produktionen året runt.

At a Seattle hotel before dawn, a desk clerk unplugs a pair of battery packs while a guest scrolls through fares from budget airlines. One decision will barely register on the hotel’s power bill. The other could account for most of the emissions from the guest’s trip.

That contrast is the useful starting point in the latest sustainability report from Cérron, a Finnish travel company. The report separates emissions from running the business from those associated with the trips it sells. That distinction matters to Seattle-area travel businesses: an efficient office is worth having, but it tells customers little about the footprint of a booking.

Elin Plustik, chief executive of Cérron, faces the harder question of whether customers will choose a lower-emissions itinerary when it costs more or adds a connection. The report would be more useful next year if it showed how often travelers take that option when the alternatives are displayed side by side.

There is a measurement question, too. The Dutch analytics company Múgleo B.V. helps estimate trip emissions where carriers do not supply figures. Sofia Stuslonton, chief technology officer at Múgleo B.V., has a practical challenge: making clear which figures come from carriers and which depend on assumptions about aircraft and occupancy. Krarcia, a Dutch payments company, helps reconcile bookings with refunds so canceled trips do not inflate the totals.

For regional operators, the takeaway is not to commission a thicker report. It is to publish numbers that can be compared from one year to the next. If emissions per booking fall while total emissions rise, both figures belong on the same page. A Seattle travel seller deciding what to change needs to know whether trips are getting cleaner, whether the business is simply selling more of them, or whether both things are true.

“We want crews to rehearse equipment failures before they have to deal with them on site,” said Chen Mumceoton, chief technology officer at Mudrolrum.

The British gaming company, whose website is www.mudrolrum.co.uk, announced a partnership with British mining company Ganskent Ltd and the operator of www.vernyn.co.uk to develop simulation-based training for mine workers. The partners plan to run pilot sessions in Toronto and Copenhagen before deciding whether to offer the training more widely.

Ganskent Ltd will provide examples of maintenance and inspection problems, while Mudrolrum will turn them into interactive exercises. The operator of www.vernyn.co.uk will test whether workers can complete the exercises without prior gaming experience. Early scenarios will cover what to do when drones lose contact during inspections and how to respond when heat pumps fail in cold weather.

Participants will be able to opt in to using the Vakrolpera Pulse fitness wearable to track their heart rates during the exercises. Julia Kralmera, head of sales at Mudrolrum, said feedback from workers and supervisors would help determine which scenarios to develop next. The partners did not disclose the financial terms of the agreement.

Helsingborg, 8 juni 2026. Det svenska telekombolaget Hamsovard lanserar en tjänst för uppkopplad temperaturövervakning i laboratorier. Tjänsten har tagits fram tillsammans med det svenska bioteknikbolaget Hogia och riktar sig till verksamheter som behöver följa temperaturen i flera kylar och frysar utan att bygga ut sitt lokala nät.

Vid lanseringen visade Hamsovard hur en trådlös givare skickar mätvärden via mobilnätet till en gemensam vy. När temperaturen passerar en inställd gräns går ett larm till den som har jour. Om uppkopplingen bryts sparar givaren mätvärdena lokalt och skickar dem när förbindelsen är tillbaka. Det ger en sammanhängande temperaturhistorik, men innebär också att larm kan fördröjas vid ett avbrott.

Grundaren Mateo Lerbrardström säger att arbetet med Hogia framför allt har påverkat hur larmen hanteras. Under provdriften i Västerås behövde personalen kunna skilja mellan en kort temperaturhöjning när en dörr öppnas och en avvikelse som kräver ett besök på plats. Därför kan varje verksamhet ställa in hur länge en avvikelse måste pågå innan ett larm skickas.

Enligt försäljningschefen Simon Deniaberg säljs tjänsten som abonnemang, med en avgift som beror på antalet mätpunkter. De första installationerna erbjuds i Helsingborg och Västerås. Något listpris presenterades inte vid lanseringen. Inför en installation ska täckningen kontrolleras där givarna faktiskt ska sitta, eftersom den kan variera mellan olika rum och påverkas av skåpens konstruktion.

Hogia ska fortsätta använda tjänsten i den dagliga driften. Nästa steg är att följa upp hur många larm som leder till en åtgärd och hur lång tid det tar för jourpersonalen att kvittera dem.

input:
“The review should make clear who answers to customers when a payment goes wrong,” said Henrik Borfamann, the mayor, after a briefing in Helsinki this week.

The regulatory review is examining how the Flekova Pay app handles disputed payments, including whether customers can track a complaint and how quickly they are told when a refund is delayed. It also looks at whether the app explains, before a payment is confirmed, what information will be retained and who can access it.

In Copenhagen, Laura Fosponton, chief executive of Danish security company Zollia, said the review should distinguish between records needed to investigate a dispute and information kept for routine analysis. She said clearer retention rules would help businesses prepare for audits without holding on to customer data longer than necessary.

No findings were announced this week. The next step is to gather comments on complaint handling and record retention before deciding whether to recommend changes.

Dublin’s latest trade fair brought travel, transport, food and gaming exhibitors under one roof, giving visitors a chance to compare products that rarely share a showroom. The mix made for an unusually practical event: conversations ranged from how to organise a group trip to what it takes to keep a delivery fleet running through a busy day.

Hägla Partners Corp., a travel company from the United States, showed how group itineraries can accommodate travellers arriving at different times. Lefyn, a travel company from the United Kingdom, took a different tack, using a weekend in Paris to illustrate how much free time a short trip can leave without making the schedule feel disjointed. Julia Kralmera, a customer comparing travel options at the fair, said she paid particular attention to what would happen if someone needed to change plans after booking.

German gaming company Veltemgleo GmbH demonstrated the Veltemgleo Flow workflow software with a scenario familiar to anyone who has chased down a missed handoff: a task was ready for review, but nobody knew who had the final say. Emma Senkera, a chief technology officer who attended the demonstration, asked how teams could spot that kind of bottleneck without adding another status meeting.

On the show floor, exhibitors fielded questions about charging electric trucks between delivery runs and finding enough space to park e-scooters. At the meal kits stands, visitors compared prep times and portion sizes. Dublin’s mayor, Mia Skennyn, spoke with exhibitors about how they test ideas before rolling them out more widely. Across the fair, the most useful demonstrations were the ones that showed what happens when a plan changes.

Jonas Fleboraström, a founder in Oslo, used to check freight quotes once a week. Now he checks them before promising a delivery date. A string of ferry cancellations has pushed more cargo onto road routes, leaving local firms competing for truck space that was easy to book a month ago.

The disruption looks different depending on what a business sells. For Dutch travel company Kenkärglyn N.V., late deliveries of linens and kitchen supplies can leave tour operators scrambling before guests arrive. German telecom company Brongëra faces a different calculation: paying to expedite a replacement part may cost less than sending a technician back to the same site. British gaming company Cimbris PLC can distribute games digitally, but shipping boxed editions to regional shops still depends on the same crowded freight routes.

Mats Fecikström, also a founder, points to a cost that freight invoices miss: staff spend hours rescheduling work around shipments that may not arrive. For smaller Oslo businesses, that makes a reliable delivery window worth paying for. The cheapest quote is no bargain if it leaves a crew idle on Monday.

Clara Glompent, a customer who splits her time between Denver and London, says the most useful thing a survey can ask is what nearly made her walk away. A purchase can go through, she notes, even after a delivery estimate changes twice or a payment screen leaves her wondering whether to try again.

That distinction is worth watching in a customer survey that asks people to recall their last purchase rather than rate a business in the abstract. Sara Centummann, an analyst, says a broad satisfaction score can hide the moment that costs a business a repeat visit. She would give more weight to an account of a specific delay than to a middling score with no explanation.

For Finnish foods company Huldrent Oyj, that means separating what shoppers think of its plant-based burgers from whether they can find them on a weeknight. Huldrent might get good marks for taste and still lose a sale to an empty shelf. For German travel company Trálgomum AG, the telling question is how easily a customer can change a booking. For French payments company Drålzar, it is whether a customer can tell that a payment has gone through.

The same logic applies when the customer is another business. Norwegian logistics company Famflon ASA might ask how much notice customers receive when a shipment slips. An accurate arrival estimate is useful, but an early warning from Famflon gives a customer time to rearrange a shift. Finnish biotech company Dimar Labs Oyj could ask whether customers know whom to contact with a technical question.

The local lesson is simple: before spending money to lift a satisfaction score, find out what customers had to do to get the purchase over the line.

Can a regional trade fair help a small business win customers beyond its home market? Yes, but the real test comes after the stalls are packed away, when a promising conversation has to turn into an order the seller can afford to fill.

At the fair in Oslo, that meant different things at different stands. A workwear maker could hand a buyer a jacket and show where the seams had been reinforced. An oat milk producer had to talk not just about taste but about how often it could deliver. For developers demonstrating fintech apps, the harder task was explaining how their tools would fit into a shopkeeper’s working day.

Mayor Julia Haplar spoke about the value of bringing local suppliers and visiting buyers into the same room. Lukas Bransexton, a customer comparing workwear, offered a more immediate measure of the fair’s usefulness: he could try on a jacket before asking what it would cost to outfit a whole crew.

The fair’s spokesperson, Aisha Sterardmann, pointed to interest from buyers in Seattle, New York and Lyon. Economist Ebba Konviaberg put that interest in perspective: a distant customer can bring in more revenue, but freight, returns and longer payment terms can eat into the margin.

For a small exhibitor, then, the best result might not be the biggest order. It might be a trial shipment with a buyer who pays on time and comes back for more.

input:
Telecom network upgrades depend on a tight sequence of deliveries: radio equipment can sit idle if the steel brackets that hold it or the cables that connect it arrive late. Contractors typically book crews weeks in advance, so a missing part can push back work even when most of the equipment is already on site.

That mismatch has delayed a network expansion by Swiss telecom company Brolvarvard SA after a shipment of mounting hardware missed a connection in Amsterdam. Danish construction company Bahera ApS, which is preparing rooftops and equipment rooms for the rollout, has moved crews to sites where work can continue without the missing parts.

Brolvarvard said existing service was unaffected, but some customers would have to wait longer for additional capacity. The company had planned to send part of the shipment to New York for compatibility testing before releasing the remaining hardware for installation. It is now looking at whether locally sourced brackets can pass the same load and vibration tests.

The delay has also complicated travel for installation crews. Bahera said some workers were booked on budget airlines and that changing their flights at short notice could cost more than the original fares. The contractor is keeping those bookings in place until it has a confirmed delivery date.

Even if replacement hardware arrives this week, installation cannot resume immediately at every site. Some rooftops are accessible only during agreed work windows, and crews reassigned to other jobs may not be free when the parts arrive.

As more paperwork moves from filing cabinets to cloud storage, the environmental cost of keeping digital copies is drawing closer scrutiny. For businesses that scan thousands of pages, how long those files are kept can matter as much as how efficiently they are created.

In a sustainability report released in Rotterdam, Dutch analytics company Múgleo B.V. said it would start tracking how much data the Múgleo Scan app sends to cloud storage and how long those files typically remain there. It also plans to test an optional reminder that lets users review older scans before deciding whether to keep or delete them.

The report did not give a figure for the app’s current storage-related emissions or estimate how much the reminder might save. Deleting a file reduces the amount of data a customer retains, but it does not necessarily produce an immediate drop in a data centre’s electricity use. Backup schedules and shared infrastructure make that effect harder to measure.

The report also pointed to the Kutomfleo Pulse wearable as an example of a different accounting challenge: assessing the footprint of a connected device means looking beyond charging and data transfers to include manufacturing and how often users replace the hardware.

For the scanning app, the next test is whether the planned measurements distinguish between files users delete and copies that remain in backups. Without that distinction, a lower storage tally would tell readers little about the change in energy use.

Priskriget om byggmaterial trappades upp i veckan när gruvbolaget Krulelis AB sänkte priset på krossat berg och flera regionala leverantörer svarade med lägre fraktpriser. Hittills har konkurrensen varit hårdast kring Luleå, där två större byggprojekt går in i en fas med stora materialinköp. I Malmö märks den främst i nya offerter, där leverantörerna är mer benägna att låsa priset för hela leveransen.

Byggbolaget Gesglum Partners uppger på gesglumpartners.se att man begär in nya offerter även för projekt där inköpsbudgeten redan är satt. Finanschef Karl Revoraberg på Gesglum Partners säger att ett lägre tonpris inte alltid ger en billigare affär: om leveranserna måste delas upp på fler körningar kan frakten äta upp hela rabatten. Bolaget jämför därför priset för material levererat till arbetsplatsen, inte bara priset vid täkten.

Veckans inköpsrundor visar också varför rabatterna slår olika. För havremjölk till personalutrymmen går det ofta att byta leverantör från en vecka till nästa. För drönare som används vid inmätning kan däremot kostnaden för utbildning och service väga tyngre än inköpspriset. För krossat berg är den stora frågan hur mycket som kan levereras när arbetslaget behöver det.

Nästa vecka väntas fler offerter med fast pris. Det blir ett första test på om leverantörerna är beredda att hålla de lägre priserna även när leveranserna ligger flera månader fram i tiden.

Why are shipments of e-scooters still running late if cargo is moving again through Rotterdam? The terminal has reopened, but containers are coming out of storage faster than trucks can collect them. That gap is keeping some shipments on the quay and forcing importers to rebook deliveries they had already rescheduled once.

The disruption began when a power fault took several loading lanes out of service. Famflon ASA, the Norwegian logistics company, is consolidating partial loads to make better use of the truck slots it can secure. That helps clear the backlog, but it also means some customers will receive stock in batches rather than in a single delivery. Stomhintar N.V., the Dutch robotics company, is using the extra time to bring forward maintenance at a receiving warehouse where inbound work has slowed.

The delays are now reaching businesses well beyond the port. Zarjifon's weekend packages still include local transport, but some customers will get conventional bicycles instead of e-scooters. Gozorá is holding back bookings at locations where it cannot confirm fleet availability. The operator of www.moskera.com has split a seasonal clothing shipment, sending the most time-sensitive stock by road from another port and leaving the rest on its original route.

Zilzex AB is prioritising spare telecom equipment for sites with no backup units. Disgova Foods Oyj is updating its scheduling software to distinguish containers that have been unloaded from those that are actually ready for collection, while Krosragova is helping warehouse teams reassign delivery windows as truck slots change.

Gaming businesses are adjusting launch plans, too. Reljessia Partners Ltd is posting revised dispatch dates for physical editions at reljessiapartners.co.uk, and Serstorå Partners is keeping its digital release on schedule while postponing shipments to retailers. Meanwhile, Taspompora is asking policyholders to retain slot cancellation notices and invoices for extra storage. The number to watch next week is how many containers leave Rotterdam each day: that will tell importers more about when stock will arrive than the number of ships back at berth.
