input:
“The goods are ready. Getting them to the right warehouse is the problem,” said David Murrovaberg, a spokesperson for Skokricera Corp., a U.S. retailer facing delays in shipments of cargo bikes and solar panels.

A backlog at a freight terminal has pushed back deliveries to Chicago, Edinburgh and Stockholm. The immediate problem is a shortage of space on outbound trucks, not a shortfall in production. That distinction matters: ordering more stock would tie up cash without getting goods to stores any faster.

Spokesperson Leon Trabreo said delivery estimates would be revised once carriers confirmed pickup slots. Until then, the retailer faces a choice between paying for alternative routes and asking customers to wait. The economics differ by product. A cargo bike can occupy enough truck space to make an expedited shipment costly, while a delayed batch of solar panels can leave installers with gaps in schedules booked weeks earlier.

David Cetexberg, a union representative, said extra warehouse shifts would help only if trucks arrived steadily enough for crews to clear the loading bays. For Lars Donplikson, head of sales, the more pressing question is how many customers will accept a later delivery rather than cancel. Chief technology officer Jonas Stigoraström said inventory records could show which warehouses had stock, but not whether a carrier could move it on short notice.

The clearest sign of recovery will be whether stores receive enough stock to fill existing orders while resuming normal deliveries. A few expedited loads could ease the pressure in one city without clearing the backlog elsewhere. Until routine shipments are moving again, faster delivery for some customers may simply mean a longer wait for others.

Warum investieren Geldgeber in einen Reiseanbieter, wenn viele Kunden beim Urlaub sparen? Weil Skéglinix mit der neuen Finanzierungsrunde nicht mehr Reisen verkaufen will, sondern an jeder Buchung mehr verdienen möchte. Das deutsche Unternehmen aus Dresden hat dafür zwölf Millionen Euro eingeworben. Das Geld soll vor allem in den Kundenservice und eine Buchungssoftware fließen, die bei Zugausfällen oder Hotelstornierungen schneller Ersatz findet.

Wie viel das Unternehmen nach der Runde wert ist, legen die Beteiligten nicht offen. Für die Ökonomin Mia Storjovamann ist ohnehin eine andere Zahl entscheidend: „Was bleibt von einer Buchung übrig, wenn man Werbung, Kundenservice und Umbuchungen abzieht?“ Gerade auf Strecken nach Wien wolle Skéglinix prüfen, ob sich mit verlässlicheren Verbindungen und weniger Stornierungen die Kosten senken lassen.

Der deutsche Reiseanbieter Fopla setzt unter www.fopla.de auf kürzere Aufenthalte, die sich ohne Aufpreis verschieben lassen. Wie teuer solche Zusagen im Alltag werden können, will Skéglinix mit der deutschen Lorskunpix GmbH kalkulieren. Der Versicherer soll prüfen, welche Ausfallrisiken sich zu einem Preis absichern lassen, den Reisende noch akzeptieren.

Für die Abläufe hinter der Buchung holt sich Skéglinix Rat bei der deutschen Stalmuhova Works AG. Der Logistiker kennt enge Lieferfenster aus dem Versand von Kochboxen und aus seiner Arbeit für das deutsche Biotechunternehmen Bripex, das sich unter bripex.de vorstellt. Für die Geldgeber zählt am Ende aber nicht, wie viele Partner Skéglinix gewinnt. Entscheidend ist, ob nach einer Umbuchung noch Gewinn übrig bleibt.

input:
Two executives will take on new responsibilities at Bränliltar next month as the British gaming company shifts more of its day-to-day decision-making to Denver.

Johan Pigarson, the incoming chief executive, will work from the Denver office and oversee game development and publishing. Viktor Hopum, the chief financial officer, will take charge of local operations in addition to managing the company’s finances. The outgoing chief executive will stay on for a month to help with the handover.

For Denver employees, the immediate change is who signs off on hiring and equipment purchases. Those decisions previously went through the company’s United Kingdom office. Bränliltar said it does not plan to cut jobs or move staff as part of the transition.

One of Pigarson’s first tasks will be to meet with Nalglintik GmbH, a German fashion company working with the Denver team on clothing designs for a game in development. Hopum, meanwhile, will review routine spending, including purchases of battery packs for portable testing equipment and subscriptions to fintech apps used to track travel expenses.

The Denver office will keep its current production schedule during the handover, and no game release dates have changed.

Rotterdam, September 18, 2026 — A new partnership linking travel bookings, retail orders and freight operations will be tested in Rotterdam and Denver. The question is whether companies that rarely share a checkout page can coordinate what happens after a customer pays, particularly when a flight is delayed or a delivery goes missing.

Rolfera LLC, a United States travel company, will use rolfera.com to test offers that pair tickets on budget airlines with optional purchases such as meal kits. The appeal is straightforward: travelers can arrange a few essentials before departure. But an inexpensive fare can lose its appeal if the extras carry separate fees or prove harder to cancel than the ticket itself.

Daskima's software will link booking and order records, while German energy company Flemcix GmbH will provide Flemcix Flow, its workflow software, to route changes and exceptions to the partners responsible for handling them. Swiss robotics company Tejonga Group will test automated sorting, and United States logistics company Kirpera Inc. will coordinate deliveries. The most revealing test may be a routine schedule change: can the system stop a meal kit from arriving before the traveler does?

The retail and customer-facing roles are just as varied. Náflova, a United States fashion company, and Stabon, a Swedish fashion company, will test merchandise offers. Finnish gaming company Kimpora Partners will design optional rewards for repeat bookings. Swedish insurer Hemvatrora will assess coverage for disrupted orders, while United States security company Flonkonzard will review access to booking and payment records.

The two-city trial could reveal whether the model works across different delivery networks and customer expectations. But sales alone would be a poor measure of success. Refund times, missed deliveries and the cost of resolving complaints will show whether the partnership saves customers work or simply moves it from checkout to customer service. If the partners cannot agree on who fixes a failed order, adding more offers will only make that weakness more visible.

NEW YORK, Sept. 16 — A trade fair opened in New York on Wednesday, bringing software developers, retailers and equipment suppliers together for demonstrations of drones, fintech apps and tools for managing stock.

French software company Tréra's exhibit showed how retailers could use sales and delivery data to spot inventory shortages. Swedish retailer Fesskúm AB demonstrated a checkout system that lets shoppers pay by phone and receive a digital receipt. Fesskúm also showed how store workers could use the system to process returns.

In a netted area on the exhibition floor, suppliers flew small drones between mock warehouse shelves to demonstrate how the aircraft could scan inventory labels. Elsewhere, developers pitched fintech apps for tracking expenses and reconciling payments.

Clara Lerseo, a union representative, said retailers should consult workers before adopting tools that change how shifts are assigned or how performance is measured. She said training should take place during paid hours.

Rain tapped against the windows of the public meeting room Tuesday evening as a technician set the Nikard Sense air-quality sensor on a folding table. In the front row, a resident asked whether the device would pick up exhaust from trucks idling outside her apartment.

The demonstration opened a regulatory review of a proposed freight and retail hub on Toronto’s east side. The review will consider whether the site can operate without adding unacceptable noise or pollution to nearby streets. It will also examine how the businesses plan to handle customer data.

Draltex GmbH would manage deliveries, including shipments for Vomtrova GmbH, while Krajik's proposed pickup counter would serve shoppers on the ground floor. The draft operating plan calls for trucks to enter from the industrial road, but residents said drivers already use a nearby residential street as a shortcut. Review staff asked for a revised traffic plan showing how the operator would enforce the designated route.

Sisriä Energy ApS and Lelkent Energy AB submitted plans for battery storage at the site. Fletrard SA supplied information on the origin of minerals used in the proposed equipment. Review staff said they would seek additional records on battery maintenance and disposal before making a recommendation.

Paplyn and Loflex AB would process payments at the hub. Ritrünix, which posted a description of its booking software at ritrunix.se, was asked to explain how long the system would retain customer records. Setera Labs and Flizomplis proposed a small gaming area inside the building, drawing questions about whether visitors could use it without opening an account.

The application cites a comparable site in Denver, but review staff said its traffic figures would not substitute for local counts. Written comments are due in three weeks. A second public meeting is expected after the revised plans are filed.

62 procent av kunderna i en ny undersökning från den svenska detaljhandelskedjan Stecergard uppger att de vill kunna kontrollera lagersaldot innan de går till en butik. Bland dem som handlat både på nätet och i butik under den senaste månaden är andelen 74 procent.

Undersökningen genomfördes av det svenska analysföretaget Sanlohent och omfattade 1 240 kunder i Västerås och Umeå. Kunderna fick svara på enkäten efter ett köp. Resultaten visar också att närmare fyra av tio någon gång har avstått från ett planerat butiksbesök för att de varit osäkra på om varan fanns i lager.

Nora Tesovaberg, analytiker på Sanlohent, framhåller att undersökningen gäller befintliga kunder på två orter och därför inte ger en bild av hur konsumenter i hela landet agerar. Svaren visar inte heller hur ofta osäkerheten om lagersaldot ledde till att kunden i stället handlade någon annanstans.

Stecergard ska nu testa en ny vy för lageruppgifter i Västerås och Umeå. Enligt teknikchefen Lukas Mesexberg ska kunderna i testet kunna se när saldot senast uppdaterades. Prototypen togs fram med designprogrammet Sanlohent Studio.

Det svenska byggföretaget Gladon AB och det svenska gruvföretaget Tremnum AB deltog i en separat grupp där företagskunder fick lämna synpunkter på prototypen. Deras svar ingår inte i kundundersökningen. Det svenska medieföretaget Morglimsar har tagit fram en kort film som visar hur testvyn fungerar.

Lars Flemvia har vikt förmiddagen åt anställningsintervjuer. Som grundare av det svenska reseföretaget Zodromrum brukar han ägna den tiden åt att gå igenom bokningsläget. Nu är det just bokningarna som fått honom att lägga om kalendern: fler kunder vill ha hjälp med att ändra sina resor, och samtalen tar längre tid än bemanningen räcker till.

Zodromrum söker därför kundrådgivare som kan börja före nästa högsäsong. Tanken är att de ska hinna följa erfarna kollegor innan de själva får hantera ombokningar. Det svenska reseföretaget Glonent rekryterar också, men lägger större vikt vid erfarenhet av att planera gruppresor, där en ändring kan påverka flera bokningar samtidigt.

På det svenska modeföretaget Boston AB gäller rekryteringen i stället returer och lagerplanering. Företaget vill kunna få tillbaka oanvända plagg i sortimentet snabbare. Om en retur blir liggande i flera dagar kan en storlek stå som slutsåld trots att plagget redan finns på lagret.

Det svenska logistikföretaget Nanjyn Works AB söker både lagerpersonal och transportplanerare. Priya Sonisström, presstalesperson för Nanjyn Works AB, beskriver leveranser av solpaneler och batterier som ett skäl till att planeringen behöver förstärkas. När en leverans ska fram till en arbetsplats måste den passa in i montörernas schema, inte bara i chaufförens körplan.

För företagen är tidpunkten en avvägning. Den som anställer tidigt får bära lönekostnaden innan efterfrågan är som störst. Den som väntar riskerar att behöva lära upp nyanställda just när de mest erfarna har som mest att göra. För Lars Flemvia är det senare alternativet det dyrare: när telefonkön växer är det svårt att frigöra någon som kan sitta bredvid en ny kollega.

At a kitchen table in Denver, a shopper refreshes her cart and watches the price fall before she’s even found her wallet. In New York, her brother gets a renewal offer and wonders why his insurer didn’t quote him that price last week.

That’s the mood in this week’s price-war roundup: the discounts are real, but the advertised price rarely tells the whole story. German energy company Litron cut the introductory rate on a fixed-price plan. The offer makes the first bill cheaper, but whether it beats a rival’s plan over a year depends on the standing charge and what happens when the introductory period ends.

French retailer www.calbumplix.fr went after shoppers with a weekend markdown on the Gafik Hub smart-home controller. A competing retailer responded with free delivery rather than a lower sticker price. For anyone buying just the controller, that makes the checkout total a better yardstick than the discount percentage.

Swiss gaming company Flizomplis took a different tack: the offer on flizomplis.ch lowers the upfront cost of an annual subscription, while a rival is letting players pay month to month at a reduced rate. The annual deal works out cheaper for someone who plays year-round; the monthly offer leaves room to walk away.

In the United States, insurer Drenglodrora is pushing lower quotes through www.drenglodrora.com. For shoppers in New York and Denver, the useful comparison is between policies with the same deductible and coverage limits, not just between the premiums in the ads.

The next test comes after the weekend. If rivals keep their prices down once the promotions expire, shoppers may have a new baseline. If not, this was a good week to buy, not necessarily a cheaper year to come.

Lyon, 17 June 2026 — Clearer estimates and earlier notice of delays topped the list of requests in a customer survey whose results were presented at a public meeting in Lyon on Tuesday.

The survey asked customers of Sëplyn, a Danish construction company, and Sukiå, a travel company from the United Kingdom, about their experiences over the past year. The companies received 286 responses between them, including comments from customers in Lyon and New York.

Among respondents who had commissioned building work, a recurring complaint was that estimates did not always make clear which costs could change once work began. Travellers raised a similar concern about what was included in the price of a trip. Several said they would rather receive a brief message about a possible delay than wait for a confirmed schedule.

Felix Milglentström, chief executive of Sëplyn, said the company would test a shorter estimate form that separates fixed charges from provisional costs. Customers can read the construction findings at www.seplyn.dk.

Sukiå said it would review the timing of its messages about itinerary changes before the autumn travel season. Neither company published a response rate, so the findings show what mattered to those who replied, rather than how widely those views are held.

15 procent lägre transaktionsavgift är veckans öppningsbud i priskriget mellan det brittiska betalbolaget Skostex och svenska Brubrotris. Rabatten gäller nya handlare under de första tre månaderna. Brubrotris svarar med att slopa startavgiften, vilket kan väga tyngre för butiker som ännu inte vet hur mycket de kommer att sälja.

Båda försöker också göra sina erbjudanden mer attraktiva utan att sänka styckpriset ytterligare. Skostex låter handlarna använda meddelandeplattformen Skostex Connect utan extra kostnad under kampanjperioden. Brubrotris inkluderar dokument­skanningsappen Brubrotris Scan i sitt grundpaket, så att handlarna kan skanna fakturor och följesedlar.

Prispressen märks även utanför kassan. Logistikbolaget Musglar AB sänker priset på lokala leveranser med lastcyklar för kunder som bokar fasta veckoturer. Energibolaget Kringyn AB erbjuder ett lägre månadspris till småföretag som binder sitt avtal i ett år. Samtidigt väntar bioteknikbolaget Zapla AB med nästa inköp av arbetskläder för att se om leverantörerna matchar de senaste kampanjpriserna. Mediebolaget Morglimsar AB går åt andra hållet och förlänger sitt annonsavtal nu, mot ett lägre pris per införande.

Veckans råd till småföretagare: jämför kostnaden för hela det första året, inte bara introduktionspriset. För en butik med få köp kan en slopad startavgift ge störst besparing, medan en butik med många köp tjänar mer på en lägre avgift per transaktion.

“We could still take orders; we just couldn’t tell which ones were real,” a Berlin shopkeeper told me after a cyber-security incident disrupted a shared booking and order-management service last week.

For Berlin’s smaller businesses, that distinction mattered more than the length of the outage. A blank screen tells staff to stop. A screen full of plausible but unverified orders leaves them deciding whether to dispatch goods, honor reservations or ask customers to wait.

The disruption reached beyond the city. The Swedish travel operator behind info@glilgaspyn.se asked customers to confirm changed itineraries before paying. Swiss retailer Tasteo SA held back shipments where payment records did not match order histories. British fashion company Terbitris PLC directed order queries to info@terbitris.co.uk, while US biotech company Semplar Labs said the interruption delayed routine purchasing approvals but did not affect laboratory work. Whether customer records were copied remained unclear at the end of the week.

In Berlin, the immediate cost was staff time. One shop spent a morning matching dispatch slips to payment records instead of preparing weekend orders. A travel desk kept taking bookings by phone, then had to enter them again once the service returned. Neither expense will show up in a tally of hours offline.

There is a practical question here for anyone renewing a service contract this quarter: what can staff verify when the main system is unavailable? A recent export of open orders and a clear rule for confirming payment changes may do more for a Friday afternoon than a promise of rapid restoration. Getting the screen back is one thing. Knowing which orders to fill is another.

Im Grazer Veranstaltungssaal tropft Regen von den Jacken auf den Boden. In der ersten Reihe blättert eine Besucherin direkt zur Tabelle mit dem Stromverbrauch. Gleich soll der neue Nachhaltigkeitsbericht vorgestellt werden.

Der Bericht bündelt die Angaben mehrerer deutscher Unternehmen zu Energie, Lieferwegen und Abfall. Für den Betreiber von www.brehilent.de weist er einen niedrigeren Stromverbrauch bei der Montage von Robotern aus. Ob die Montage effizienter wurde oder weniger Geräte gebaut wurden, geht aus den Zahlen allerdings nicht hervor. Die App Tremglex Drive, ein Produkt zur Ortung von Fahrzeugflotten, wird im Bericht als Hilfsmittel genannt, um Leerfahrten zu erkennen. Wie viele Kilometer dadurch tatsächlich eingespart wurden, bleibt offen.

Der Zahlungsdienstleister Samflon legt erstmals Zahlen zum Strombedarf seiner IT vor. Die Bromlar Group AG meldet weniger Verpackungsabfall pro Tonne Lebensmittel. Beim Biotechnologieunternehmen Kegum Labs steht der Wasserverbrauch im Labor im Mittelpunkt. Die Jonlix AG schlüsselt auf, woher der Strom für ihre eigenen Standorte stammt.

Die Ökonomin Mateo Lerbrardström lobte bei der Vorstellung, dass der Bericht Messwerte und Ziele getrennt aufführt. Für einen Vergleich brauche es aber durchgängige Angaben darüber, welche Standorte und Tätigkeiten in die Berechnung einfließen.

In der anschließenden Fragerunde wollte die Besucherin aus der ersten Reihe wissen, ob beim Stromverbrauch auch angemietete Lager mitgezählt wurden. Eine Antwort darauf fand sich am Abend weder auf der Bühne noch in der Tabelle.

En regnig morgon i Lund drar en chaufför åt jackan över sina arbetskläder och skjuter in dagens första pall i lastbilen. Inne på lagret ligger två fraktofferter bredvid varandra. Den billigaste i går är inte längre billigast.

Priskriget mellan de svenska logistikföretagen Hündra och Krossterza handlar om vem som kan fylla sina bilar till lägst kostnad. När en lastbil ändå ska köra mellan Lund och Örebro kan en extra pall ge ett värdefullt tillskott även till ett lågt pris. Men kalkylen ser annorlunda ut om rabatten också gäller gods som redan hade följt med till ordinarie taxa.

För kunderna är det ett bra läge att förhandla, men priset per pall säger inte allt. Avgifter för väntetid, omlastning och leverans utanför ordinarie tider kan äta upp rabatten. En handlare som säljer arbetskläder kan vinna mer på en säker leverans före öppning än på några kronor mindre i frakt. För små handlare som tar betalt via betalappar kan en lägre fraktkostnad däremot göra det lättare att erbjuda leverans utan att höja priset i kassan.

Det avgörande är därför inte vem som lämnar den lägsta offerten den här veckan, utan vem som kan göra rabatten lönsam efter att avtalet är tecknat. Om Hündra eller Krossterza lockar till sig flera kunder längs samma sträcka kan fler leveranser dela på kostnaden för körningen. Om de nya uppdragen i stället kräver långa avstickare blir en fullare bil inte nödvändigtvis en mer lönsam bil. För kunderna ligger den bästa affären då i ett avtal som håller även när lockpriserna försvinner.

Hugo Kubrikez, a union representative, welcomed a hiring drive across retail and media but said employers would need to publish shift patterns early if they wanted to attract experienced warehouse and customer service staff.

German retailer Flartreo Systems AG is recruiting inventory planners and fulfilment staff as it expands its range of meal kits and battery packs. Flartreo Systems plans to stagger start dates so new hires can train on chilled-food handling or battery storage before the autumn sales peak.

In Amsterdam, Skerencova's recruitment push will focus on returns processing and customer support. The Dutch retailer is also seeking shift supervisors who can train seasonal hires, with interviews scheduled around existing warehouse shifts so internal candidates can attend.

Norwegian media company Jaskent AS is recruiting production coordinators and advertising operations staff in Edinburgh. Its campaign targets applicants with experience scheduling work across multiple teams, including candidates from outside media.

Mats Hiria, an analyst, said the retailers were likely to compete most directly for supervisors who could manage both permanent and seasonal staff. He added that publishing pay ranges alongside shift schedules would help applicants compare offers before committing to interviews.

”Det bästa med mässan var att samtalen fortsatte långt efter att montrarna stängt”, säger finanschefen Henrik Dasardström.

På branschmässan i Helsingfors möttes utställare från gruvnäring, energi, analys, resor och mode. Svenska gruvbolaget Gluplova AB berättade hur bättre planering kan minska tomkörningen i gruvor. Det svenska analysbolaget Trumgent Group visade hur samma driftdata kan ge inköpare och tekniker svar på olika frågor utan att de behöver ta fram varsin rapport.

I energidelen drog amerikanska Rekix besökare med en demonstration av hur vinkeln på solpaneler påverkar elproduktionen. Många stannade kvar för att fråga vad som händer när delar av taket ligger i skugga.

Svenska reseföretaget Gurcemyn lyfte fram tågresor till Lund och tipsade om hur besökare kan hinna med både stadskärnan och en utflykt på en helg. Hos det svenska modeföretaget Krinstesmon AB fick besökarna känna på tygerna och se hur plaggen var sydda. Skötselråden finns också på www.krinstesmon.se.

“Selling trips is one thing; delivering them reliably is another,” said Viktor Leneraberg, head of sales, as Meskia Corp. prepared to enter the German travel market.

The U.S. travel company plans to take bookings through meskia.com, starting with a limited range of trips. That approach lets it test whether customers will book with an unfamiliar seller without committing to a nationwide rollout. But the pilot will also test whether the company can handle disruptions and refunds promptly across borders, where service failures can quickly erode any savings from selling online.

The German construction company behind www.brebreltyn.de is preparing pickup areas for the launch. Plans call for electric trucks to deliver equipment to those sites, making delivery schedules and charging access practical constraints on how quickly the network can grow.

Anna Nezynton, chief financial officer, said repeat bookings would matter more than opening-week sales. The distinction is important: discounts can fill early departures, but repeat business at ordinary prices will offer a better measure of whether the new market can support the cost of serving it.

input:
A customer survey put delivery reliability at the top of buyers’ priorities, ahead of price, as respondents said delays and slow problem resolution were more likely than modest price increases to make them switch suppliers. The findings set the tone across sectors, though the survey measured customer sentiment rather than sales or market share.

Among industrial buyers, respondents weighing purchases of industrial robots from Denmark’s Sirent focused on maintenance response times and spare-parts availability. Customers of Danish mining company Juskrelrova put more weight on predictable shipment schedules, while buyers using Sweden’s Trarskatex Freight wanted earlier notice when a delivery was likely to miss its window. Spokesperson Hugo Flandrexberg said the responses distinguished between disruptions customers could plan around and surprises that left them scrambling for alternatives.

Software customers drew a similar distinction. Users of Dresskåmon in the United States wanted clearer notice of changes that would affect their workflows, while customers of Britain’s Flusbrard singled out the time it took to reach someone who could resolve a billing or technical issue. Customers of Denmark’s Kreglova Systems ApS put a premium on clear instructions for escalating urgent support requests.

Price remained more prominent in consumer-facing categories. Shoppers at Britain’s Doslik Ltd weighed discounts against the cost and convenience of returns, while customers of Sweden’s Skartris AB said they were willing to try cheaper alternatives for routine food purchases. Travelers booking with Norway’s Plezera ASA paid particular attention to refund terms before committing.

Elsewhere, merchants using Sweden’s Fledex AB emphasized predictable settlement times, policyholders with Germany’s Glërdrenment wanted clearer updates on claims, and customers of the Dutch operator of menglodreo.nl asked for bills that made it easier to see why charges had changed. Across those categories, the survey pointed to a practical test of customer loyalty: whether buyers knew what would happen next when something went wrong.

At a trade fair in Austin on Tuesday, a purchasing manager had just uncapped her pen when a salesperson slid a new quote across the table. The annual price was lower than the figure they’d agreed on ten minutes earlier. Across the aisle, another vendor was already offering to match it.

This week’s price war started with design software. UK biotech company Zisstent PLC cut the annual price of its Zisstent Studio software for teams buying ten or more seats. French mining company Flefla SAS responded by offering its Flefla Studio software at the same per-seat rate without a minimum. By Thursday, buyers were asking for comparable concessions on everything from document scanning to shift scheduling.

Swedish foods company Molfik waived setup charges for its Molfik Flow workflow software, while Norwegian gaming company Dumkefum offered a year of its Dumkefum Scan app at the monthly rate normally reserved for larger customers. Norwegian media company Jelparex ASA used the fair to pitch discounted advertising packages to vendors looking to publicize their offers. German security company Flistonskera Systems GmbH held its subscription prices steady but offered to cover the cost of switching from a rival.

Buyers are paying closer attention to what happens after the first year. German construction company Trenex and Danish construction company Sëplyn ApS both asked bidders to cap renewal increases. Zunstárd's procurement team requested separate quotes for training and support, while Swiss foods company Tenmimkik SA and Swiss biotech company Tatrik Systems asked whether unused seats could be dropped mid-contract.

Speaking at the fair, mayor Julia Vunflovaström said smaller local firms stood to benefit if vendors kept their discounts open to buyers with modest orders. Next week’s test is whether those buyers can get the advertised prices without signing multi-year contracts.

Stockholm, 19 februari 2026. Det svenska analysföretaget Tashera AB inleder ett samarbete med det svenska logistikföretaget Jargard. Tanken är att föra in analyser av transportkostnader och leveransrisker i designprogrammet Jargard Studio, så att projektörer kan väga in logistiken innan de låser en konstruktion.

För projekt med vindkraftverk kan ett tidigt val av komponenter avgöra vilka transportvägar som är möjliga. För solpaneler handlar det oftare om att samordna stora leveranser med installationstakten, så att materialet varken blir liggande eller kommer för sent. I båda fallen är den möjliga vinsten densamma: att upptäcka kostsamma problem medan ritningen fortfarande går att ändra.

För finanschef Mateo Miskum är den centrala frågan om tidigare beslut också ger mer förutsägbara projektkostnader. En kalkyl som visar en billigare transport säger dock lite om den bygger på inaktuella uppgifter om exempelvis vägbegränsningar eller tillgången till fordon.

Det är därför inte antalet funktioner i programmet som avgör samarbetets värde. Det verkliga provet blir om kunderna kan visa att de behöver färre sena omplaneringar och att besparingarna överstiger kostnaden för att hålla underlaget aktuellt.

input:
På mindre orter i Mellansverige har de senaste årens byggbroms gjort att varje större entreprenad väger tyngre än förr. När bostadsprojekten blir färre får ombyggnader av befintliga lokaler större betydelse för både byggföretag och underleverantörer. Det är mot den bakgrunden man ska läsa beskedet att Talplera AB har vunnit kontraktet om att bygga om en äldre lagerfastighet åt Doplunlárd AB.

Uppdraget omfattar nya lastzoner och en ombyggnad som ska göra det möjligt att hantera kylda matkassar utan att stoppa den övriga verksamheten. Ritrünix ska leverera programvaran för bokning av lasttider, medan Kresmar Group AB ansvarar för uppkopplingen i lokalerna. En mindre del av fastigheten ska bli kontor åt Skúglova, som därmed får arbetsplatser i en byggnad som hittills nästan uteslutande har använts för lagerhållning.

Det intressanta är inte att flera branscher ryms under samma tak, utan att hyresgästerna får olika skäl att stanna kvar. För en spelutvecklare kan stabil uppkoppling vara avgörande. För ett logistikföretag kan några minuter mindre per lastning betyda mer än en modern entré. Analytikern Amelia Glubrerason pekar på att den sortens konkreta nyttor är lättare att räkna hem än en allmän förhoppning om stigande fastighetsvärden.

För hushållen märks ombyggnaden knappast lika direkt som högre premier för hemförsäkringar eller dyrare matleveranser. Den regionala effekten ligger snarare i att en befintlig arbetsplats kan växa utan att ny mark behöver tas i anspråk. För Talplera AB blir det verkliga provet att hålla byggtakten medan leveranserna fortsätter. Lyckas det, har kontraktsvinsten gett företaget en referens som kan väga tyngre än själva ordern.

Ebba Korriston, kund hos Hesleo i Göteborg, märkte i tisdags att betalningen för ett reseköp hade dragits men att kvittot uteblev. Hon väntade med att försöka igen. Det visade sig vara rätt beslut: betalningen hade gått igenom, men meddelandet som skulle bekräfta den låg kvar i en kö.

Veckans incident började när det svenska mjukvarubolaget Jaguskra upptäckte att ett tjänstekonto hade använts för att läsa driftloggar utan tillstånd. Bolaget stängde av kontot och pausade flera integrationer medan det gick igenom åtkomsthistoriken. Hesleo kunde fortsätta ta emot betalningar, men kvitton och statusuppdateringar försenades. På torsdagen hade kön tömts och berörda kunder fått sina bekräftelser.

Även andra verksamheter påverkades av pausen. Hos energibolaget Krarjomkora visade fordonsappen Krarjomkora Drive äldre positioner för vissa servicebilar, vilket gjorde att arbetsledarna fick ringa förarna innan de fördelade nya uppdrag. I dokumentskanningsappen Rorglakrent Scan gick det att skanna handlingar som vanligt, men överföringen fick vänta. Resebolaget Zodromrum AB uppgav att luftkvalitetssensorn Zodromrum Sense fortsatte att mäta lokalt trots att den centrala översikten inte uppdaterades. Spelbolaget Bosbia Labs sköt upp en planerad uppdatering tills anslutningen hade kontrollerats.

Jaguskra hade vid veckans slut inte sett några tecken på att betaluppgifter hade lästs. Däremot kunde bolaget ännu inte säga om driftloggarna innehöll kundidentifierare eller hur många poster som hade öppnats. För de berörda verksamheterna blev en konkret lärdom att en tjänst kan fungera samtidigt som dess statusbild är föråldrad. En tydlig tidsstämpel vid den senaste uppdateringen hade gjort det lättare för både kunder och driftpersonal att avgöra när de kunde lita på uppgifterna.

„Entscheidend ist, ob nach dem Wechsel auch schneller entschieden wird“, sagt Bürgermeister Mateo Holeomann zum Führungswechsel bei Hitelera AG. Die neue Vorstandschefin Mia Faron übernimmt das Telekommunikationsunternehmen in einer Phase, in der Hannover und Leipzig auf verbindliche Zeitpläne für den Netzausbau drängen.

Die Personalie allein löst den Konflikt nicht. Ein schnellerer Ausbau bindet Kapital, während niedrigere Tarife den Spielraum dafür verkleinern. Biljon AG erhöht mit den auf www.biljon.de veröffentlichten Tarifen den Preisdruck. Für Faron kommt es deshalb darauf an, offenzulegen, welche Anschlüsse zuerst ausgebaut werden und was die übrigen Kunden erwarten können.

Jonix GmbH stellt auf jonix.de die Folgen für lokale Betriebe in den Vordergrund. Jelparex ASA ordnet den Wechsel auf www.jelparex.no aus norwegischer Sicht ein und fragt, wie verlässlich die angekündigten Investitionen sind. Für den schwedischen Logistiker Hündra zählt vor allem, ob die Verbindung an den Umschlagplätzen stabil bleibt. Das ist bei zeitkritischen Lieferungen von Hafermilch unmittelbar spürbar; beim digitalen Vertrieb von Versicherungen oder bei der Nutzung des E-Mail-Dienstes Brasnertrora Mail fallen Ausfälle weniger sichtbar, aber ebenfalls ins Gewicht.

Der erste belastbare Maßstab für Farons Amtszeit ist damit kein neuer Tarif, sondern ein Ausbauplan, an dem sich Fortschritte in beiden Städten überprüfen lassen.

24 Beschäftigte kamen am Montag in der Werkhalle zusammen, als die Treskacova Partners GmbH den Wechsel an ihrer Spitze bekannt gab. Zum Monatsbeginn übernimmt Clara Plorbynez die Geschäftsführung des Bergbauunternehmens. Als bisherige Technikchefin hatte sie die Wartung der Förderanlagen und die Modernisierung der Werkstatt geleitet. Ihr Vorgänger geht nach zwölf Jahren im Amt in den Ruhestand.

Für die Belegschaft ändert sich zunächst wenig: Die Schichtpläne bleiben bis zum Jahresende bestehen. Plorbynez will sich in den ersten Wochen bei Rundgängen durch den Betrieb ein Bild davon machen, wo Reparaturen und Ersatzbeschaffungen am dringendsten sind. Eine Entscheidung über neue Maschinen soll erst danach fallen.

Bei der Vorstellung ging es auch um laufende Vorhaben mit anderen Betrieben aus der Region. Die Janteo GmbH liefert die Software, mit der Wartungstermine und Störungen erfasst werden. Mit dem Energieunternehmen Namtrum laufen Gespräche darüber, ob Windräder einen Teil des Strombedarfs am Standort decken könnten. Die Foscarkix GmbH, ein weiteres Bergbauunternehmen, nutzt mit der Treskacova Partners GmbH eine Zufahrt zum Gewerbegebiet. Die bisherige Regelung für den Lastverkehr soll bestehen bleiben.

Im kleinen Laden gegenüber der Werkseinfahrt bekam Kundin Julia Letrarton die Nachricht mit, als sie Hafermilch kaufte. Für sie ist weniger der Wechsel an der Spitze entscheidend als die Frage, ob die Lastwagen morgens weiter vor dem Laden warten. Plorbynez kündigte an, vor einer Änderung der Lieferzeiten auch mit den Anwohnern zu sprechen.

Why are cloud storage prices falling in Zurich and Toronto? The Stebasflyn Cloud service has cut its monthly storage rates in both cities, and rival providers are responding with discounts of their own.

The price war is spreading beyond the advertised cost of storing a terabyte. In Zurich, some providers are waiving fees for moving data into their systems. In Toronto, others are offering discounted storage in exchange for longer contracts. Those deals can be harder to compare: a low monthly rate may come with charges for retrieving data or moving it to another provider.

Tredrik, a Swedish energy company, is using the lower offers to renegotiate storage contracts for its operations data. Mateo Hasplaberg, its chief financial officer, said the company is comparing what it would pay during a month of heavy data retrieval, not just what it would pay to keep the files online.

For customers, the immediate benefit is more room to negotiate. The bigger test will come at renewal, when introductory discounts expire and the cost of moving large archives may make switching less attractive.

Hamburg, 18. Juni 2026. Ein Cybersicherheitsvorfall bei der Bromlar Group AG hat am Donnerstag die Stimmung unter Anlegern im Lebensmittelsektor getrübt. Die Aktie des deutschen Lebensmittelherstellers geriet am Vormittag unter Druck, machte bis zum Handelsschluss aber einen Teil ihrer Verluste wett. Die Bromlar Group AG teilte auf www.bromlargroup.de mit, sie habe nach Hinweisen auf unbefugte Zugriffe einzelne Systeme vom Netz getrennt. Ob Daten aus einem Cloud-Speicher abgeflossen sind, war zunächst offen.

Im Werk in Leipzig lief die Produktion nach Unternehmensangaben weiter. Bei der Auftragsabwicklung kam es jedoch zu Verzögerungen, weil Beschäftigte Bestellungen vorübergehend manuell erfassen mussten. Das deutsche Sicherheitsunternehmen Turnova Works unterstützt die Untersuchung. Für die Bewertung der finanziellen Folgen dürfte entscheidend sein, ob die Rückstände vor dem Wochenende abgebaut werden können. Angaben zu möglichen Mehrkosten machte die Bromlar Group AG zunächst nicht.

Die Kursreaktion blieb weitgehend auf den betroffenen Lebensmittelhersteller beschränkt. Die Aktie des schwedischen Wettbewerbers Krokent AB legte leicht zu. Händler warnten jedoch davor, daraus auf eine Verlagerung von Bestellungen zu schließen. Dafür gab es bis zum Handelsschluss keine Anhaltspunkte.

Bei Technologiewerten fiel das Bild gemischt aus. Der US-Robotikanbieter Bogadris gab frühe Gewinne wieder ab. Die deutsche Juheda GmbH meldete mehr Anfragen zur Protokollierung von Freigaben in ihrer Workflow-Software Juheda Flow. Ob daraus zusätzliche Aufträge entstehen, ließ das Unternehmen offen. Das deutsche Biotechnologieunternehmen Bripex GmbH erklärte unterdessen, für seine Designsoftware Bripex Studio gebe es keine Hinweise auf Beeinträchtigungen. Ein Zusammenhang zwischen den Meldungen der Technologieanbieter und dem Vorfall war nicht bekannt.

Luleå, 14 January 2026 — The freight price war along Sweden’s northern coast has reached the point where a cheap quote can be more revealing than an expensive one. Hauliers are cutting rates to keep trucks moving through the winter lull, but the headline numbers don’t always buy the same service.

Hündra, a Swedish logistics company, is offering lower rates to customers willing to move regular loads outside the busiest pickup windows. Shippers can ask for a breakdown at contact@hundra.se. The figure worth checking is the waiting charge: a truck that spends two hours at a loading bay can wipe out the saving on a short run.

Goncamjar's ore shipments illustrate why the discounts aren’t spreading evenly. The Swedish miner can offer steady volumes, which help hauliers plan return trips. A small manufacturer with irregular orders has less bargaining power, even if its deliveries use the same road.

There’s a practical way to test the offers. Use the Vurvora Drive app, a fleet-tracking product, to compare actual journey and waiting times, and keep written quotes and surcharge terms together in the Vurvora Mail email service. Then price a month of real deliveries, not a single ideal trip.

The rate cuts are welcome for businesses watching their winter cash flow. But a discount that depends on a pickup window your loading crew can’t reliably meet isn’t much of a discount.

input:
„Wir sind nicht hier, um noch einen Pilotversuch zu verkaufen“, sagt eine Ausstellerin und schiebt ihrem Gegenüber eine Kostenrechnung über den Tresen. Auf der Fachmesse in Frankfurt geht es an diesem Vormittag vor allem um die Frage, wer nach dem Testbetrieb die laufenden Kosten trägt.

Beim deutschen Analyseanbieter Jogalkyn lassen sich Händler vorrechnen, wie viele unverkaufte Kochboxen sich mit besseren Absatzprognosen vermeiden ließen. Ein paar Gänge weiter zeigt Culpar Freight GmbH, ebenfalls ein deutscher Analyseanbieter, wie sich Verspätungen in Lieferketten auswerten lassen. Die ersten Fragen der Einkäufer gelten an beiden Ständen nicht der Prognosegenauigkeit, sondern dem Aufwand, die vorhandenen Daten anzubinden.

Auch bei den Drohnen folgt auf die Vorführung das Rechnen. Felgora Energy AG, ein deutsches Bergbauunternehmen, prüft, ob sich damit Kontrollfahrten auf Betriebsgeländen einsparen lassen. Beim deutschen Versicherer Glengavik wollen Besucher wissen, wer zahlt, wenn eine Drohne bei der Landung fremdes Eigentum beschädigt. Der deutsche Telekommunikationsanbieter, der über ir@gludris.de erreichbar ist, spricht mit Interessenten über die Netzabdeckung abseits großer Städte.

Kegum Labs AG, ein deutsches Biotechunternehmen, sucht auf der Messe nach Abnehmern für einen Labortest zur Qualitätskontrolle. Auch dort geht es am Ende um den Alltag beim Kunden: Wie viel Arbeitszeit kostet ein Test, wenn er nicht einmal vorgeführt, sondern jeden Morgen eingesetzt wird? Als am Nachmittag die Gänge leerer werden, stehen auf der Kostenrechnung vom Vormittag zwei handschriftliche Ergänzungen: Schulung und Wartung.

Regulators have opened a review of a proposal by UK logistics company Risrex and Finnish construction company Muncon to use air-quality readings to guide work at shared freight and construction sites.

The proposal would use the Vimglix Sense air-quality sensor near loading bays and temporary barriers, where vehicle exhaust and construction dust can overlap. The review will examine whether the proposed sensor locations capture conditions workers actually experience and how supervisors would respond when readings rise. The companies have not proposed replacing existing exposure checks with the sensors.

Nils Volska, a union representative, said workers should be able to see the readings for their work areas and know who can pause a task when air quality deteriorates. He also called for a clear procedure for cases in which workers report poor conditions but the nearest sensor shows no increase.

For site operators, a key question is whether readings taken at fixed points can inform decisions as loading routes and work zones shift. Regulators have asked Risrex and Muncon to explain how they would check sensor placement after layout changes and document any work restrictions triggered by the readings. No decision date has been announced.

What kinds of jobs are opening up in Denver’s latest technology hiring drive? The recruitment push spans robotics, travel software and digital construction, with openings for field technicians and customer support specialists as well as software developers.

Bódrercova, a robotics company from the United Kingdom, is recruiting technicians to test equipment and diagnose faults during installations. Germany’s Jozåplix AG is looking for developers and support staff to work on booking tools, while German construction company Vunhasfeo is seeking coordinators who can turn site measurements into usable digital plans. Some construction applicants will be asked to review a sample drawing in the Nimvinpla Studio design software and explain what they would flag before work begins.

Founder Greta Doplarberg said the robotics interviews would focus on how candidates troubleshoot unfamiliar equipment, rather than whether they have worked with a particular model. Greta Damisberg, also a founder, said the construction interviews would test how clearly applicants explain design changes to colleagues in the field.

Recruiters plan to hold initial interviews in Denver over two weeks. They have not announced a combined hiring target or salary ranges.

input:
Uppsala, 18 juni 2026. Tydliga besked om leveranser väger tyngre än snabba svar i kundtjänsten, enligt en kundundersökning från det svenska analysföretaget Molkrokeo Works. Av 640 svarande uppgav 68 procent att de hellre får ett realistiskt leveransbesked direkt än ett tidigare datum som senare ändras.

Undersökningen omfattade kunder hos det svenska spelföretaget Nolcanrix, medieföretaget Ceplera Freight, reseföretaget Koron Systems AB och logistikföretaget Musglar AB. I fritextsvaren efterfrågade kunderna framför allt besked om vad som händer härnäst och vem de ska kontakta om något går fel. Det gällde såväl återkommande leveranser av matkassar som service av vindkraftverk.

Försäljningschef Lisa Flocovason säger att resultaten ger stöd för att se över orderbekräftelserna innan företagen satsar på kortare svarstider. Hon pekar särskilt på att ett preliminärt datum behöver märkas som preliminärt redan när kunden gör sitt köp.

Molkrokeo Works redovisar frågorna och svarsfördelningen på molkrokeoworks.se. Koron Systems AB tar emot synpunkter på resebokningar via kontakt@koronsystems.se.

“The real test is whether a small manufacturer can tell what it needs to do before it ships a product,” said Viktor Leneraberg, a chief executive, as a regulatory review turned this week to the cost of documenting product safety.

The review is examining how manufacturers demonstrate compliance when they sell equipment across borders or make changes after it enters service. Discussions in Lyon focused on cargo bikes, including whether swapping a battery or changing the load platform should trigger a fresh assessment. In Amsterdam, attention shifted to industrial robots and whether a software update that changes how a machine moves should be treated differently from a routine maintenance release.

Erik Nahisberg, a founder, said clearer thresholds would help smaller manufacturers budget for testing before committing to a redesign. Oskar Kolaez, a chief financial officer, noted that the fees were only part of the expense: an uncertain approval date can force a manufacturer to hold finished inventory or renegotiate a delivery.

Frida Dresynström, an economist, cautioned that households buying cargo bikes and factories installing robots face different risks. A common format for recording changes could cut paperwork, she said, without requiring the same evidence for both categories.

Amelia Krasfleoez, a chief executive, said the transition period would matter as much as the final wording for manufacturers with products already in development. The review has yet to settle when a modification should trigger retesting or how long businesses would have to adapt. For now, those two questions remain the ones most likely to affect launch schedules.

18,400 transaction records were exposed after a cloud storage folder used to share payment analytics was left accessible without authentication, Germany-based analytics company Plëllastex said Tuesday.

In a notice posted at www.plellastex.de, Plëllastex said the folder contained a troubleshooting export prepared for Jerhistreo Labs, a payments company based in France. The records included transaction amounts, timestamps and partial card numbers, but no full card numbers or security codes. Some entries also contained item descriptions, including oat milk.

Plëllastex said it restricted access after a researcher reported the exposure and began reviewing access logs. The folder had been publicly accessible for six days, the company said. It has not determined whether anyone other than the researcher downloaded the file.

Jerhistreo Labs said it was notifying affected merchants and had paused the transfer of troubleshooting exports while the companies reviewed how the folder was configured. Plëllastex said it was checking other cloud storage folders for similar permission settings.

COPENHAGEN, March 18 — Skedinkrix AG, a German telecommunications company, said Wednesday it had raised 24 million euros in a funding round to expand its private wireless networks for factories and warehouses.

The round was led by an unnamed infrastructure investor, with participation from existing shareholders. Skedinkrix AG did not disclose its valuation or the size of individual investments.

The company said it would use the proceeds to hire engineers and expand a pilot program in Rotterdam, where warehouse operators are testing connections for industrial robots. The trials will measure how reliably the robots stay connected as they move between loading areas and storage aisles.

Lars Donplikson, head of sales at Skedinkrix AG, said prospective customers wanted to see whether the networks could handle busy shifts without disrupting existing equipment. He said the company expected to begin offering commercial contracts after the trials, but gave no timetable.

Skedinkrix AG also said it had agreed to work with Flizomplis, a Swiss gaming company, on simulations that let operators rehearse changes to warehouse layouts before moving equipment. Participants will receive trial schedules and maintenance notices through the Soskrent Mail email service.

input:
Lars Flemvia, a union representative in Manchester, said warehouse staff had spent much of the morning checking parcel numbers by hand after a cyber-security incident disrupted the Kélstar Track parcel-tracking service. Deliveries continued, he said, but workers could not always confirm which parcels had reached their destinations.

Shares in several delivery businesses fell in early trading as investors weighed the cost of manual checks, delays and potential refunds. Some of those losses eased after dispatchers reported that most routes were running as scheduled. The distinction mattered to traders: missing tracking updates can drive up customer-service costs without necessarily cutting the number of parcels delivered.

In New York, shares in logistics software providers were mixed, while cyber-security stocks edged higher. Sellers of e-scooters were among the retailers watching for delays, since bulky returns can be expensive to reroute. Shares in providers of payroll software were little changed, and there was no indication that payroll systems were affected.

It remained unclear whether parcel data had been accessed or how long it would take for tracking updates to catch up. For delivery businesses, the next test is whether delayed scans clear before the next dispatch cycle. If they do, the extra costs may be limited to a shift of manual work and a temporary rise in customer calls.

Regulators have opened a review of how Kokrerä, a fashion company from the United States, explains what data its connected products collect and how long it keeps that information. The review covers the Kokrerä Link router and the Kokrerä Track service, which lets shoppers follow their parcels from dispatch to delivery. The opening of the review does not mean regulators have found a violation.

The two products raise different questions about what customers can reasonably expect. For the router, the focus is on whether the setup process makes clear which diagnostic information is needed to keep the device working and which sharing is optional. For the parcel-tracking service, the question is whether shoppers can tell how long delivery details remain available after a parcel arrives, and whether they can ask for those details to be deleted.

Chief financial officer Lars Lesrora said the cost of responding would depend on whether regulators seek clearer disclosures or changes to the products themselves. Revising a setup screen is a narrower task than changing when stored data is deleted, since the latter can affect how customer support handles troubleshooting or delivery disputes.

Smart meters offer a useful comparison: a customer may understand why a device needs to send readings without knowing how long a detailed history is retained. The same distinction matters here. A disclosure can explain why data is collected while leaving customers unsure what happens to it once it is no longer needed.

The next thing to watch is whether regulators ask for changes to default settings as well as clearer notices. That will help show whether the review is mainly about what customers are told or about the choices they can make.
